title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA and Acute Myocarditis: A Comparative Multiparametric Evaluation.
abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and acute myocarditis (AM) often present with overlapping clinical features and biomarker profiles, making early differential diagnosis challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference modality for etiological assessment through functional evaluation and multiparametric tissue characterization. The aim of this study was to compare clinical and CMR characteristics of patients with MINOCA and suspected AM, and to identify imaging features enabling accurate differentiation. We retrospectively analyzed 127 consecutive patients undergoing CMR (February 2021-October 2024): 62 with suspected MINOCA and 65 with suspected AM. Clinical data, laboratory findings, ECG, and CMR parameters (cine imaging, T1/T2 mapping, extracellular volume [ECV], and late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) were assessed. MINOCA patients were older (median 59 years) and predominantly female (64.5%), whereas AM patients were younger (median 29 years) and mainly male (81.5%). AM was associated with higher troponin and inflammatory markers. Among patients initially referred with suspected MINOCA, LGE was present in 50.0%, compared with 93.8% of those referred with suspected acute myocarditis (p < 0.001). MINOCA showed predominantly ischemic LGE patterns, while AM exhibited non-ischemic subepicardial or mid-wall LGE with myocardial edema. CMR confirmed myocardial infarction in 48.4% of patients and identified alternative diagnoses in 41.9%, while 9.7% had normal CMR findings. Multiparametric CMR reliably distinguishes ischemic from inflammatory myocardial injury in patients with chest pain, elevated troponin, and non-obstructive coronaries. Early CMR integration improves diagnostic accuracy and supports tailored management.

title: The predictive value of 99m Tc-MIBI SPECT/ 18 F-FDG PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging in patients with unrevascularized coronary chronic total occlusion and left ventricular dysfunction.
abstract: To explore the predictive value of hibernating myocardium detected by single photon emission computed tomography (SEPCT)/positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging for the adverse cardiovascular events in unrevascularized chronic coronary total occlusion (CTO) patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Additionally, we explore whether hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory can independently predictive outcomes. Patients with at least one unrevascularized CTO on coronary angiography and LV dysfunction and who underwent rest 99mTc-MIBI SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging as well as 18F-FDG PET myocardial metabolic imaging were enrolled. All patients were followed up through telephone interviews and review of medical records. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, the extents of hibernating myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories, the extent of total scarred myocardium, and the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were calculated according to the segmental perfusion/metabolism score and the segmental assignment of coronary dominance and the results of coronary angiography. The Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between the extent of hibernating or scarred myocardium and adverse cardiovascular events. Seventy eight patients were included in the final analysis. The median follow-up duration was 70.2 (27.7, 80.3) months. The extent of total hibernating myocardium and the extent of hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory were both independent predictors for cardiac death [hazards ratio (HR) = 1.289, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.083-1.533, P = 0.004; HR = 1.262, 95% CI 1.022-1.557, P = 0.030] and the composite endpoint events (HR = 1.190, 95% CI 1.032-1.372, P = 0.016; HR = 1.273, 95% CI 1.025-1.581, P = 0.029). The extent of hibernating myocardium in the non-CTO territory, the extent of total scarred myocardium, the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were all not associated with the outcome. 99mTc-MIBI /18F-FDG SPECT/PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging has an important predictive value for prognosis in unrevascularized CTO patients with LV dysfunction. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, especially hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory, was an independent predictor for adverse cardiovascular events.

title: Amyloid-targeted PET after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy for cardiac amyloidosis: a systematic review.
abstract: To assess myocardial positron emission tomography (PET) positivity after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy, while distinguishing test discordance from independently confirmed cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through 5 August 2026, with targeted source assessment through 2 October 2026. Negative and low-grade imaging denoted Perugini grades 0 and 1, respectively; study-defined negative results were described separately. Eligibility required linked PET and bone-scan results with an extractable denominator. Acquisition modality, PET thresholds and cardiac reference standards were examined. A restricted synthesis required documented tomographic acquisition; a broader three-report synthesis was exploratory. Nine reports provided extractable paired results. In the hereditary transthyretin subgroup examined with carbon-11 Pittsburgh compound B, 20/23 participants were PET-positive after excluding one acquired, domino-transplant case. The exploratory pooled proportion was 87.0% (95% profile-likelihood confidence interval, 68.5-97.8%). Restriction to clearly documented cohort-wide tomography retained only two reports, precluding the planned pooled analysis. Uptake definitions and cardiac verification differed substantially. General diagnostic studies without complete bone-grade denominators, including REVEAL, were excluded from the eligible synthesis and retained as context. PET positivity is common in selected hereditary transthyretin cohorts with negative or low-grade bone scans, but does not establish cardiac amyloidosis or earlier diagnosis. Conditional diagnostic accuracy remains unresolved. Prospective paired studies require tomographic localization, tracer-specific thresholds and independent cardiac verification.

title: Early selective deep capillary plexus impairment at diagnosis in children with type 1 diabetes: an OCT angiography study.
abstract: Retinal microvascular dysfunction may precede clinically visible diabetic retinopathy in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), but whether it is detectable at diagnosis remains unclear. To evaluate retinal microvascular alterations at T1DM diagnosis using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and assess associations between deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density and metabolic severity. This cross-sectional study included 50 children with newly diagnosed T1DM (100 eyes) and 50 age- and sex-matched controls (100 eyes). OCTA was performed using 6×6-mm macular and 4.5×4.5-mm optic disc scans. Vessel density (VD) was assessed in the superficial capillary plexus (SCP), DCP, and radial peripapillary capillary network. Foveal avascular zone metrics and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness were also analyzed. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for inter-eye correlation. Subgroup analyses were performed by HbA1c level and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) severity. SCP VD did not differ significantly between groups. DCP VD was lower in T1DM eyes in the whole image (53.1±3.0% vs 54.6±2.8%, p=0.006), parafoveal region (54.0±3.1% vs 55.8±2.9%, p=0.002), and perifoveal region (53.4±3.0% vs 54.7±2.8%, p=0.02). Peripapillary VD and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness were similar. Higher HbA1c was independently associated with lower DCP VD, which also declined with increasing DKA severity. DCP impairment is detectable at T1DM diagnosis before clinically visible diabetic retinopathy. OCTA may provide a sensitive, noninvasive biomarker of early retinal microvascular involvement in pediatric T1DM.

title: Unusual metastatic recurrence of pulmonary adenocarcinoma with a focal neuroendocrine component presenting with bilateral renal metastases and an accompanying pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion: a case report.
abstract: A 72-year-old woman with a history of resected lung adenocarcinoma presented with a pancreatic mass and multiple bilateral renal masses. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition of the pancreatic lesion showed neuroendocrine morphology, synaptophysin positivity, focal chromogranin A positivity, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 2%, leading to an initial diagnosis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grade 1. Renal biopsy also demonstrated neuroendocrine differentiation with a Ki-67 labeling index of 17%. However, the pancreatic lesion was hypovascular and poorly defined, and the multifocal bilateral renal involvement was atypical for a low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. Re-evaluation of the resected lung specimen revealed a focal neuroendocrine component showing large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma-like features, although the strict diagnostic criteria for such a diagnosis were not fully met. Genomic analysis identified a KRAS G12V mutation shared by the renal and lung tumors, supporting the interpretation that the renal lesions represented metastatic recurrence of the previously resected lung tumor. Direct molecular confirmation was unavailable for the pancreatic lesion because of insufficient residual endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition material; therefore, its origin remained diagnostically uncertain. Nevertheless, based on the overall clinicopathological context, the pancreatic lesion was interpreted as an accompanying neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion most consistent with metastatic recurrence. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical history, imaging features, disease distribution, archival pathology, and molecular findings when evaluating neuroendocrine tumor-like lesions in patients with a prior malignancy.

title: Delayed diagnosis of MEN1 after kidney transplantation: unrecognized pre-transplant features and implications for clinical practice.
abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), characterized by multiglandular endocrine tumors such as hyperparathyroidism (HPT), is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations of the MEN1 gene. In patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), abnormalities in calcium-phosphate metabolism may obscure this diagnosis, making the recognition of MEN1 challenging. A 68-year-old man with end-stage renal disease underwent an ABO-compatible living-donor kidney transplantation (KT); however, persistent hypercalcemia prompted further evaluation, which revealed recurrent HPT with bilateral parathyroid enlargement. Pre-transplant imaging revealed an adrenal adenoma and a pancreatic tail lesion. Subsequent pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of MEN1. A retrospective review of the patient's medical history revealed several pre-transplant findings suggestive of MEN1 that had not been recognized. This case highlights that MEN1 may remain unrecognized in KT candidates owing to the occurrence of metabolic abnormalities also associated with CKD. The early recognition of MEN1 in KT candidates with recurrent or multiglandular hyperparathyroidism may improve pre-transplant risk assessment and enable appropriate long-term oncological surveillance.

title: Divergent Trends in Relapse Activity and Relapse-Independent Progression Over Two Decades in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) management has increasingly favored earlier high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy (DMT). We examined diagnosis-era changes in relapse activity and disability accrual alongside evolving DMT use. We retrospectively analyzed two Italian cohorts of adults with MS onset in 2001-2024 across four diagnosis eras. Annualized relapse rate (ARR) was modeled by Poisson regression; confirmed disability accrual (CDA), relapse-associated worsening (RAW), and progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) by Andersen-Gill Cox models. CDA was classified as RAW when relapse onset occurred from 90 days before through 30 days after the event, otherwise as PIRA. Treatment was time-varying: untreated, low-/moderate-efficacy therapy (LET/MET), or high-efficacy therapy (HET). Inverse probability-weighted models included residual adjustment. Sensitivity analyses examined a strict common 2-year horizon, MRI restriction/adjustment, relapsing-onset MS, first-event analyses, 90-day DMT lag, early-HET exclusion, pre-treatment versus never-treated person-time, visit frequency, and center stratification. Among 1096 patients (228, 214, 292, and 362 across eras 1-4), first-line HET use reached 45.9% in era 4. Each later diagnosis year was associated with lower ARR (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99; p < 0.001), with steeper calendar-time declines during LET/MET and HET than untreated person-time (joint interaction p < 0.001). Later diagnosis year was also associated with lower RAW (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.97; p < 0.001) and modestly lower CDA over full follow-up (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00; p = 0.026), although CDA attenuated in weighted and common-horizon analyses. PIRA was not associated with diagnosis year (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.99-1.04; p = 0.262). Lower ARR and RAW persisted across sensitivities, whereas the strict 2-year analysis suggested higher early PIRA in more recent eras. Later diagnosis-era cohorts had lower relapse activity and relapse-associated disability accrual, whereas overall disability accrual was less consistent and PIRA did not decline. Improvements in relapse-related disease activity were not accompanied by a comparable reduction in relapse-independent disability accrual.

title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
abstract: Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation. The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. title: An investigation of dental anomalies in individuals with amelogenesis imperfecta.
abstract: To explore the presence of dental anomalies in children with amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) and to describe their distribution across different AI genetic variants. This cross-sectional study undertook secondary analysis of data from a primary study of children with AI below 18 years of age. After training and calibration, participants' panoramic radiographs and clinical photographs were assessed for the presence of six dental anomalies (pre-eruptive crown resorption, eruption abnormalities, pulp calcifications, taurodontism, gingival enlargement and anterior open bite). The enamel phenotype was assessed. Dental age was estimated using the Demirjian method and compared with chronological age. The genetic diagnosis, where available, was mapped to the identified dental anomalies. Thirty participants were assessed (16 male, 14 female). Twenty-one (70.0%) had hypomineralised enamel and 9 (30.0%) had hypoplastic enamel. Twenty-two (73.3%) had at least one dental anomaly in addition to the enamel phenotype. One participant was excluded from dental age analysis. Sixteen participants (55.2%) had advanced dental age, 12 (41.4%) had delayed dental age, one had matching ages (3.4%). Twenty-six participants (89.7%) had a dental age within 18 months of their chronological age. Thirteen individuals had known molecular causes for their AI, including FAM83H, LAMB3, ENAM, COL17A1, AMBN, MMP20 and SP6. Amongst these individuals, a range of the dental anomalies considered were observed. Several dental anomalies were found to occur alongside AI. Dental age did not appear to vary substantially from chronological age. Dental anomalies should be considered as part of comprehensive clinical and radiographic assessment for those with AI.

title: Performance of AI-based models in prenatal detection of trisomy 21 via ultrasonography: a systematic review.
abstract: To systematically evaluate the performance, strengths, and limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) models for trisomy 21 classification and risk prediction, and for enabling ultrasound tasks, using fetal ultrasound. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception through October 2026, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. Original, peer-reviewed studies that developed or validated AI models for trisomy 21 classification or risk prediction, or for enabling ultrasound tasks (nuchal translucency and facial marker measurement, segmentation, and plane recognition), using human fetal ultrasound images or ultrasound-derived measurements and reporting quantitative performance metrics were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias with PROBAST (prediction-model studies) and QUADAS-2 (enabling-task studies), resolving disagreements by consensus. Studies were categorized by primary task and synthesized narratively, without meta-analysis. Nineteen studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included: eight image-based classifiers, seven marker-based risk models, and four enabling-task studies. Image-based classifiers reported accuracies of 84-98.3% and AUCs of 0.95-0.985. Marker-based models reported AUCs of 0.84-0.983; detection rates of 90-100% at false-positive rates of about 3.6-3.9% came from one research group, whereas the largest cohort reported a sensitivity of 84% at a false-positive rate of 2.28%. Enabling-task studies were evaluated with task-specific metrics and were not compared with classification performance. Ten of fifteen prediction-model studies were at high risk of bias, mainly in the analysis domain; seven reported only image counts, and leakage between training and test data was likely in six. Most studies were retrospective with limited external validation. Reported performance of AI models for trisomy 21 is high but comes mostly from retrospective, internally validated studies, and benefits for screening performance, invasive testing, or operator dependence have not been demonstrated. No study compared AI with cell-free DNA screening, so the role of these tools within current screening pathways remains undefined. Prospective, multicenter validation with karyotype-confirmed outcomes and standardized reporting is needed before clinical integration can be supported.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

title: SSH1 knockdown increases autophagosome formation through ATG9A recruitment and promotes tau protein degradation.
abstract: Pathological accumulation of MAPT/tau protein is a defining feature of Alzheimer disease (AD) and related tauopathies, highlighting the need to identify druggable regulators of MAPT/tau clearance. Using Drosophila behavioral assays focused on cytoskeletal remodeling pathways dysregulated in AD, we identified genes whose genetic modulation mitigates MAPT/tau-induced behavioral deficits. These modifiers were validated by histopathology and mechanistically examined in human tauopathy cell models to determine their impact on autophagy-dependent MAPT/tau degradation. Autophagic flux, ATG9A trafficking, and autophagosome biogenesis were further analyzed. Across models, reduction of the phosphatase SSH1 consistently lowered steady-state MAPT/tau levels by enhancing autophagic flux through a mechanism distinct from its canonical regulation of CFL1. Mechanistically, SSH1 functions as a negative regulator of early autophagosome formation: SSH1 depletion promotes ATG9A mobilization to the endoplasmic reticulum-phagophore assembly site (ER-PAS), thereby accelerating autophagic vesicle biogenesis. Importantly, the MAPT/tau-lowering effect of Dmssh attenuation was abolished in flies haploinsufficient for DmAtg9, demonstrating that SSH1-mediated MAPT/tau clearance requires ATG9 function. Consistent with a direct regulatory interaction, in vitro phosphatase assays revealed that recombinant SSH1 decreases ATG9A phosphorylation in the presence of actin, identifying an SSH1-ATG9A regulatory axis controlling autophagosome initiation. These findings position SSH1 as a nodal inhibitor of autophagy initiation whose inhibition enhances MAPT/tau proteolysis. Notably, SSH1 haploinsufficiency also reduces SNCA/α-synuclein accumulation in vivo, indicating broader relevance to neurodegenerative proteopathies. By integrating in vivo functional screening with mechanistic studies in human cells, this work identifies SSH1 as a druggable phosphatase that constrains autophagy at the level of ATG9A-dependent vesicle formation.

title: DPSeg: Differentiated Perception Medical Image Segmentation via Context-Aware Compensation and Stratified Uncertainty Attention.
abstract: In medical image segmentation, accurate recognition of regions hindered by blurry boundaries, low contrast, and complex backgrounds is crucial. These issues lead to significant differences in segmentation difficulty within a single image. However, existing methods typically adopt a uniform modeling strategy across the entire feature map, overlooking the mismatch between segmentation difficulty and attention intensity. Consequently, they fail to adequately focus on key regions, diluting the representations of challenging regions. To address these challenges, we propose DPSeg, a differentiated perception medical image segmentation framework via context-aware compensation and stratified uncertainty attention. Specifically, DPSeg comprises three key components. The Context-Aware Compensation (CAC) module refines encoder features by integrating key region-aware prompts and contextual information, compensating for encoding-induced distortions and enabling differentiated perception, thereby providing higher-quality representations for decoding. Additionally, the Stratified Uncertainty Transformer (SUTrans) module explicitly modulates the attention intensity of different regions based on their segmentation uncertainty, thereby possessing differentiated perception ability while effectively suppressing redundant feature interactions. Moreover, we propose a Foreground-Uncertainty Adaptive Weighted Loss (FUAWL) to enable differentiated supervision across decoding stages, applying stronger guidance to uncertain regions in shallow decoding and emphasizing foreground regions in deep decoding to improve boundary delineation and mitigate foreground-background imbalance. Extensive experiments on four challenging datasets demonstrate that DPSeg achieves competitive segmentation performance.

title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI.
abstract: Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient-related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient-related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_Kapp achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_Kapp and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_Kapp, and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_Kapp, and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
abstract: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management. The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology. Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy. This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.

title: Styloidogenic Jugular Venous Compression Syndrome: A Rare Vascular Variant of Eagle Syndrome.
abstract: Styloidogenic jugular venous compression syndrome, a recently recognized vascular variant of Eagle syndrome, a rare condition caused by the elongation of the styloid process or calcification of the stylohyoid ligament, occurs when the internal jugular vein is compressed between the styloid process and C1 transverse process, leading to a spectrum of neurovascular and cervicofacial symptoms. A 46-year-old male pilot presented with right-sided pulsatile tinnitus, vertigo, and episodic near-syncope that progressively worsened over 4 years despite multiple interventions. Computed tomography and MRI revealed an elongated right styloid process (approximately 35 mm) compressing the internal jugular vein against the C1 transverse process. The patient underwent a right-sided styloidectomy with partial resection of the C1 transverse process by a transcervical approach. The facial and spinal accessory nerves were preserved, and postoperative recovery was uneventful. By postoperative day 2, the patient reported near-complete resolution of tinnitus and pain, with sustained improvement at 1-month follow-up. Styloidogenic jugular venous compression syndrome should be considered for patients with pulsatile tinnitus or symptoms of impaired cerebral venous outflow. Computed tomography venography is considered the diagnostic gold standard. Surgical decompression through styloidectomy with C1 resection can provide effective and durable symptom relief. Early diagnosis and surgical management can result in excellent outcomes.

title: Internal Jugular Compression Syndrome Because of Compression Between the Styloid Process and C1 Transverse Process: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis, and Management.
abstract: Internal jugular vein (IJV) compression at the skull base represents a rare cause of cerebral venous outflow obstruction and may mimic Eagle's syndrome. Unlike classic Eagle's syndrome, this condition results from venous compression between the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and the styloid process, producing symptoms such as pulsatile tinnitus, headache, and cognitive disturbances. We describe our experience highlighting the diagnostic protocol and management strategies. We retrospectively reviewed 5 patients with symptomatic IJV compression syndrome. Demographics, clinical presentation, and treatment outcomes were analyzed. Diagnostic evaluation included computed tomography venography, duplex ultrasonography with head rotation, and cerebral angiography. Four (80%) patients underwent microsurgical decompression of the IJV through a posterolateral suboccipital approach with resection of the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and decompression of the V2-V3 vertebral artery. One patient was managed conservatively. The mean age was 57 years (3 females, 2 males). The mean symptom duration was 7.2 years. Presenting symptoms included pulsatile tinnitus, headache, dizziness, syncope, ear pain, and cognitive complaints. Two patients (40%) had undergone previous treatment without symptom relief. Postoperatively, 3 patients (75%) experienced complete resolution of symptoms and one demonstrated partial symptom improvement with persistent tinnitus attributable to neurovascular compression of cranial nerve VIII. Imaging confirmed restoration of IJV patency in all cases. One patient had spontaneous symptom resolution because of extensive venous collaterals. One patient developed intraoperative vertebral artery dissection because of atherosclerosis which was managed by endarterectomy and reconstruction with Hemashield patch. IJV compression syndrome caused by the hypertrophic C1 transverse process is a distinct clinical condition that should be considered in patients with refractory pulsatile tinnitus or suspected venous intracranial hypertension. Computed tomography venography of head and neck along with head rotation is critical for diagnosis. Microsurgical decompression through a posterolateral far-lateral approach provides effective symptom relief and durable restoration of venous outflow.

title: Quantifying the Effect of Synthetic Colour Fundus Photograph Scaling on Foundation Models
abstract: Abstract Scaling synthetic colour fundus photographs (CFPs) offers a tunable strategy for retinal foundation-model pretraining. From 28,430 real CFPs, we generated 568,600 synthetic CFPs and compared six one-pass strategies: real-only, synthetic-only, real-plus-1×synthetic, real-plus-5×synthetic, real-plus-10×synthetic and real-plus-20×synthetic. Average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was highest in internal validation with real-plus-10×synthetic (0.906 versus 0.862 for real-only across 12 test datasets), but in external validation with real-plus-20×synthetic (0.777 versus 0.683 across eight datasets). The real-plus-1×synthetic strategy increased both averages with the lowest counted computation among real-plus-synthetic strategies. At a matched image count, synthetic-only achieved comparable average external AUROC to real-only. Generation accounted for approximately 99% of the estimated 9 × 10¹⁹ floating-point operations for generation and backbone pretraining. These findings identify complementary uses of synthetic scaling: lower-volume supplementation for a performance–computation balance and larger volumes for stronger external generalisation, with strategy selection guided by evaluation objectives and computational resources.

title: Predictive Value of Quantitative T2-Weighted MRI Morphometric Parameters for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in PI-RADS v2.1 ≥4 Lesions
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of quantitative T2-weighted MRI morphometric parameters for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) in prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 category ≥ 4. Methods This retrospective study included 153 patients who underwent multiparametric MRI according to the PI-RADS v2.1 protocol followed by prostate biopsy. A total of 165 prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 scores ≥4were analyzed. Based on histopathological results, lesions were classified as csPCa or benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Quantitative morphometric parameters, including maximum diameter, mean diameter, cross-sectional area, and volume, were measured on tri-planar T2-weighted images. Differences between csPCa and BPH lesions, as well as zone-specific characteristics in the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ), were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of each parameter and to determine optimal cutoff values. Results Among the 165 lesions, 108 were csPCa (69 in the PZ and 39 in the TZ) and 57 were BPH (20 in the PZ and 37 in the TZ). csPCa lesions demonstrated significantly larger maximum diameter, mean diameter, area, and volume compared with BPH lesions in both the PZ and TZ (all p < 0.05). ROC analysis showed that lesion volume achieved the highest diagnostic performance among all morphometric parameters, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.819 in the PZ and 0.811 in the TZ. The optimal volume thresholds for differentiating csPCa from BPH were 1.23 cm³ in the PZ and 1.07 cm³ in the TZ, respectively. Conclusions In prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 category ≥ 4, lesion volume demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy compared with maximum diameter, mean diameter, and area. Volume-based assessment may serve as a valuable quantitative imaging biomarker to improve the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer, particularly when accounting for zone-specific differences.

title: Clinical criteria for suspected early hip osteoarthritis at the earliest radiographic stage: an international Technical Expert Panel study
abstract: Abstract Background Early hip osteoarthritis (EHOA) remains challenging to recognise at presentation, particularly when symptoms are recent and radiographic abnormalities are absent or minimal. Standardised clinical criteria for this stage are limited. This study aimed to develop expert-derived criteria for identifying suspected EHOA at the earliest radiographic stage and to propose monitoring suggestions. Methods An international, multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel study was conducted, supported by a structured literature review and expert panel voting. Candidate items were generated from the literature review and face-to-face expert discussion, then organised into domains and subdomains. Items were included in the final framework when they achieved > 66% agreement. The perceived strength of each retained item was rated on a 0–10 numerical scale. Results The final framework included two overarching areas: criteria for identifying suspected EHOA and suggestions for careful monitoring. Five domains were retained for identification: exclusion/applicability criteria, symptoms and signs, risk factors, time framework and imaging. Key clinical indicators included load-related mechanical pain, pain during hip rotation, brief start-up or morning stiffness, walking limitation and difficulty with squatting, getting in or out of a car, and putting on socks. Supportive risk factors included elevated body mass index, previous hip symptoms, occupational loading, high-level sports participation, previous hip injury or surgery, family history, femoroacetabular impingement, hip dysplasia, Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, slipped capital femoral epiphysis and leg-length discrepancy. A symptom duration of < 6 months was retained as the preferred timeframe. Baseline radiography was emphasised to exclude established OA, while MRI and ultrasound were considered selective complementary tools. Conclusions This Technical Expert Panel proposes a clinical framework for identifying suspected EHOA at the earliest radiographic stage and guiding careful monitoring. Prospective studies are required to validate its diagnostic and prognostic performance before clinical implementation as formal criteria.

title: Lightweight Pure 3D Lung Nodule Detection and Segmentation Network with Asymmetric Feature Interaction
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D CNNs) for lung nodule analysis face a tension between accuracy and computational cost: isotropic cubic kernels match anisotropic CT data poorly, detection and segmentation are modeled in isolation, and parameter-constrained networks collapse to the trivial all-background solution under class imbalance. This study proposes Light3D-NoduleNet, a lightweight pure 3D joint detection and segmentation network for edge deployment. An asymmetric 3D depthwise separable convolution factorizes the cubic kernel into in-plane and inter-slice branches, cutting kernel parameters by about 56%; a scale-aware efficient channel attention adapts its kernel size to the channel count; and a bidirectional feature interaction module exchanges a spatial attention map and a channel attention vector between the two branches, closing the loop between tasks. Joint training on LUNA16 and LIDC-IDRI uses dynamic loss masking. On LIDC-IDRI, the model reaches a Dice coefficient of 0.5233 (median 95% Hausdorff distance 6.00 mm) with 5.24 M parameters and 178.3 G FLOPs, exceeding reproduced 3D U-Net and V-Net by 0.1545 and 0.0701. Three variants lacking bidirectional interaction all stagnate at 0.2302 after 100 epochs, whereas the full model converges to 0.5233. On a 15 W Jetson Orin NX it runs at 3.0 FPS with 435 MB VRAM, indicating that bidirectional feature interaction is a necessary architectural condition for lightweight 3D networks to escape the trivial solution under extreme foreground-background imbalance.

title: Ultrasound Deep Learning for Distinguishing Benign Reactive from Hematologic Malignancy-Associated Cervical Lymphadenopathy in Children: Development and Validation
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical lymphadenopathy is a common reason for pediatric outpatient visits. It is usually reactive but may also accompany leukemia or lymphoma. Because these conditions may have overlapping ultrasound appearances, we developed a deep-learning model to distinguish benign reactive from hematologic malignancy-associated cervical lymphadenopathy. The model may provide valuable support for diagnosing hematologic malignancies and guiding differential diagnosis in pediatric outpatient practice. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 653 cervical lymph-node annotations after four duplicate images with discordant diagnoses were excluded. The benign reactive group comprised 283 annotations, and the hematologic malignancy-associated group comprised 370. Related images were kept in the same data fold, yielding 559 non-redundant image groups for analysis. An ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetV2-S model using consensus lesion masks was evaluated with grouped nested five-fold cross-validation. Model probabilities were calibrated with Platt scaling. The primary endpoint was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and the Brier score were also assessed. Results The model achieved an AUC of 0.863 (95% confidence interval, 0.834 to 0.893) and an average precision of 0.865. title: MVMGNN: Multi-View Masked Graph Neural Network for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis using Structural MRI
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, and early diagnosis is essential for timely intervention. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) provides valuable information for characterizing AD-related brain alterations. However, existing sMRI-based brain graph methods often rely on single graph construction strategies, limiting their ability to capture complementary spatial and morphological relationships among brain regions. Moreover, multi-view approaches may introduce redundant features and noisy connections without effective selection and fusion mechanisms.To address these issues, we propose a Multi-View Masked Graph Neural Network (MVMGNN) for AD diagnosis using sMRI data. Brain regions are represented as graph nodes with radiomics features, and two complementary graph views are constructed based on spatial proximity and feature similarity. A joint node–edge masking mechanism is introduced to adaptively select informative feature dimensions and structural connections. In addition, a patient-level cross-view gated fusion module is developed to integrate multi-view representations. Experimental results on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that MVMGNN achieves competitive performance compared with existing methods across AD-related classification tasks. Interpretability analysis further reveals discriminative brain regions and structural connections associated with AD, providing insights into sMRI-based brain network analysis.

title: Vision Foundation Models for Multi-Modal Medical Image Classification
abstract: Abstract Clinicians combine several imaging modalities to reach a diagnosis. Yet assembling large annotated datasets for every modality combination is rarely feasible, and modalities are frequently missing in practice. Vision foundation models (FMs) could ease both problems by transferring from few labels, but this has mainly been shown for single images. We therefore compare FM initialisation (DINOv2 and MedSigLIP) against random initialisation, across fusion and training strategies, on three tasks: glioma subtyping from multi-sequence MRI, HER2 scoring from paired histopathology stains, and liver-lesion classification from multi-phase MRI. At full data, FM initialisation matched or outperformed random initialisation, raising liver-lesion sensitivity from 54 % to 76 %. The advantage held as labels grew scarce and was largest under missing modalities, where FM initialisation kept sensitivity near 73 % as random initialisation fell to 29 %. For multi-modal medical imaging, FM initialisation is a strong default, most valuable when labels are scarce or acquisition protocols incomplete.

title: Analyzing the Prognostic Value of Radiomic Variables from PET-CT with [18F]FDG in a Retrospective Cohort of Patients with Adrenocortical Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate whether radiomic features extracted from [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT are associated with established prognostic factors and survival outcomes in patients with adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) in an exploratory proof-of-concept study. Methods In this retrospective study, 22 patients with histologically confirmed ACC who underwent pretreatment [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT were included. Conventional PET metrics (SUVmax, SUVmean, MTV, and TLG) and radiomic features were extracted. Dimensionality reduction was performed using principal component analysis (PCA). Machine learning models were developed to predict 5-year survival. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC). Associations between imaging parameters and clinical-pathological variables were evaluated statistically. Results Interobserver agreement for tumor segmentation was high (mean DSC = 86.2% ± 6.0%). The Naive Bayes model based on both PET and CT data achieved the highest accuracy among all other models (AUC = 0.750). Conventional PET parameters were not significantly correlated with Ki-67 or Weiss score; however, higher TLG had a non-significant association with p53-positive tumors in this small sample (p = 0.065). Conclusions Radiomic features derived from [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT demonstrate potential prognostic value in ACC. PET-based models outperformed CT-based models. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Diagnostic Value of Peripheral Zone PSA Density for Detecting Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in Men with Peripheral Zone MRI Lesions Running title: Peripheral Zone PSA Density in Prostate Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Whole-gland prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD) may underestimate the diagnostic contribution of peripheral zone (PZ) tumors, as it is diluted by transition zone (TZ) volume, which expands with age independent of cancer risk. We investigated whether PZ-specific PSAD (PSAD_PZ) improves the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) in men with PZ-only multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) target lesions, and evaluated the analogous TZ-specific PSAD (PSAD_TZ) in men with TZ-only targets. Methods We analyzed 651 men from the prospectively enrolled SUPER-PC registry, supplemented by a retrospectively identified non-cancer cohort, who underwent combined systematic and MRI-targeted fusion biopsy (416 with PZ-only and 235 with TZ-only mpMRI targets). Clinically significant prostate cancer was defined as International Society of Urological Pathology Grade Group 2 or greater. The diagnostic performance of PSA, whole-gland PSAD, and zone-specific PSAD was compared using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and optimal cut-off values were determined using the Youden index. Results In the PZ-target group, PSAD_PZ achieved a significantly higher area under the curve (AUC) than PSA (0.825 vs. 0.707, p < 0.001) and whole-gland PSAD (0.825 vs. 0.702, p < 0.001). This advantage persisted among men with Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) category 4 or higher lesions (AUC 0.842) and remained significant after multivariable adjustment. The optimal PSAD_PZ cut-off value was 0.285 ng/mL/cm³, yielding a sensitivity of 70.8% and specificity of 84.3%. PSAD_TZ did not outperform PSA or whole-gland PSAD in the TZ-target group. Conclusions PSAD_PZ improves the detection of csPCa in men with PZ-only mpMRI targets and outperforms conventional whole-gland PSAD, supporting a zone-matched normalization strategy that may help reduce unnecessary biopsies and guide treatment decisions. PSAD_TZ conferred no comparable benefit among men with TZ-only targets.

title: CT Colonography as a Triage Examination After a Positive Fecal Immunochemical Test: A Retrospective Cohort Study in a Chilean Screening Program
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate computed tomography colonography (CTC) as a triage examination for colonoscopy within a fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based colorectal cancer screening program in a resource-limited region of Chile. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included asymptomatic FIT-positive individuals aged 45–75 years who underwent CTC between January 2019 and November 2022. Patients with CT Colonography Reporting and Data System (C-RADS) C2–C4 findings were referred for optical colonoscopy. The primary outcome was the per-patient positive predictive value (PPV) of CTC for polyps measuring ≥ 6 mm among patients with an evaluable colonoscopy. Results: The cohort comprised 675 patients (mean age 64.0 years, SD 9.2; 443 women, 65.6%). Overall, 473 patients (70.1%) were classified as C1 and were not referred for immediate colonoscopy, 62 (9.2%) had C3–C4 findings and 71 (10.5%) had unresolved C0 examinations. Of 131 patients referred for colonoscopy, 115 (87.8%) underwent the procedure and 108 had an evaluable examination. Colonoscopy confirmed at least one polyp measuring ≥ 6 mm in 93 patients, yielding a PPV of 86.1% (95% CI 78.3–91.4). Advanced colorectal neoplasia was confirmed in 48 patients (PPV 44.4%, 95% CI 35.4–53.8). The detection rates was 42/675 (6.2%) for advanced adenoma and 6/675 (0.9%) for colorectal cancer. Conclusion: Among FIT-positive patients with CTC findings warranting colonoscopy, clinically relevant colorectal lesions were frequently confirmed. CTC may help prioritize colonoscopy in settings with limited endoscopic capacity. Further evaluation of the complete screening pathway is warranted.

title: Ethmoidal alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma with orbital extension in a young adult: A case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is an uncommon malignant neoplasm of skeletal muscle differentiation that predominantly affects children. Sinonasal RMS is rare in adults, and the alveolar subtype tends toward aggressive local growth with regional and distant spread. Its clinical and radiologic presentation can overlap with inflammatory, infectious, and other malignant sinonasal processes, which makes diagnosis difficult. Case presentation A 28-year-old Middle Eastern man presented with a one-week history of right-sided proptosis and right eye pain, associated with diplopia and painful upward gaze but without prominent sinonasal symptoms. Computed tomography demonstrated a heterogeneous expansile mass centered in the right ethmoid and maxillary sinuses with extension through the lamina papyracea into the right orbit. Endoscopic sinus surgery with tumor debulking and biopsy demonstrated erosion of the lamina papyracea and extensive involvement of the ethmoid air cells. Histopathology showed an infiltrative malignant small round blue cell neoplasm arranged in nests and lobules separated by delicate fibrovascular stroma, with brisk mitotic activity, including seven mitotic figures per high-power field. Tumor cells showed diffuse strong nuclear expression of myogenin and MyoD1 and retained INI1. Pan-cytokeratin, CK5/6, chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100, CD99, FLI1, CD20, and CD3 were negative. Molecular testing was positive for FOXO1 rearrangement, supporting the diagnosis of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma. Staging demonstrated no definite distant metastatic disease. Systemic chemotherapy with ifosfamide and etoposide was initiated, and the patient remains under treatment and follow-up. Conclusion Adult sinonasal alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is rare and can be difficult to diagnose; it may present with orbital manifestations despite limited sinonasal symptoms. Its characteristic morphology, myogenic immunophenotype, and FOXO1 rearrangement help establish the diagnosis. Management requires a multidisciplinary team and careful evaluation of orbital and intracranial extension.

title: Sonographic Appearance of Congenital Cervical Teratoma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background : Cervical teratomas account for only 3–9% of neonatal teratomas. Although usually benign, they may cause significant airway compression, necessitating prompt diagnosis and surgical intervention. Cervical teratomas are typically cystic or cystic-solid and often contain calcifications; a predominantly solid, hypervascular mass without calcification is rare and may pose a diagnostic challenge. We report such a case to highlight its atypical sonographic features and the diagnostic value of combining ultrasound with color Doppler imaging and ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (FNA). Case presentation : A six-hour-old female neonate was transferred for respiratory distress after tracheal intubation. Physical examination revealed a firm midline cervical mass (4×3×5cm). Ultrasonography showed a predominantly solid, heterogeneously echogenic mass with irregular margins and increased vascularity. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated mild enhancement with tracheal displacement, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed tracheal compression. Ultrasound-guided FNA yielded fibrous and cartilaginous elements, supporting the diagnosis of teratoma. The tumor was surgically resected, and histopathology confirmed a mature solid teratoma. Conclusions : Cervical teratomas may present atypically as predominantly solid, hypervascular masses without detectable calcification. In neonates with respiratory distress and a cervical mass, prompt diagnosis and surgery are imperative. Ultrasonography combined with color Doppler imaging and FNA provides valuable preoperative information for surgical decision-making.

title: Sex differences in quantitative fundus parameters measured by artificial intelligence: a cross-sectional community study
abstract: Abstract Background Automated analysis of fundus photographs yields numerous quantitative measures, but sex differences in these measures and their modification by systemic conditions are not well characterized. We quantified these differences in a large community screening cohort. Methods This cross-sectional study included 21,844 participants contributing 32,576 eye-level records to a community health-screening program in Ganzhou, China. EVisionAI was used to quantify 49 vascular, optic disc and cup, peripapillary atrophy, and fundus tessellation density parameters from color fundus photographs. Generalized estimating equations clustered by participant estimated male-female differences in standardized parameters. Models were unadjusted, adjusted for age and age squared, and further adjusted for 20 binary systemic conditions. Sex-by-condition interactions were examined for 19 conditions; prostatic hyperplasia was assessed separately using a three-level variable. Benjamini–Hochberg correction was applied across all fundus parameters within each model for the primary comparisons and within each condition for the interaction analyses. Results Mean age was 63.6 ± 9.8 years in women and 63.9 ± 10.1 years in men. After full adjustment and FDR correction, sex differences were found in 41 of 49 parameters: 19 of 22 optic disc and cup, 8 of 11 vascular, 7 of 7 peripapillary atrophy, and 7 of 9 fundus tessellation density measures. The largest standardized differences in men were a lower disc vertical-to-horizontal ratio (β = −0.170; 95% confidence interval, − 0.196 to − 0.144) and a higher atrophy arc height-to-disc vertical diameter ratio (β = 0.166; 95% confidence interval, 0.141 to 0.192). The arteriole-to-venule ratio was also lower in men (β = −0.113; 95% confidence interval, − 0.137 to − 0.089). Estimates were generally stable across models. Twenty-three effect-modification findings remained significant after false discovery rate correction, predominantly involving prostatic hyperplasia. Conclusions Sex differences were present across most quantitative fundus parameters and changed little after adjustment for measured systemic conditions. Their relevance to screening requires validation in datasets with ocular biometry and clinical outcomes.

title: Habitat Radiomics-Based Stacking Ensemble Model for Predicting Disease-Free Survival in Early-Stage Cervical Cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose Despite undergoing curative surgery, about 30% of patients with early-stage cervical cancer (ECC) face the risk of recurrence. However, current prognostic tools are not very effective, with concordance index (C-index) typically ranging from 0.60 to 0.70. This study aimed to develop and validate a stacking survival ensemble model that incorporates intratumoral and peritumoral habitat radiomic features derived from routine preoperative multiparametric MRI to predict postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) in ECC. Methods This retrospective-prospective study enrolled 583 ECC patients (training: n = 293, internal validation: n = 165, external validation: n = 125). Habitat radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and 3-mm peritumoral regions on preoperative T2WI, DWI, and CE-T1WI. A two-tier stacking survival ensemble framework was constructed with five base survival models (Cox regression, Random Survival Forest, Elastic Net-Cox, DeepSurv, and Support Vector Regression) and a Cox regression Meta-learner. Performance was assessed by C-index, time-dependent AUC, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. The incremental value of the model-derived lymph node metastasis probability (pLNM) from our prior classification model was also evaluated. Results The Meta-model achieved C-indices of 0.878, 0.868, and 0.848 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, outperforming most base models (P < 0.05). Externally, it yielded time-dependent AUCs of 0.887, 0.875, and 0.860 at 12, 24, and 36 months. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the Meta-model effectively stratified into high- and low-risk groups with distinct DFS outcomes (log-rank P < 0.001 for all cohorts). Adding pLNM further improved C-index from 0.878 to 0.913 in the training cohort (P < 0.001). Conclusion The stacking survival ensemble model enables accurate postoperative risk stratification for ECC patients using routine preoperative MRI without additional imaging, potentially guiding individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance intensity.

Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the Meta-model effectively stratified into high- and low-risk groups with distinct DFS outcomes (log-rank P < 0.001 for all cohorts). Adding pLNM further improved C-index from 0.878 to 0.913 in the training cohort (P < 0.001). Conclusion The stacking survival ensemble model enables accurate postoperative risk stratification for ECC patients using routine preoperative MRI without additional imaging, potentially guiding individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance intensity.

title: Exploring the Spectrum of Clinical and Radiological Findings in Active Tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract Background Clinical data may not accurately diagnose pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), mainly due to manifestation overlap with other diseases, causing delays and misdiagnoses. Many gaps in the interpretation of clinical and radiographic findings were addressed and updated in our study. Methods An institutional-based study was carried out between 02/01/2018 and 26/06/2020 to clinically assess TB outpatients in high-burden zones. Those patients were identified through smear microscopy, GeneXpert Ultra, and chest X-rays and TB positives were interviewed. Of total, 329 patients were enrolled from Bench-Skeko, 23 from Skeka, and 29 from Keffa. Both descriptive and inferential statistics were performed using Stata 14/16. Results A total of 410 TB confirmed cases, with 328 (80%) being PTB, 79 (19.3%) EPTB, and 3 (0.73%) involving both forms were involved in this study. The mean age was 27.65 ± 11.44 years, with 55% male. Most patients were recently identified (99.3%). GeneXpert was used in 62.4%, AFB in 8.78%, and lesion biopsy or FNAC for EPTB in 16.83%, and 98% was on the intensive therapy for susceptible TB. A febrile episode was diagnosed in 93% (5.4% >40°C, 87% <39°C), night sweat in 93.17%, appetite loss in 89%, fatigue in 90%, and weight loss in 88%. Respiratory symptoms were very common, with cough reported in 94.2%: productive in 91%, and prolonged (> 3 wks) in 77%. Abnormalities in chest X ray were reported in 16.3%, with pleural effusion in 11.2%, cavitary formations in 13%, and lymph node enlarged in 14%. Blood pressure abnormalities were relatively low, with 76.3% having normal. Only few findings were reported as statistically significant predictors of active PTB. Chest abnormalities (OR = 6.87), prolonged cough (OR = 6.4), mucoid (OR = 14.6), and mucopurulent sputum (OR = 56.4) increased PTB odds, while lymphadenopathy was less commonly reported (OR = 0.16). Appetite loss (OR = 3.26), pleural effusion (OR = 2.41), and fibrosis (OR = 2.31) showed weak associations. Conclusions A high prevalence of the TB tetrad: prolonged cough, night sweat, fever and appetite loss were observed. PTB odds were higher with chest abnormalities, effusion, fibrosis, infiltration, and expansion, highlighting the diagnostic value of radiology. Clinical Trial Registration : No applicable

title: Unsupervised multimodal brain MRI registration with complementary learned and structural descriptors.
abstract: Abstract Deformable registration of T1- and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance images is difficult because tissue intensities differ across contrasts. We investigate whether learned and hand-crafted descriptors provide complementary similarity information for unsupervised registration. A Cross-Modal Descriptor Network learns contrast-invariant voxel embeddings through self-supervised contrastive training on aligned same-subject pairs. These embeddings are combined with the modality-independent neighbourhood descriptor with self-similarity context (MIND-SSC) to train a compact diffeomorphic attention U-Net without anatomical labels. In inter-subject T1-to-T2 registration on the IXI dataset (n=45), the hybrid achieved a mean Dice coefficient of 0.700 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance of 3.21 mm, with no observed folded voxels. It outperformed the evaluated classical, learned, structural-descriptor, transformer, and foundation-model baselines (p<0.05, paired Wilcoxon tests). Gains were largest for small deep gray-matter structures, and the hybrid also performed best in the evaluated unseen-scanner and BraTS glioma experiments. Descriptors are used only during training; inference requires one 83 ms forward pass of a 0.247 M-parameter network. These results support combining learned and structural descriptors for accurate and computationally efficient multimodal brain registration.

title: QSGT: Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer for Faithful Multi-modal Radiology Report Summarization
abstract: Abstract Improving the alignment between visual evidence andtextual descriptions in medical vision-language models(VLM) remains a critical challenge for achieving entitylevelfaithfulness in low-resource generation tasks. Thispaper proposes Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer(QSGT), a hybrid approach of token pruningand mixture of experts (MoE), grounded on the conceptionof quantum many-body wavefunction. This hybridapproach was aimed at improving the selectionof both modality-specific expert tokens and the formationof non-dominating experts to determine stableconjugates. The token pruning approach was improvedusing the quantum orbital style token assignments andthe mixture of experts by the quantum doubly occupancyapproximation. We also introduce two clinicallymotivated regularization terms, pair loss and seniorityloss, further enforce semantic consistency and dominanceof diagnostically relevant features. Our extensiveexperiments across seven thoracic disease categoriesdemonstrate that QSGT significantly outperforms stateof-the-art medical VLMs on multiple evaluation metrics,including RadGraph (36.2), SPICE (42.68), andconsistently high BERTScore (98), on the MIMIC-CXRtest set. QSGT achieves substantial gains in clinical correctnessand semantic accuracy, particularly for complexconditions such as pneumonia and pneumothorax. Ablationstudies confirmthe importance of each architecturalcomponent, while convergence analyses show stable andinterpretable learning dynamics. These results indicate that QSGT provides a robust and clinically meaningfulsolution for multimodal medical report summarization,enabling more reliable, interpretable, and patientcentredclinical AI systems.

title: Clinical cutoffs for plasma biomarkers to identify intracranial pathology in traumatic brain injury patients with Glasgow Coma Scale scores 13 to 15: a TRACK-TBI study.
abstract: The authors sought to identify plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase-L1 (UCH-L1) cutoffs corresponding to a range of high positive predictive values (PPVs) for detecting intracranial pathology on CT and detecting pathology on MRI (when CT is negative) in patients who present to a level I trauma center for TBI evaluation with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores of 13-15. This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data from the Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury (TRACK-TBI) study, which is a longitudinal, observational study of patients with TBI who presented to one of 18 US level I trauma centers within 24 hours of injury. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours. Plasma samples were analyzed for GFAP (pg/mL) and UCH-L1 (pg/mL). The CT or MRI scan was considered positive (CT+, MRI+) if there was evidence of acute intracranial pathology related to TBI. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis (AUC) was performed to evaluate the ability of day-1 GFAP and UCH-L1 to discriminate CT+ versus CT-, and CT-/MRI+ versus CT-/MRI-. A K-fold cross-validation procedure was used to identify GFAP cutoffs for predicting CT+ among patients with GCS scores of 13-15 and for predicting MRI+ among patients with GCS scores of 13-15 and CT- subjects, based on the adjusted PPV thresholds. Among the 1718 TBI participants with GCS scores 13-15, 633 (37%) had CT+ findings. Of the 1085 CT- participants, 608 underwent MRI at 2 weeks postinjury, of whom 154 (25%) had MRI+ findings. Day-1 GFAP had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82 (95% CI 0.80-0.84), and UCH-L1 had an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.57-0.63) for discriminating CT+ from CT-. Day-1 GFAP had an AUC of 0.76 (95% CI 0.71-0.81) while UCH-L1 had an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.55-0.65) for discriminating CT-/MRI+ from CT-/MRI-. For CT+ prediction, assuming a prevalence of 0.36 (from our data) and 0.1 (from the literature), the median GFAP cutoffs to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.9 were 2879 (95% CI 2195-4704) and 5191 (95% CI 3779-5426), respectively. For MRI+ prediction among GCS 13-15 CT- patients, the median GFAP cutoffs were 1382 (95% CI 1145-2424) to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.9 and 2317 pg/mL (95% CI 1262-2551 pg/mL) to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.98. These threshold values can be used as an aid-in-diagnosis tool and assist in appropriate triaging of patients who have sustained TBI to urgent neuroimaging, potential escalation in care, and interventions as clinically indicated.

title: Near real-time intraoperative assessment of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors using stimulated Raman histology during endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery: comparison with conventional histopathology.
abstract: Accurate intraoperative identification of adenomatous versus normal pituitary tissue remains challenging during surgery for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs), as both can appear similar macroscopically. Stimulated Raman histology (SRH) is a label-free optical imaging technique that provides high-resolution digital histological images of unprocessed tissue within minutes. This study evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic accuracy, and histopathological concordance of SRH compared with conventional hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining in PitNETs. Adult patients (≥ 18 years) who underwent surgery for suspected PitNET were included. Fresh tissue samples from the tumor core and, when feasible, from peritumoral regions were analyzed intraoperatively using SRH followed by standard histopathological processing. A board-certified neuropathologist, blinded to clinical data, independently compared SRH and H&E images regarding diagnostic accuracy, tissue classification (adenomatous vs nonadenomatous), and histopathological features using a semiquantitative scoring system. A total of 28 patients were included, yielding 66 tissue samples for final comparative analysis. SRH imaging was feasible in all cases. SRH demonstrated excellent comparability with conventional H&E in 37 samples (56.1%), good comparability in 20 (30.3%), and low comparability in 9 (13.6%). No significant difference in comparability was observed between tumor core and peritumoral tissue samples (p = 0.409). SRH accurately depicted key histopathological features, including the loss of the lobular glandular structure in adenomatous tissue and connective tissue organization in surrounding structures. Characteristic subtype features-such as Crooke cells in corticotroph PitNET or perivascular tumor cell arrangements in gonadotroph PitNET-were also identifiable. SRH showed high feasibility for intraoperative assessment of PitNETs, generating near H&E-quality digital images within minutes. It reliably enabled distinguishing tumor from normal gland tissue and detected tumor infiltration into adjacent structures. These findings support SRH as a useful aid to intraoperative decision-making in pituitary surgery, with future AI integration likely to further improve diagnostic speed and accuracy.

title: Osteoporosis Screening Gaps Among Patients Undergoing Lumbar Fusion Surgery.
abstract: Osteoporosis is associated with elevated complication rates after lumbar fusion surgery. Despite this, osteoporosis remains both underscreened and undertreated in the United States. Currently, rates of dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DEXA) screening before lumbar fusion surgery are unknown, as is the proportion of patients who, after being diagnosed with osteoporosis, receive appropriate treatment. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess osteoporosis screening and treatment rates among patients undergoing lumbar fusion surgery. Patients older than 50 years undergoing lumbar fusion for lumbar stenosis with degenerative spondylolisthesis were identified using the TriNetX database. Patients receiving surgery for indications of malignancy or infection, as well as those with diagnoses of osteoporosis before the screening window, were excluded. The prevalence of DEXA scans in the 2 years before fusion was calculated for the overall cohort and for high-risk cohorts defined by Endocrinology Society guidelines. A secondary analysis assessed rates of osteoporosis treatment among patients receiving preoperative DEXA scans. Of 46,104 patients who underwent lumbar fusion surgery, only 4.5% of men and 15.6% of women received a preoperative DEXA scan in the 2 years before their fusion. Women were more likely to receive DEXA scans than men (OR, 3.93; 95% CI, 3.64 to 4.23; P < 0.001). Only 5.6% of high-risk men and 17.5% of high-risk women received preoperative DEXA screening. Among patients diagnosed with osteoporosis after DEXA screening, only 11.0% received anabolic therapy and 23.1% received antiresorptive therapy. Despite most patients undergoing lumbar fusion being at risk of osteoporosis (and eligible for screening), a small minority were screened using DEXA in the 2 years before surgery. Efforts are warranted to increase the prevalence of DEXA screening so that osteoporosis is appropriately diagnosed and treated before lumbar fusion surgery.

title: AI-Enhanced Segmentation and Scoring of Histopathological Growth Patterns in Resected Colorectal Liver Metastases
abstract: Histopathological growth patterns, predominantly the presence of an encapsulated rim, serve as powerful prognostic biomarkers in colorectal liver metastases. However, conventional visual estimation is limited by interobserver variability, human rounding bias, and categorical thresholds. We aimed to develop and externally validate a deep-learning segmentation framework that produces continuous, spatially resolved, and objective encapsulation metrics from routine whole-slide images. In this multicenter study of chemo-naive resected CRLM patients, a modified nnU-Net architecture was developed on 40 pixel-annotated H&E-stained WSIs to segment liver parenchyma, tumor, and the encapsulation interface. Model performance was optimized across spatial resolutions. An automated continuous AI encapsulation score was computed to determine patient-level metrics. The prognostic value for 5-year overall survival was evaluated using restricted cubic spline Cox regression, a log-rank optimized threshold, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses across a main cohort (Erasmus MC; n=546, 1,910 WSIs) and an independent external validation cohort (Radboud UMC; n=212, 615 WSIs). The segmentation network achieved optimal tissue boundary delineation at a resolution of 2.0 micrometer/pixel on the 40 annotated slides (overall foreground DICE: 0.86+-0.09; encapsulation DICE: 0.70+-0.11). Spline modeling demonstrated that while visual assessment displayed non-linear hazard plateaus, the continuous AI encapsulation score exhibited a linear reduction in mortality risk across the critical intermediate range (25%-75% encapsulation, p=7.81x10^(-4)). Log-rank optimization identified a primary global threshold at 47.4% (p=3.73x10^(-8)), which in confirmed significant OS stratification in external validation (p=0.018). A secondary threshold was found at 69% (p=2.93x10^(-6)) that captured high-encapsulation favorable-risk patients matching the current manual 100% Rotterdam cut-off. Our deep-learning model transforms qualitative HGP grading into a continuous, explainable, and fully automated prognostic biometry. By eliminating observer subjectivity and capturing fine-grained risk gradients, the model establishes a scalable, standardized foundation for CRLM risk stratification on digital pathology.
