title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients
abstract: Background: Alterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown. Methods: We conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients. Results: ALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearman's rho = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearman's rho = -0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p < 0.001). Discussion: These findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.

title: Loss of Farnesoid X Receptor Signaling Promotes Choroidal Neovascularization in Mice
abstract: Choroidal neovascularization (CNV) is a defining feature of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). Although anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapies suppress neovascular activity, incomplete responses, recurrent leakage, and subretinal fibrosis remain important clinical challenges. The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) is a bile acid-activated nuclear receptor with anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic, and anti-angiogenic functions in other tissues, but its role in CNV is unknown. Analysis of publicly available human transcriptomic data (GSE135092) showed FXR expression in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE)/choroid and significant downregulation in AMD-affected macular RPE/choroid. To define the role of FXR in CNV, laser photocoagulation was performed in wild-type (WT) and FXR-deficient (FXR-KO) mice, with disease progression assessed by in vivo imaging, histology, ex vivo choroidal sprouting, and endothelial cell assays. FXR expression in the RPE/choroid was reduced 14 days after laser injury. Compared with WT mice, FXR-KO mice developed larger CNV lesions, more extensive hyperfluorescence on fluorescein angiography, and increased lesion area during disease progression. FXR deficiency also impaired resolution of fibrotic remodeling. In WT mice, alpha-SMA peaked at day 14 and declined by day 21, whereas collagen I remained low throughout; in FXR-KO mice, both collagen I and alpha-SMA were significantly elevated relative to WT and remained significantly higher than WT at day 21. Consistent with these findings, FXR-deficient choroidal explants exhibited increased vascular sprouting, and FXR-KO endothelial cells formed more extensive capillary-like networks. Together, these findings identify FXR as an endogenous regulator of pathological angiogenesis, vascular leakage, mesenchymal activation, and fibrotic remodeling during CNV and provide a rationale for investigating FXR-directed strategies for nAMD.

title: CVP-BAA: Efficiently Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Various task-specific medical segmentation models have demonstrated strong performance, their heavy reliance on extensive annotations and highly specialized architectures limits their versatility, scalability, and clinical applicability. Recently, adapting vision foundation models, particularly the segment anything model (SAM), has emerged as a promising alternative. However, prevalent parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt tuning and adapter tuning, often lack an explicit mechanism to embed local structural priors into the long-range dependency modeling of vision transformers (ViT), rendering them insufficiently sensitive to fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we introduce CVP-BAA, a novel hybrid PEFT method that improves SAM's sensitivity to domain-specific textures and local details, leading to superior boundary delineation. The proposed CVP-BAA adopts two key ideas. First, it introduces a convolutional visual prompting (CVP) strategy that leverages convolutional features as structural priors, prepending them to the key and value projections within the multi-head self-attention layers of strategically selected ViT blocks. Through a dedicated prompt generation-and-injection module, this mechanism effectively bridges local spatial details with global context semantics. Second, a boundary-aware adapter (BAA) is designed as a parallel branch to the feed-forward network within the same selected blocks. By explicitly computing and amplifying high-frequency components, the BAA enhances feature representations along tissue boundaries and fine-grained lesion structures. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks across three imaging modalities demonstrate that CVP-BAA achieves superior segmentation performance, surpassing existing task-specific models and PEFT-based SAM adaptations in both quantitative metrics and qualitative results.

title: Lychee: Certified Screening of Inverted Lists for High-Recall Vector Search
abstract: Nearest-neighbor search over embedding vectors matches faces against watchlists, transactions against known fraud patterns, and medical images against confirmed cases, where a missed neighbor is a missed threat, fraud, or diagnosis. Because an approximate index cannot report which queries lost a true neighbor, these applications require recall of 0.999 to 0.9999, at a cost far below that of exact search over billions of vectors. Inverted-file indexes reach high recall by probing more lists, but they read and score every probed vector at full precision, so that throughput falls in inverse proportion to the number of probed lists. Graph indexes saturate below these targets, whereas quantized lists must rerank their candidates with the full vectors. Our insight is to decide for almost every probed vector that it cannot enter the top k of the probed lists without reading the vector, through the certified lower bound of exact search by certified exclusion. This paper turns this insight into Lychee, a GPU inverted-file search that screens the probed lists on tensor cores under a threshold from anchors of the same lists and computes exact distances only for the few survivors. We prove that Lychee returns exactly the k nearest vectors of the probed lists, the answer of an inverted-file search at full precision, while it reads a few hundred full vectors per query regardless of the number of probed lists. On eleven datasets from one million to one billion vectors and against ten GPU and CPU baselines, Lychee is 9.7 to 117 times faster than IVF-Flat at equal recall with 200 probed lists on datasets of up to 100 million vectors. It also reaches recall levels that CAGRA and HNSW do not reach and outruns exact search by certified exclusion by 5 to 18 times above ten million vectors. On four GPUs, Lychee searches one billion vectors at recall 0.9999, 44.5 times faster than IVF-Flat on BIGANN-1B.

title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
abstract: Histopathology images are recognized as a reliable and comprehensive modality for Deep Learning (DL) based diagnosis. However, effectiveness is constrained by limited large-scale annotated datasets, as collecting expert-labeled medical data is costly and time-intensive. Recent advances in generative models, particularly diffusion models, demonstrate strong capabilities in synthesizing medically relevant content for dataset augmentation. Existing generative frameworks treat histopathology patches as generic natural images, failing to enforce biological constraints such as histomorphological structures and heterogeneous staining patterns essential for valid synthesis. We propose a guided wavelet diffusion model (GWDM) framework that captures image details at multiple scales using wavelets and leverages controllable conditioning based on domain-specific histopathological features (e.g., tissue patterns and color variations). We further formulate a histomorphological guidance loss applied to real and generated patches. A loss ramping strategy gradually introduces these constraints during training, ensuring stable optimization and robust modeling of tissue architecture. GWDM was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative methods. Ablation studies confirmed that domain-guided conditioning, perceptual loss, and structural similarity loss each contribute meaningfully to synthesis quality. Downstream nuclei and tissue segmentation experiments further validated the clinical utility of GWDM-generated images, demonstrating consistent performance improvements when synthetic data augments real training sets. This work shows that domain-specific conditioning and dual-loss optimization generate realistic histopathology patches, reducing data scarcity and improving clinical downstream segmentation performance.

title: H-2DGS: Height-Field Gaussian Splatting for Sharp and Deformable Neurosurgical Surface Reconstruction
abstract: Neurosurgical navigation commonly presents magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as 2D slices, making it difficult to relate the anatomy in those slices to the cortical surface observed through the surgical microscope. We seek a common 3D visualization that combines a photorealistic reconstruction of the exposed cortex during tumor surgery with whole-brain MRI context and diffusion tractography pathways. This requires the reconstructed cortex to form a clear boundary around the brain anatomy rather than a diffuse volume that obscures internal structures. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) can reproduce observed views but, under limited surgical view coverage, may distribute opacity through a thick and geometrically ambiguous band. We introduce height-field 2D Gaussian Splatting (H-2DGS), a three-stage pipeline that concentrates a robust 3DGS reconstruction, fuses its depth into a shared truncated signed distance field (TSDF) surface, and represents that surface with curved, surface-oriented Gaussian primitives. Separate height, color, and opacity bases provide local geometry and appearance, while a neighbor-transition objective coordinates overlapping patches. The explicit surface further supports postoperative alignment: MRI-derived depth deforms the reconstruction, and tracked-color supervision with alternating optimization preserves its appearance. Across five real neurosurgical cases, H-2DGS gives low multi-view depth inconsistency, a compact 7.97MB representation, and interactive rendering at 29--42ms per frame. The resulting sharp, deformable surface integrates clearly with tractography and MRI anatomy, including a postoperative resection cavity.

title: Diagnostic Loss: Asymmetric Supervision for Radiology Report Generation
abstract: Automated radiology report generation requires models to do more than produce fluent clinical narratives: they must explicitly state supported diagnoses while avoiding unsupported ones. However, existing medical vision-language models (MedVLMs) are typically trained with token-level maximum likelihood objectives, which prioritize text agreement over diagnostically critical terms. As a result, models can miss key diagnoses and introduce wrong ones. We identify this as an objective misalignment between conventional language modeling and the asymmetric diagnostic requirements of radiology reporting. To encode these requirements, we introduce Diagnostic Loss (DLoss), a differentiable, architecture-agnostic objective that operates directly on decoder token probabilities. DLoss separately aggregates probability mass over vocabularies associated with diagnoses supported by the reference report and with unsupported alternatives. Using asymmetric pooling across token positions in the report, it encourages supported diagnoses to receive sufficient probability in at least one position while suppressing spurious probability spikes for unsupported diagnoses across all positions during training. The loss can be applied to existing 3D MedVLMs without modifying their vision backbones, language decoders, or inference procedures, and introduces no additional inference-time computation. We train and evaluate DLoss on 50,000 abdominal CT scans across several 3D MedVLM architectures on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution report-generation benchmarks. Across these settings, DLoss improves diagnostic faithfulness while maintaining competitive performance on conventional language-generation metrics, showing the value of asymmetric sequence-level supervision for radiology report generation. The code for DLoss is available at https://github.com/gmum/DLoss.

title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
abstract: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
abstract: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent

On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. title: Pos4CHD: A Positive-Free Mask-Guided Counterfactual Synthesis Framework for Fetal Congenital Heart Defect Analysis
abstract: The scarcity of positive cases remains a major bottleneck in developing automated diagnostic systems for fetal Congenital Heart Defects~(CHDs), particularly for rare subtypes. Although normal cases are accessible with effort, positive cases are hard to collect due to low incidence rates and privacy concerns, causing severe class imbalance or absence of positive training samples. Existing works resort to synthesizing positives with conditional generative models, but they are task-specific and require positive training samples, hindering application for fetal CHDs. To this end, we propose a positive-free mask-guided counterfactual generation framework for fetal echocardiography, namely Pos4CHD, which enables realistic, high-quality synthesis of pseudo-positive samples from semantic masks, with only normal samples at hand. Technically, we first develop FE-Gen, a mask-guided generative model tailored for fetal heart ultrasound synthesis that mitigates histogram drift and enhances image-mask spatial alignment. Building on FE-Gen, Pos4CHD employs a mask-to-image generation paradigm for CHD synthesis. It first manipulates semantic masks to simulate fetal-heart structural anomalies and then renders anatomically consistent images. Extensive experiments on in-house datasets, together with expert evaluations, demonstrate the visual fidelity~($-12.97$ FID) and anatomical consistency~($+3.96\%$ DSC) of synthesized images. Further validations across diverse real-world CHD diagnosis tasks exhibit promising results and consistent increments, including zero-shot classification~(achieving $93.25\%$ ACC on EbA and $72.92\%$ ACC on TAPVC), lesion detection~($+6.95\%$ mAP50 on VSD), and anatomy segmentation~($+10.49\%$ DSC on fetal heart) compared with baselines. Codes and models are publicly available on \href{https://github.com/DREAMXFAR/Pos4CHD}{GitHub}.

title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can answer clinical questions about medical images, but trustworthy use requires visual grounding: models should localize the pathology they report rather than rely on spurious shortcuts. Whether MLLMs can visually ground clinical findings in retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT), the most widely used imaging modality in ophthalmology, remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce RetinaGroundBench, the first benchmark for biomarker visual grounding in retinal OCT. It comprises 815 B-scans exhaustively annotated by ophthalmologists with 4,537 bounding boxes covering 13 biomarkers across 8 diseases. Because MLLMs often fragment a single lesion into multiple partial predictions, we propose AggIoU, a metric that evaluates whether the union of overlapping predicted boxes covers the annotated region. Across 27 open-source MLLMs (0.8-38B parameters), we find that visual grounding remains largely unsolved: the best general-purpose model achieves a macro F1 of just 23.7%, with consistently low recall, despite reaching up to 73% balanced accuracy on biomarker presence questions. To narrow this gap, we developed RetGrounder, an MLLM fine-tuned using an OCT-specific strategy integrating grounding and textual information. Despite its relatively small size (8B), RetGrounder improves grounding F1 to 33.9%, a 43% relative improvement. Our benchmark provides a reference point for measuring progress in the field of OCT diagnosis with MLLMs.

title: Lightweight Frame Compensation for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation under Frame Skipping
abstract: Real-time polyp segmentation in computer-assisted colonoscopy is hampered by the difficulty of deploying high-accuracy models under strict latency budgets. Frame skipping, which performs inference every K frames and reuses or interpolates the rest, improves throughput but introduces motion blur and lesion misalignment that degrade temporal consistency. To close this gap, we propose the Lightweight Frame Compensator (LFC), a 77K-parameter plug-and-play module inserted before a frozen segmentation backbone. Operating on a three-frame window, LFC fuses consecutive frames via spatio-temporal attention into a single compensated frame, and is trained only on pseudo-labels generated by a differently seeded model, without any expert annotation. Experiments on three polyp video benchmarks show that LFC recovers most of the accuracy degraded by direct frame skipping and, in several settings, reaches the accuracy of frame-by-frame inference, while retaining a 2.05X--2.55X throughput gain. We further evaluate the temporal stability of three backbones spanning CNN, pyramid Transformer, and global-attention Transformer architectures, revealing a spectrum of sensitivity to frame skipping that arises from how locally or globally each architecture aggregates misaligned input. The compensation gain of LFC follows this spectrum: it is largest for high-capacity Transformer backbones, which achieve the best static accuracy but suffer the most under skip-frame inference. LFC thus offers a lightweight, pluggable, and deployment-friendly route to real-time polyp segmentation.

title: Reinforcing intra-operative tumour localisation with weak supervision from pre-operative appearances
abstract: Limited tumour visibility on intra-operative images complicates surgical navigation, including liver hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) targeting on computed tomography (CT) imaging. This makes labelled datasets difficult to curate for deep learning, and transferring pre-operative delineations through registration remains challenging due to intra-operative deformation and lack of paired pre- and intra-operative data. We propose to transfer tumour appearances learned from pre-operative magnetic resonance (MR) images to guide localisation on intra-operative CT through weak supervision. A classifier is trained to classify tumour presence on pre-operative images. This is applied to windows on intra-operative images, and despite the domain gap, it assigns higher tumour-presence probabilities on average to tumour-containing windows. These weak cross-domain signals guide a reinforcement learning agent to localise tumours on intra-operative images. We compare direct transfer, few-shot adaptation and synthetic transfer (trained using unpaired MR and CT), which translates CT into synthetic MR before localisation. On an external HCC cohort, synthetic transfer outperformed other tested methods and CT-only baselines. Our framework enables cross-modality tumour localisation without paired MR-CT training images.

title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
abstract: Many clinical decisions are a choice among a few fixed options, taken quickly and in large numbers. Such decisions also need an uncertainty estimate to know when to defer to a clinician. Generative language models answer slowly in free text and state their confidence poorly. In contrast, System 1 models answer zero-shot with a probability for each answer. However, their performance across clinical tasks is unknown. Four System 1 models, two proprietary and two with open weights, were evaluated zero-shot on 86 public tasks from 14 clinical domains in 20 languages, spanning examination questions and medical imaging. Tasks were assigned to six capability tiers before analysis. The primary outcome was the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC). Secondary outcomes included calibration, language effects and comparisons with published results and generative models. Across 179,111 cases, the mean AUROC of the best model per task was 0.94 for medical knowledge, 0.93 for text understanding, 0.83 for clinical judgement from text, 0.89 for image perception, 0.84 for 2D image findings and 0.69 for volumetric findings. Imaging tasks scored 0.09 (95% CI, 0.06 to 0.11) lower than text tasks (P < 0.001). The best model matched or exceeded the best published result on 13 of 26 text tasks and on 8 of 35 imaging tasks. Triage nurses outperformed the best model (accuracy, 0.85 vs. 0.56). One decision took 0.34 to 0.44 seconds and 24 to 81 joules on open-weight models run locally. Accuracy on identical questions fell by up to 39 percentage points from English to Yoruba. Generative models of the same family were 11 to 76 times slower, with 3 to 5 percentage points higher balanced accuracy. System 1 models decide quickly, cheaply and with usable confidence when the answer is stated in a text or recalled from medical knowledge, but not when it must be judged or read from an image.

title: Diffusion-Based Synthesis of Complete 3D Biparametric Prostate MRI
abstract: Synthetic biparametric MRI (bpMRI) may help alleviate the limited availability of large and representative prostate MRI datasets for deep learning applications. In this work, we present a conditional 3D diffusion framework for anatomy-conditioned synthesis of complete prostate bpMRI from anatomical masks. The framework supports sequential synthesis, in which T2w and diffusion modalities are generated by separately trained models, and joint synthesis, in which all bpMRI modalities are generated simultaneously within a single model. Five configurations were trained using PI-CAI, FastMRI Prostate, and PROSTATEx datasets to investigate different conditioning schemes, target modalities, and synthesis strategies. Evaluation using distribution-based metrics, paired-image similarity, and qualitative assessment demonstrated the feasibility of both synthesis pathways. Joint synthesis achieved competitive distributional fidelity while generating complete bpMRI, whereas direct synthesis of ADC and computed high-b-value DWI outperformed their derivation from synthetic diffusion-weighted images.

title: LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality of Superpixels
abstract: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image. Most existing methods are designed for a specific context, with a strong focus on industrial defect detection, where they achieve excellent performance on well-established benchmarks. However, we observe that these methods can exhibit significant performance drops in other contexts, especially when the inlier distribution is multimodal. To account for this inlier complexity, we propose LACToS, a principled local OOD detection method based on statistical typicality and made tractable through two innovations: (i) grouping pixels into superpixels and (ii) using a computationally efficient proxy to estimate typicality. We evaluate LACToS across three diverse applications spanning medical imaging, human faces, and X-ray security screening. LACToS performs more robustly than prior methods across these benchmarks. The code is released here: https://github.com/voilalab/LACToS.

title: Maternal genitourinary tract infections and spontaneous preterm labor: A narrative review of pathogens, pathways, and prevention.
abstract: Preterm birth is the leading cause of death among children aged under 5 years of age worldwide. Maternal genitourinary tract infections (GUTIs) are among the few modifiable risk factors for spontaneous preterm labor (sPTL), yet the gap between association and effective intervention remains unresolved. This narrative review consolidates recent evidence on GUTIs and sPTL, integrating pathogens, ascending and hematogenous pathways, and prevention. MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched (January 2000-January 2026); evidence was synthesized narratively and stratified by preterm-birth subtype where possible. Pooled estimates showed increased odds of preterm birth with urinary tract infection (odds ratio [OR] 1.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.62-2.27), asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB; OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.30-2.01), bacterial vaginosis (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32-2.43), Ureaplasma colonization (OR 2.76, 95% CI 1.63-4.68), Trichomonas vaginalis (relative risk 1.42, 95% CI 1.15-1.75), and Chlamydia trachomatis (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.11-2.22). A 2026 Swedish register cohort (n = 684 595) demonstrates that the hazard for preterm birth after urinary tract infection (UTI) diagnosis is highest in the first 6 days and declines with advancing gestation (adjusted hazard ratios 18.5, 13.5, and 6.7 at 22-27, 28-31, and 32-36 weeks). Gene-environment analyses further indicate that preterm birth subtypes differ in susceptibility to UTI versus vaginal infection. Antibiotic treatment of ASB reduces pyelonephritis (RR 0.24), but its effect on preterm birth in unselected populations is uncertain. Ascending infection drives decidual cytokine release and premature myometrial activation; amniotic-fluid sludge on transvaginal ultrasound is an accessible marker of subclinical intra-amniotic infection. Targeted screening, evidence-based antibiotic selection, and antimicrobial stewardship remain the practical priorities.

title: Compartment-specific skeletal involvement in systemic sclerosis characterized by peripheral QCT and serum osteoimmune mediators: a case-control study.
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with increased bone fragility, yet early, compartment-specific alterations and their osteoimmunological correlates remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to assess bone status in SSc using dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) complemented by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), and to evaluate their associations with a targeted osteoimmunological biomarker panel and clinical risk scores. This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 women with SSc (disease duration ≤ 7 years from diagnosis) and 45 non-immune female controls, frequency-matched by age. Bone status was assessed by DXA (lumbar spine, femoral neck) and distal radius pQCT. Serum levels of routine bone and mineral metabolism markers, alongside a targeted panel of osteoimmunological mediators (OPG, OPN, PDGF-BB, ACP5, RANKL, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1) using multiplex immunoassay were measured. FRAX scores were calculated to contextualize clinical fracture risk. With broadly comparable DXA-defined bone status, pQCT revealed significantly lower trabecular volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) in SSc, while total and cortical+subcortical vBMD were comparable. Routine biochemical markers showed substantial overlap between groups, whereas SSc patients exhibited a distinct osteoimmune profile with significantly elevated OPG, ACP5, RANKL, PDGF-BB, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1, and RANKL/OPG after FDR correction. Exploratory biomarker-bone associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing. In women with relatively early SSc, pQCT identified compartment-specific differences, particularly within the trabecular compartment, despite comparable DXA-defined bone status. A distinct osteoimmunological biomarker profile was also observed in SSc, providing complementary information on disease-related skeletal alterations, while specific biomarker-bone associations require further confirmation.

title: Deep learning-based detection of pneumoperitoneum on computed tomography: performance and clinical feasibility.
abstract: Early detection of pneumoperitoneum on computed tomography (CT) is critical because delayed diagnosis of gastrointestinal perforation is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. We evaluated the diagnostic performance and clinical applicability of a deep learning model for automated pneumoperitoneum detection on CT. In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, CT scans for 263 patients with surgically confirmed gastrointestinal perforation and 78 normal controls from a single tertiary center (January 2010-September 2024) were included. Positive CT scans were divided into training, validation, internal test, and temporally independent external test datasets, with 78 normal controls included in the external test dataset. Free air was manually segmented and verified by surgical and radiological experts. A segmentation-based deep learning model was developed using the no-new-Segment Anything Model (nnSAM) framework and compared with a conventional no-new-Net (nnUNet) model. Segmentation and classification performance were assessed on internal and temporally independent external test datasets. In the internal test dataset (n = 43 positive cases), the nnSAM model achieved a higher detection rate (97.7% vs. 90.7%) and significantly higher mean Dice similarity coefficient (0.739 ± 0.266 vs. 0.684 ± 0.283; p = 0.045) than the nnUNet one. In the external test dataset, nnSAM also showed a higher detection rate in positive cases (97.9% vs. 85.4%) and a significantly higher mean Dice similarity coefficient (0.863 ± 0.189 vs. 0.746 ± 0.208; p = 0.003). The performance advantage of nnSAM was particularly evident in small-volume pneumoperitoneum cases. The nnSAM-based model showed improved accuracy and robustness for pneumoperitoneum detection on CT, supporting its potential as a clinically useful decision-support tool for emergency radiology workflows and triage of patients with suspected gastrointestinal perforation.

title: An interpretable contrast-enhanced CT-based cross-attention transformer model for predicting progression-free survival in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) typically have a dismal prognosis, even after undergoing radical cystectomy (RC). To address this limitation, we constructed and evaluated a preoperative deep learning (DL) model that leverages computed tomography (CT) imaging to stratify MIBC patients according to their risk of postoperative disease progression. Data from MIBC patients undergoing RC at one of four institutions were retrospectively analyzed and allocated to training and validation cohorts. A dual-channel information fusion DL model was developed to predict the postoperative risk of progression according to preoperative CT images. Subsequently, a DL-based clinical signature was created by combining clinical features with the DL-derived score. The concordance index (C-index) and area under the curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the DL model's predictive capability, which was compared with the DL-based clinical signature, a clinical model, and a Ki67 model. In the retrospective cohort of 427 patients with MIBC, the DL score demonstrated favorable predictive performance for disease progression in the validation cohort (C-index: 0.774; AUC: 0.785), and generally showed higher predictive performance than the comparator models in the validation cohort. Using an optimal threshold, the patient cohort was categorized into two distinct subgroups, high-risk and low-risk, with differences in the cumulative incidence of progression observed between the two groups, supporting the model's ability to stratify patients according to progression risk. The utilization of preoperative CT imaging in a DL framework enabled PFS prediction and risk stratification in patients with MIBC, with potential value for individualized postoperative surveillance.

title: Prediction of short-term and long-term responses to cladribine in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: a Danish nationwide real-world study.
abstract: Cladribine is regarded highly efficacious in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). However, prediction of treatment response and optimal management remain elusive, particularly during long-term. We screened the Danish Multiple Sclerosis Registry for patients with RRMS who received ≥2 5-day treatment cycles of cladribine and were followed for >90 days. Annualised relapse rates (ARR) and activity parameters (relapses or MRI activity) were analysed from 90 days after the first dose (index) to year 3 (short-term) together with time-to-first 24-week confirmed disability worsening (CDW), CDW independent of relapses (PIRA), and activity/CDW (loss of "no evidence of disease activity", NEDA-3). Kaplan-Meier log-rank tests were validated in a subgroup who completed ≥4 five-day cladribine cycles before year 3 and contributed with >3 years follow-up (3YFS). Predicting covariables included age (< /≥ 45 years), pre-baseline activity, and short-term NEDA-3 status regarding 3YFS outcomes beyond year 3 (long-term). ARR declined significantly from ~0.55 in the year pre-baseline to ~0.23-0.25 from index to year 3. Younger age and pre-baseline activity predicted more frequent short-term activity. Pre-baseline activity additionally predicted short-term NEDA-3 loss. Short-term findings were consistent in 3YFS patients. CDW and PIRA were rare during short-term (~ 10%) and long-term (~ 20%), even in older patients. However, during long-term, NEDA-3 loss resumed steadily and this was largely unpredictable. While cladribine showed sustained short-term efficacy, treatment response appeared more favourable in older patients and patients without pre-baseline activity. Rare CDW and PIRA events warrant more research in cladribine for disability prevention. Optimal long-term management following cladribine treatment requires more research.

title: Hemobezoar-related jejunojejunostomy obstruction after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a systematic review.
abstract: Hemobezoar-related jejunojejunostomy (JJ) obstruction is a rare early complication after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB). Although early small bowel obstruction after RYGB is well described, obstruction caused by hemobezoar formation remains poorly characterized. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261320591). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 2026. Eligible studies reported adults undergoing primary minimally invasive RYGB with early hemobezoar-related JJ obstruction. Data were extracted on study characteristics, presentation, diagnostic modality, operative strategy, gastric decompression, and outcomes. Given its rarity and lack of comparative cohorts, findings were summarized descriptively. Six studies met inclusion criteria, including 7669 minimally invasive RYGB procedures and 29 hemobezoar-related JJ obstructions. The crude incidence was 0.38%, with per-study incidence ranging from 0.09% to 1.94%. Presentation was consistently early, most commonly within 72 postoperative hours, frequently included tachycardia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, hematocrit decline, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Computed tomography with intravenous contrast was the predominant diagnostic modality, demonstrating dilation of the excluded stomach and proximal limbs with hyperdense intraluminal content at the JJ. Operative management evolved from laparotomy with JJ revision in earlier reports to laparoscopic clot evacuation with selective revision when anastomotic compromise, leak, ischemia, or ongoing bleeding was identified. Gastric remnant decompression was emphasized to reduce closed-loop distension and intraperitoneal contamination. No deaths were reported among 29 cases, although morbidity included abscess formation, anastomotic or staple-line complications, pancreatitis, respiratory complications, readmission, and repeat reoperation. Hemobezoar-related JJ obstruction after minimally invasive RYGB is uncommon but important. It typically presents within the first postoperative days with obstructive symptoms and evidence of intraluminal bleeding. Across retrospective studies, favorable outcomes were reported following prompt CT diagnosis, early operative exploration, remnant decompression, and minimally invasive clot evacuation with selective anastomotic revision. Prospective validation of this management approach is needed.

title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning-based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges. A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation. Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation. AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation. AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.
abstract: Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification. In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment. Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

title: The evolution of image-guided ablations for thyroid disorders: a historical review.
abstract: Over the past four decades, the management of thyroid nodules and selected thyroid malignancies has progressively shifted from surgery-centered approaches toward image-guided minimally invasive treatments (MITT). What began in 1985 with ultrasound-guided percutaneous ethanol injection evolved into a range of energy-based techniques, including laser ablation (LA), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation (MWA), and high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU).This historical review aimed to reconstruct the major milestones in the development of image-guided thyroid ablation. A systematic PubMed literature search and predefined selection criteria were used to identify seminal studies, first clinical applications, major technological innovations, comparative studies, guideline-defining publications, and landmark long-term follow-up studies. Overall, 43 milestone papers were included for qualitative historical analysis. The evolution of thyroid ablation can be divided into five phases: conceptual origins (1985-1999), birth of the thermal procedures' era (2000-2006), methodological standardization (2007-2012), oncologic consolidation and comparative evidence (2013-2018), and final codification by means of international guideline endorsement and long-term validation (2019-2025). Recent 10-year follow-up studies have confirmed the durable efficacy of MITT for benign nodule management and their sustained oncologic control in low-risk papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. Image-guided thyroid ablation has transitioned from experimental innovation to an evidence-based, guideline-supported therapeutic domain, representing a paradigm shift toward precision medicine, organ preservation, and minimally invasive endocrine oncology.

title: Utility of super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction for improving visibility of hepatocellular carcinoma at hepatic dynamic CT: comparison with hybrid iterative reconstruction and conventional deep-learning reconstruction.
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate whether Precise IQ Engine (PIQE), a super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction designed to enhance spatial resolution while reducing image noise using a deep convolutional neural network, improves the visibility of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) compared with hybrid iterative reconstruction (Adaptive Iterative Dose Reduction with three-dimensional processing [AIDR 3D]) and conventional deep-learning reconstruction (Advanced Intelligent Clear-IQ Engine [AiCE]) in hepatic dynamic CT. We evaluated 64 patients with HCC who had undergone hepatic dynamic CT. Hepatic arterial- and equilibrium phase (HAP and EP) scans were reconstructed with AIDR, AiCE, and PIQE. A radiologist measured the standard deviation of attenuation in the liver parenchyma as the image noise and calculated the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) = (ROIT - ROIL)/N in HAP and (ROIL - ROIT)/N in EP. ROIL is the mean attenuation of the liver parenchyma, ROIT the mean tumor attenuation, and N the noise. HCC visibility was assessed by 2 additional radiologists and graded with a focus on tumor margin delineation on a 5-point confidence scale. PIQE showed the lowest image noise, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). The CNR of HCCs was highest with PIQE, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). Qualitative visibility scores for HCCs were also highest with PIQE, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). PIQE significantly improves HCC visibility compared with AIDR and AiCE in hepatic dynamic CT, along with reduced image noise and increased CNR.

title: Novel Imaging Techniques Prior to Surgical Management of Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review.
abstract: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of novel imaging modalities in working up invasive bladder cancer prior to surgical management and their potential role in guiding treatment decisions. Multiple new imaging modalities, including VI-RADS and Biparametric MRI have been developed to better guide management of invasive bladder cancer. There lacks a comprehensive review of these modalities and their diagnostic performance. We performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through 2025. Studies reporting sensitivity and specificity of novel imaging for muscle invasion detection or nodal staging were included. Quality assessment used the QUADAS 2 tool. Thirty three studies encompassing 4,689 patients were included. Twenty three studies evaluated the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System for muscle invasion detection, achieving median sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 82% at a threshold of three or greater and 84% and 92%, respectively, at four or greater. Nine studies assessed positron emission tomography for nodal staging, with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrating superior sensitivity (23 to 81%) compared to conventional computed tomography (13 to 47%). Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers showed the highest sensitivity (82 to 100%) with specificity of 82 to 90%. One radiomics study achieved 73% sensitivity and 84% specificity for lymph node detection. Novel imaging modalities demonstrate promising diagnostic accuracy for bladder cancer staging. The Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System provides reliable muscle invasion assessment with threshold dependent performance. Positron emission tomography with fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers substantially improves nodal staging over conventional computed tomography. Integration of these modalities may optimize patient management, including use or omission of neoadjuvant therapy and consideration for organ sparing approaches. Prospective multicenter validation is needed.

title: Retinal Microvascular Morphometry in Recreational Athletes Using Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Illicit use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) is common among recreational athletes and is associated with cardiovascular complications and premature death. However, effects on the microvasculature have not been quantified. The retina provides non-invasive access to the systemic microvasculature, and retinal vessel morphometry has been associated with incident cardiovascular events. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 151 recreational athletes from the Fitness Doping in Denmark study: 74 active AAS users, 26 former users who had ceased AAS use at least 3 months before enrollment, and 51 age- and sex-matched controls with no lifetime AAS exposure. Disc-centered fundus photographs were analyzed using semiautomated software to obtain the arteriovenous ratio (AVR), central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE/CRVE), arteriolar and venular fractal dimensions, and arteriolar and venular tortuosity. Associations of active AAS use and cumulative lifetime AAS exposure with retinal vessel morphometry were assessed through multivariable linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and body fat percentage. Active users had a lower arteriolar fractal dimension than both controls (1.12 vs. 1.16, P < 0.05) and former users (1.12 vs. 1.18, P < 0.05), and a lower AVR than controls (0.67 vs. 0.70, P < 0.05) in multivariable models. Former users did not differ from controls on any retinal variable. Cumulative lifetime AAS exposure was not independently associated with any outcome. Active AAS use was associated with lower arteriolar fractal dimension and lower AVR after adjustment. These differences were absent in former users and unrelated to cumulative exposure duration. The cross-sectional design precludes determining the prognostic significance of these differences. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05178537.

title: Fetal Brain Volumes in Complete Vascular Ring: A Cross-Sectional MRI Study.
abstract: The association between complete vascular ring (CVR) and prenatal brain development remains poorly characterized. To compare global and regional fetal brain volumes between fetuses with CVR and controls, accounting for gestational age (GA), fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight. In this retrospective single-center study, 70 prenatally diagnosed CVR fetuses and 200 GA-matched controls with normal brain anatomy (22-37 weeks) underwent 1.5-T fetal MRI. Motion-corrected three-dimensional brain reconstructions were generated by slice-to-volume registration, and 19 regions were automatically segmented using a deep-learning pipeline. Linear regression included continuous GA, group, their interaction, fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight. Regional-to-intracranial volume ratios and sensitivity analyses incorporating maternal body mass index were evaluated. Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. At the 28-week reference age, adjusted supratentorial brain, cortical gray matter, white matter, thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular volumes were smaller in the CVR group (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted P<0.05). Intracranial volume did not differ significantly. Thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular proportions were also smaller. No group-by-GA interaction survived correction in the primary model. CVR was associated with differences in selected fetal brain volumes, including regional differences relative to intracranial volume. Larger longitudinal studies with postnatal follow-up are needed.

title: Determinants of lung cancer screening follow-up care in community care settings: A qualitative multi-case study in the ACCELL trial.
abstract: Adherence to lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up is essential to achieve mortality benefits from screening. However, population-based studies demonstrate follow-up is <50% in clinical settings. Determinants (barriers and facilitators) of LCS follow-up in community settings are under-studied. What are determinants of LCS follow-up in community settings? This qualitative multi-case study informed a pre-post intervention trial, testing pragmatic interventions to address LCS follow-up in community settings. We conducted rapid ethnographic assessments (REA) through virtual and in person site visits of LCS delivery in three community-based healthcare systems in Washington state. Additionally at the two future intervention sites, we conducted provider and patient interviews. Interview transcripts were analyzed using Rapid Group Analysis Process. All data were triangulated according to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities Research Framework domains. Twenty-eight organizational leaders, providers, and staff participated in REA. Thirty-one patients and 15 providers from the future intervention sites participated in interviews. Determinants of LCS follow-up in the intervention domain included role of primary care, LCS complexity and care process standardization. In the inner setting domain (organization and clinic), screening prioritization, EHR use, radiology support, and context of wellness visits affected LCS. The main theme in the outer setting domain was the influence of social determinants of health on LCS. In the individuals domain, shared beliefs in LCS and LCS education and information sharing were key. In the process implementation domain, clinical champions and use of data and metrics were crucial. Integrated findings suggest determinants related to LCS complexity, care fragmentation, socioeconomic status and language, and limitations of PCPs could be overcome through more centralized approaches. However, increased use of EHR tools, increased education and standardizing LCS performance metrics may enable follow-up in decentralized settings. NCT06324110.

title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.
abstract: Background High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information. Case summary A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal. Discussion This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque. Take-home message PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.

title: Mapping International Lung Cancer Screening Quality Indicators to the American College of Radiology Lung Cancer Screening Registry: A Crosswalk Analysis.
abstract: The International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) established 26 consensus quality indicators (QIs) for lung cancer screening (LCS) programs, of which 20 were rated as essential and 6 as desirable by the expert panel. We evaluated the extent to which the American College of Radiology (ACR) Lung Cancer Screening Registry (LCSR), the largest LCS registry in the U.S., can support measurement of the IASLC QIs. We performed a crosswalk analysis, mapping all 26 IASLC QIs to the LCSR Data Dictionary and its 46 clinical performance measures, classifying each as directly measurable, derivable, or not measurable. The crosswalk was reviewed and independently validated by members of the ACR Early Lung Cancer Detection Registry Quality and Education Committee. Eight QIs (30.8%) were directly measurable, 10 (38.5%) were derivable, and 8 (30.8%) were not measurable from LCSR data alone. The LCSR therefore contains sufficient data elements to support measurement of approximately 69% of IASLC QIs. Remaining gaps involve screening uptake, clinical investigation, procedure complications, curative-intent treatment, treatment equity, diagnostic investigation equity and selected wait-time measures and would require additional registry fields or external data linkage.

title: LungCheck: Pilot Testing a Theory-Informed Multicomponent Strategy to Increase Lung Cancer Screening in Primary Care Settings.
abstract: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific and all-cause mortality, yet uptake remains low. This study evaluates LungCheck, a theory-informed multicomponent behavior change and implementation strategy designed to increase LDCT ordering in two diverse primary care settings. This pilot study compared 16-month pilot and pre-pilot periods at a federally qualified health center (FQHC) and an academic faculty practice in New York City. LungCheck comprised educational meetings, materials and clinician reminders, an implementation blueprint, patient navigation, and EHR modifications. LDCT ordering rates (primary outcome) were compared using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Post-implementation surveys assessed acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. A total of 5,918 patient-period observations were included (1,569 academic; 4,349 FQHC). Among patients with documented LCS eligibility, the odds of LDCT ordering were significantly higher during the pilot at both the academic practice (OR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.47-4.85; p=0.001) and FQHC (OR, 4.53; 95% CI, 2.29-8.94; p<0.001). A combined-site multivariable model adjusting for site, age, sex, and race confirmed higher odds of LDCT ordering during the pilot (OR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.44-2.63; p<0.001). Among patients with an LDCT order, completion was 71.4% (10/14) pre-pilot versus 35.7% (15/42) during the pilot at the academic practice and 42.9% (18/42; 95% CI, 28%-59%) versus 39.3% (24/61; 95% CI, 27%-53%) at the FQHC. The strategy was rated as highly acceptable (AIM, 4.47/5), appropriate (IAM, 4.44/5), and feasible (FIM, 4.41/5). LungCheck was associated with significantly increased LDCT ordering at both sites, high acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness ratings and high provider knowledge, confidence, and perceived skills related to LCS. Although a corresponding improvement in LDCT completion was not observed, the small number of LDCT orders limited the precision of completion estimates. Persistent environmental and patient-level barriers underscore the need to adapt LungCheck into a multilevel intervention addressing patient-, provider, and system-level barriers across the LCS continuum, to be evaluated in a future cluster randomized trial.

title: Patient-specific pharmacokinetics of intratumoral cisplatin track pathologic necrosis in early-stage lung cancer.
abstract: Intratumoral injection of cisplatin into lung cancer is feasible and can increase local drug exposure while reducing systemic toxicity. However, its success relies on achieving sufficient drug exposure to the tumor, which has not been quantitatively evaluated in a clinical setting. In the context of a Phase I clinical trial of intratumoral cisplatin injections into resectable lung tumors via robotic bronchoscopy (N = 6), we developed a quantitative framework to assess delivery effectiveness and long-term cisplatin exposure in tumors. Initial injectate retention was estimated using a novel image analytics pipeline based on intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography scans, by assuming that emerging high-attenuation regions are due to injectate deposition. Long-term drug exposure was estimated using a novel pharmacokinetic model tailored for intratumoral drug delivery and informed by sequential venous blood draws following the injections. The area under the platinum concentration curve in the tumor compartment at t = 3-21 h and platinum concentration in the tumor compartment (t = 3-6 h), estimated from the fitted pharmacokinetic model, showed a strong monotonic association with percentage pathological necrosis assessed post-resection by three independent, blinded pathologists (Spearman's ρ = 0.93, 95% bootstrap CI 0.67-1.00, unadjusted exact p = 0.033), which was not statistically significant when corrected for multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.17). No other pharmacokinetic variable correlated was significantly correlated with necrosis or other pathological response metrics prior to multiple comparison correction. This result aligns with the known time-concentration dependency of cisplatin action in tumor. Further studies will be needed to evaluate this observation for repeatability and clinical relevance. Our approach provides a framework for estimating intratumoral drug exposure in clinical settings, which may help with the interpretation of clinical trial outcomes and future evaluation of injection strategies.

Our approach provides a framework for estimating intratumoral drug exposure in clinical settings, which may help with the interpretation of clinical trial outcomes and future evaluation of injection strategies.

title: Network pharmacology-guided investigation of the anti-angiogenic mechanisms of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stem in rheumatoid arthritis.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a severe systemic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint destruction. Spatholobi Caulis (SC), derived from the vine stem of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn, has a long history of clinical application in traditional Chinese medicine for activating blood circulation and relieving rheumatic arthralgia. However, its pharmacological material basis and anti-angiogenic mechanisms for treating RA remain insufficiently elucidated. To systematically investigate the active constituents of SC and elucidate its anti-angiogenic mechanisms in RA using an integrated approach combining chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and in vivo experimental validation. The chemical profile of SC was characterized using HPLC-QE-MS. A network pharmacology approach-incorporating target screening, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and GO/KEGG enrichment-was utilized to predict core targets and pathways. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate the binding stability between key active compounds and hub targets. Finally, the anti-arthritic and anti-angiogenic effects were validated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using micro-CT, H&E, immunohistochemistry (CD31), ELISA, and Western blot analysis. Additionally, to directly verify the predicted interactions, the effects of the core compound 7,3',4'-trihydroxyisoflavone (THIF) on TNF-α-induced MH7A cells were assessed. Cell proliferation, VEGF secretion, migration, and protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB were evaluated after 24 h treatment with THIF. HPLC-QE-MS identified 24 active ingredients in SC. Network analysis identified key hub targets including SRC, PIK3CB, AKT1, EGFR, and ESR1 and revealed that SC predominantly modulates the PI3K/AKT, HIF-1α, and VEGF signaling pathways. Molecular docking, MD simulations and SPR demonstrated strong binding affinities and high structural stability between core compounds (e.g., THIF, Hesperetin, Afzelechin, (-)-Maackiain) and key hub targets (e.g., PIK3CB, EGFR, ESR1). In vivo, SC administration significantly alleviated joint swelling, preserved bone morphology (increased BV/TV and BMD via micro-CT), and reduced the organ indices of the thymus and spleen. Crucially, SC remarkably suppressed synovial neovascularization (decreased CD31-positive vessels), downregulated systemic inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, VEGF, TGF-α), and significantly inhibited the protein expression of SRC, STAT3, EGFR, PI3K, AKT, and HIF-1α in synovial tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SC effectively inhibits the proliferation of MH7A cells. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that SC significantly induces apoptosis in MH7A cells; However, this pro-apoptotic effect was alleviated upon addition of the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Further in vitro validation with the pure compound THIF showed that it dose-dependently suppressed TNF-α-induced MH7A cell proliferation, reduced VEGF secretion from 292.18 to 80.32 pg/mL, and inhibited cell migration. Western blot analysis confirmed that THIF significantly downregulated the protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB in a dose-dependent manner, directly validating the SPR binding results and demonstrating targeted inhibition of the downstream pathological signaling pathways associated with RA. SC effectively ameliorates RA progression by mitigating synovial inflammation and preventing structural joint damage. Its therapeutic efficacy is primarily driven by the suppression of pathological angiogenesis via the targeted dual-inhibition of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α signaling axes.

title: Procedure-Specific Cranial Base Responses After Surgically Assisted Rapid Palatal Expansion and Le Fort I Osteotomy.
abstract: The biological effects of maxillary surgery may extend beyond the operative site to involve the posterior cranial base. Although biomechanical studies have suggested force transmission to the spheno-occipital synchondrosis (SOS), procedure-specific cranial base responses have not previously been quantitatively evaluated using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based radiomics. To compare postoperative cranial base responses following surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion (SARPE) and Le Fort I osteotomy by quantitatively evaluating the SOS using CBCT-based radiomics. This retrospective observational study included 25 skeletally mature patients treated with either SARPE (n = 12) or Le Fort I osteotomy (n = 13). Preoperative and three-month postoperative CBCT scans were analyzed. The SOS was manually segmented using a standardized anatomical reference framework, and 107 radiomic features were extracted according to Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative recommendations. Within-group and between-group comparisons were performed using non-parametric tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Selected radiomic features were further analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Radiographic SOS separation rates were comparable between the SARPE and Le Fort I groups (p > 0.05). Following false discovery rate correction, 43 radiomic features demonstrated significant postoperative alterations in the SARPE group, whereas four features showed nominally significant changes after Le Fort I osteotomy (p < 0.05), none of which remained significant after FDR correction. Nominal between-group comparisons identified four features with p < 0.05, but none remained significant after FDR correction. Linear mixed-effects analysis identified a significant Group × Time interaction for GLSZM Large Area Low Gray Level Emphasis (FDR-adjusted p = 0.024), supporting a procedure-specific longitudinal response. Heatmap and volcano plot analyses demonstrated a broader distribution of postoperative imaging-derived changes following SARPE than after Le Fort I osteotomy. SARPE and Le Fort I osteotomy produced distinct postoperative responses within the spheno-occipital synchondrosis, suggesting that cranial base adaptation varies according to the surgical procedure. The broader radiomic response observed following SARPE is consistent with the hypothesis that preservation of the pterygomaxillary connection may permit greater force transmission to the posterior cranial base. CBCT-based radiomics may provide a sensitive quantitative method for characterizing procedure-specific cranial base responses.

title: Synchronous Percutaneous Biopsy and Cryoablation for Suspicious Solitary Pulmonary Nodules.
abstract: To evaluate the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and safety of synchronous CT-guided core needle biopsy and cryoablation for highly suspicious 1-2 cm pulmonary nodules MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 102 consecutive patients undergoing synchronous CT-guided core needle biopsy and cryoablation between August 2020 and October 2025. Treatment was undertaken on the basis of clinical and imaging suspicion before final histopathologic diagnosis. A cryoprobe was placed before biopsy to provide an intraprocedural landmark. Technical success, diagnostic yield, and adverse events were evaluated in all 102 patients; local tumor progression and overall survival were evaluated separately in 81 patients with pathology-confirmed NSCLC. Cryoablation technical success was 100% (102/102), and concurrent biopsy diagnostic yield was 87.3% (89/102). Biopsy identified 86 malignant diagnoses, including 81 NSCLCs. Mean nodule diameter was 1.52 ± 0.30 cm. Median follow-up in the NSCLC cohort was 34.5 months (IQR, 18.4-49.4 months). The cumulative incidence of recorded local tumor progression was 8.8% at both 1 and 3 years, and overall survival was 100% and 90.8%, respectively. Pneumothorax requiring chest tube drainage occurred in 20.6% (21/102), and no procedure-related deaths were reported. The synchronous biopsy and cryoablation approach was technically feasible and provided a specific histopathologic diagnosis in 87.3% of selected patients with highly suspicious 1.0-2.0-cm pulmonary nodules. Among patients with pathology-confirmed NSCLC, local-control outcomes were within the range reported in similar cryoablation-only series.

title: Brain volume analysis-guided basic research in psychiatry.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetric analysis is among the few tools able to probe the living human brain, offering a route from clinical findings back to basic neuroscience. Here we propose a reverse-translational framework for psychiatric research that links human MRI findings to their underlying molecular mechanisms in model animals. The framework rests on three "liaisons": a species liaison, confirming that a volume change identified in humans is also observed in mice using the same imaging and analytical method; a scale liaison, in which a histological pipeline explains the macroscopic volume change in terms of cell number and cell volume; and a causal liaison, in which molecular or cell-biological intervention converts correlative histological findings into causal evidence by inducing or reversing the volume change. We further propose that unbiased, whole-brain MRI volumetric analysis in mice can serve as an exploratory region-screening method, identifying disease- or treatment-related regions without a predefined region of interest, and capturing the maintained structural outcome of an intervention rather than its immediate functional trace. Together, the three-liaison framework and the region-screening approach outline a general strategy by which MRI-guided reverse and forward translation can uncover the structural and molecular basis of psychiatric diseases and their treatments.
