title: Two-Year Outcomes of the XXX Trial: Longitudinal Analysis of Safety, PSA Kinetics, and Patient-Reported Outcomes.
abstract: To assess the 2-year incidence and longitudinal trajectory of grade (G) ≥2 genitourinary (GU) and gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events (AEs) following single-dose ablative radiotherapy (SDRT) for organ-confined prostate cancer (PCa), alongside associated changes in patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and PSA kinetics. XXX (XXX) is a single-institution prospective study enrolling patients with unfavorable intermediate-risk or selected high-risk organ-confined PCa treated with SDRT delivering 24 Gy in one fraction to the prostate and seminal vesicles. Treatment incorporated urethra-sparing and intrafraction motion control and was delivered on a linear accelerator using a 10-MV flattening filter-free single partial arc in combination with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). AEs were graded using CTCAE v5.0. PSA and testosterone were monitored longitudinally, and scheduled multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) were performed to assess radiological response. PROs were assessed using EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-PR25, IPSS, and IIEF questionnaires. Mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal trajectories and associations with baseline and dosimetric factors. Thirty patients were treated. At 2 years, no ≥G3 AEs were observed. Cumulative G2 GU and GI AEs were 23% and 7%, respectively. Two years point prevalent G2 GU and GI AEs were 10% and 3%, respectively. Longitudinal analysis showed an overall stable safety profile, with higher baseline IPSS and bladder trigone D1cc significantly associated with higher GU AEs. PRO analyses demonstrated statistically significant changes in urinary domains, although effect sizes remained below minimal important difference thresholds, indicating no clinically meaningful deterioration. Baseline symptom burden strongly predicted long-term PROs trajectories. Biochemical relapse-free survival was 100% at 2 years, with a consistent and significant PSA decline over time and local radiological control confirmed by mpMRI. Testosterone recovery occurred in 76% of patients receiving ADT. Single-fraction 24 Gy SDRT combined with ADT was feasible and well tolerated, with low rates of ≥G2 AEs and largely maintained quality of life at 2 years in patients with unfavorable localized prostate cancer. Early oncologic outcomes are encouraging but require confirmation with longer follow-up and comparative validation.

title: Streamlining Liver SABR: Validation and Initial Experience of Bulk Density Override Based Single-Session, Simulation-Free Adaptive Workflow.
abstract: Conventional liver stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) typically requires a CT simulation visit followed by multiple treatment fractions, which can increase patient burden and limit access. We propose an approach that consolidates imaging, planning, adaptation, and delivery into one session, utilizing an MR-guided adaptive workflow. We report here the workflow and dosimetric validation of a streamlined bulk density override (BDO) strategy and the initial clinical implementation of this simulation-free approach. A single-institution phase II trial was designed to deliver liver SABR (30-40 Gy in 1 fraction) in a single-session using an MR-guided Linac for patients with liver cancers using BDO strategy. To validate dosimetric accuracy, 17 previously treated single-fraction liver SABR plans were recalculated retrospectively using (1) CT-based electron density and (2) BDO-based density. DVH endpoints and 3D gamma analysis (1%/1mm) were compared. Early clinical experience from the first five trial patients is reported, including dose comparisons between BDO-based calculations and diagnostic CT-based calculations. For the retrospective analysis, BDO-based calculation closely matched the CT-based calculation. For the PTV and GTV, the median percent differences were close to zero for all evaluated metrics and the maximum percent differences were all within 2%. For organ-at-risk (OAR) endpoints (chest wall, bowel, liver minus GTV, spinal cord), mean and maximum dose differences were within 0.1 Gy and 0.6 Gy, respectively. The average 3D gamma pass rate was 99.2%. For the first 5 patients treated on trial, BDO- and diagnostic CT-based reference plan metrics agreed within 1.5% for PTV coverage and within 0.5 Gy for key OAR endpoints. The mean gamma pass rate was 98.8%. The BDO strategy provides dosimetric agreement comparable to CT-based calculation and supports an efficient and patient-centric single-visit delivery model. Our results support further investigation of simulation-free, single-session MR-guided adaptive liver SABR.

title: Humanity in the loop: Reframing artificial intelligence and the global medical imaging divide.
abstract: Access to radiology and nuclear medicine remains profoundly unequal across global health systems. Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face persistent shortages in imaging equipment, specialist workforce, digital infrastructure, maintenance, regulation and sustainable financing. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned as a mechanism to improve imaging access, but it may also reinforce existing inequities. This narrative review examines the potential for discriminative, generative and agentic AI to reduce or widen inequities in LMIC medical imaging and proposes a sociotechnical governance framework based on the concept of Humanity-in-the-Loop. Discriminative AI may improve image interpretation, triage, segmentation, quantification and image-quality assessment; generative AI may enhance reporting, education, translation, communication, synthetic data generation and research workflows; and agentic AI may coordinate referrals, scheduling, follow-up, supply logistics and imaging pathways. They may also exacerbate inequity through data colonialism, algorithmic under-performance, dataset shift, infrastructure dependence, commercial lock-in, second-tier automation, liability transfer and unequal participation in AI research and development. Human-in-the-loop governance is insufficient for equitable AI implementation in LMIC medical imaging because the assumptions underpinning effective human oversight are often absent in resource-constrained settings. The proposed Humanity-in-the-Loop sociotechnical framework embeds equity, local agency, contextual validity and public benefit throughout the AI lifecycle. The framework comprises six interconnected domains: patient humanity, workforce humanity, community humanity, data humanity, system humanity and global humanity. Responsible implementation of AI in medical imaging requires governance frameworks that extend beyond algorithm performance to include workforce development, data sovereignty, infrastructure, community priorities, equitable partnerships and sustainable capacity building. Adoption of a Humanity-in-the-Loop approach may help ensure that AI narrows rather than widens the medical imaging divide between high-income countries and LMICs.

title: Artificial intelligence, disclosure and consent: a comparative review of Australian and European Union legal frameworks for medical imaging.
abstract: To conduct a comparative narrative review of Australian and European approaches to transparency, disclosure, and informed consent in AI-assisted medical imaging, with attention to patient autonomy, professional responsibilities, and regulatory oversight. AI systems are increasingly integrated into medical imaging workflows and offer significant benefits in diagnostic speed, efficiency, and accuracy. However, the reviewed literature highlights substantial concerns relating to transparency, algorithmic bias, automation bias, informed consent, and accountability. Compared with Australia, the European Union has more explicit statutory requirements for transparency, information provided to AI deployers, human oversight, and the governance of high-risk AI systems. Australian regulation remains distributed across privacy law, medical device regulation, common law, state consent legislation, and professional guidance. Current regulatory approaches to AI-assisted medical imaging remain inconsistent internationally. European legislation currently represents a stronger and more comprehensive model for disclosure and transparency obligations compared to Australia's developing framework. Ongoing legal reform, interdisciplinary collaboration, and responsive governance structures will be necessary to address the rapid advancement and increasing integration of AI systems within healthcare. Disclosure should be proportionate to the role, autonomy, risk, and clinical significance of the AI system. Where AI materially affects an examination or diagnostic decision, patients should receive clear information about its involvement, the extent of human oversight, material risks and limitations, how their data may be used, and any reasonably available alternatives. Radiographers and radiologists require appropriate AI literacy and clear local governance to support consistent communication, professional judgement, and accountability.

title: From contouring variability to dosimetric impact: a comprehensive assessment of online adaptive MR-guided SBRT for pancreatic cancer.
abstract: To quantify inter-physician contouring variability and evaluate its dosimetric impact in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients treated with daily online adaptive MR-guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MRgSBRT), to assess safety and clinical robustness of online contouring. Fifty treatment sessions from ten PDAC patients treated with 50 Gy in five fractions on a 1.5 T MR-Linac were retrospectively analyzed. During each treatment session ("online"), targets and organs-at-risk (OARs) within 3 cm of the tumor were delineated by seven physicians working on the MR-Linac. All structures were re-contoured offline by a single pancreatic-expert radiation oncologist ("reference"). Geometric agreement was assessed using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Mean Distance to Agreement (MDA), and 95 % Hausdorff Distance (HD95). Dosimetric analyses were performed on delivered treatment plans using both online and reference contours, with evaluation based on fraction-wise worst-case dose metrics. High geometric concordance was observed for stomach and duodenum, whereas smaller or anatomically complex structures (GTV, major vessels, bile duct) showed greater variability. Online GTVs were larger than reference contours. Despite these differences, target coverage (V50Gy and V35Gy) was maintained with online contours. While occasional per-fraction gastrointestinal (GI) dose constraint exceedances were identified using reference contours, fraction-wise worst-case analysis showed GI doses remained within clinical tolerance for nearly all patients. Daily online adaptive MRgSBRT for PDAC provides robust target coverage and clinically acceptable OAR sparing, despite contouring variability. Multi-physician online contouring appears safe in clinical practice, although further improvements may be achieved through standardized contouring guidelines and harmonization strategies.

title: Adult aphasic status epilepticus: A systematic review and patient-level synthesis of clinical phenotypes and multimodal diagnostic evidence.
abstract: Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is an uncommon manifestation of focal status epilepticus in which aphasia is the sole or predominant clinical feature. Recognition may be difficult because consciousness can be relatively preserved, convulsive activity may be absent, and the presentation can mimic acute stroke. To characterize diagnostic phenotypes of adult ASE and synthesize clinical, electrographic, and neuroimaging features across published cases. We conducted a systematic review and patient-level synthesis of adult ASE cases. Eligible patients were adjudicated as definite or probable ASE using prespecified criteria. Clinical phenotype, electroencephalographic (EEG) findings, neuroimaging, initial diagnostic impressions, treatment, and language outcomes were extracted. Ninety-nine publications contributed 168 adults with ASE, including 89 definite and 79 probable cases. Aphasia was the sole manifestation in 42.9% and predominant in 57.1%, while consciousness was preserved in 78.0%. Ictal EEG activity or electrographic status epilepticus was documented in 53.0%, and 41.7% had supportive epileptiform abnormalities. Among cases with interpretable EEG laterality, 92.7% were left-lateralized. Peri-ictal MRI abnormalities occurred in 41.2% of performed interpretable studies. Among 55 patients with interpretable functional perfusion or metabolic imaging, hyperperfusion was reported in 32. FDG-PET hypermetabolism was treated as a distinct metabolic finding. Stroke or transient ischemic attack was the most frequent reported initial impression (44.2%). Complete language recovery was reported in 77.4% of evaluable patients. Published adult ASE cases show a heterogeneous phenotype in which recognition commonly rests on concordance between language disturbance and focal EEG abnormalities, with peri-ictal imaging providing complementary evidence. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy of individual features or multimodal combinations.

title: A multidimensional integrated diagnostic strategy using needle sheath flushing solution: combining PGM-based GPC3 protein detection and gene methylation analysis for improved liver cancer diagnosis.
abstract: Background liver cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide, with many patients diagnosed at advanced stages due to limitations in current diagnostic methods. Morphological pathological diagnosis of liver biopsy samples often suffers from insufficient sensitivity, particularly in distinguishing malignant lesions from benign conditions with atypical cellular changes. There is a critical need for objective, precise biomarker detection methods to supplement traditional pathology and reduce missed diagnosis rates. Methods this study developed and validated a novel multidimensional diagnostic approach utilizing needle sheath flushing solution (NSF) obtained after ultrasound-guided liver puncture. We established a personal glucose meter (PGM)-based Glypican-3 (GPC3) protein detection system using carboxylated magnetic nanomaterials. Simultaneously, Septin9 and RASSF1A gene methylation was analyzed in shed cells from the same NSF samples. Detection thresholds were determined through stratified randomization and ROC curve analysis. The diagnostic performance of individual and combined methods was evaluated against final clinical diagnosis as the gold standard. Results a total of 312 patients were enrolled, comprising 185 tumor cases and 127 benign disease controls. The PGM-based GPC3 detection achieved 83.2% sensitivity and 81.1% specificity (AUC = 0.8217). Septin9 and RASSF1A methylation analysis yielded sensitivities of 72.4% and 47.0%, respectively, with combined methylation detection reaching 81.1% sensitivity and 87.4% specificity (AUC = 0.8424). The integrated strategy combining GPC3, gene methylation, and morphological pathology outperformed all single methods, achieving an AUC of 0.8846, 93.0% sensitivity, and 91.7% negative predictive value. For 68 patients with indeterminate atypical cell pathology, GPC3 and/or methylation positivity was associated with 2.82-fold higher risk of malignancy ( P < 0.05). Conclusions this study demonstrates that NSF-based multidimensional analysis integrating PGM-based GPC3 protein detection and Septin9/RASSF1A methylation profiling provides substantial complementary diagnostic value to conventional pathology. The combined approach reduces missed diagnosis rates and offers objective risk stratification for patients with equivocal histological findings, presenting a promising strategy for precision diagnosis of liver cancer.

a total of 312 patients were enrolled, comprising 185 tumor cases and 127 benign disease controls. The PGM-based GPC3 detection achieved 83.2% sensitivity and 81.1% specificity (AUC = 0.8217). Septin9 and RASSF1A methylation analysis yielded sensitivities of 72.4% and 47.0%, respectively, with combined methylation detection reaching 81.1% sensitivity and 87.4% specificity (AUC = 0.8424). The integrated strategy combining GPC3, gene methylation, and morphological pathology outperformed all single methods, achieving an AUC of 0.8846, 93.0% sensitivity, and 91.7% negative predictive value. For 68 patients with indeterminate atypical cell pathology, GPC3 and/or methylation positivity was associated with 2.82-fold higher risk of malignancy (P < 0.05).

Conclusions

this study demonstrates that NSF-based multidimensional analysis integrating PGM-based GPC3 protein detection and Septin9/RASSF1A methylation profiling provides substantial complementary diagnostic value to conventional pathology. The combined approach reduces missed diagnosis rates and offers objective risk stratification for patients with equivocal histological findings, presenting a promising strategy for precision diagnosis of liver cancer.

title: Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management.
abstract: Mesenteric venous thrombosis (MVT) is a rare but clinically important cause of mesenteric ischemia. It most often affects the superior mesenteric vein and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Nonspecific symptoms often delay diagnosis. Severe disease courses may occur in the presence of intestinal infarction. The aim of this article is to provide a structured overview of the etiopathogenesis, imaging findings, and interventional radiological treatment options for MVT. Narrative, literature-based review taking into consideration current guidelines, radiological imaging protocols, and endovascular techniques. The pathogenesis of MVT can be classified according to Virchow's triad, including hypercoagulability, stasis, and endothelial injury. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the method of choice for diagnosis. It demonstrates thrombosis as a contrast filling defect within the portomesenteric venous system and allows assessment of bowel viability. Important CT findings include bowel wall thickening, mesenteric edema, ascites, and the halo or target sign. Pneumatosis intestinalis and portomesenteric venous gas suggest transmural ischemia and indicate the need for immediate surgical management. Systemic anticoagulation is the cornerstone of treatment. Mechanical thrombectomy, local thrombolysis, stent angioplasty, and, where appropriate, TIPS placement may be considered in complex or prolonged clinical courses. Early interdisciplinary, imaging-guided management is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning. CT guides further management by detecting thrombosis and assessing bowel viability. Interventional radiological recanalization is not a first-line treatment, but it may represent an important escalation strategy in selected patients. · Mesenteric venous thrombosis is an uncommon but clinically relevant cause of mesenteric ischemia.. · Early interdisciplinary diagnostic work-up is essential to prevent irreversible intestinal ischemic injury.. · Contrast-enhanced CT represents the key imaging modality, enabling both detection of venous thrombosis and assessment of bowel viability.. · In the absence of contraindications, systemic anticoagulation constitutes the cornerstone of treatment.. · Surgical management is indicated in the presence of suspected transmural bowel necrosis or clinical signs of peritonitis.. · Interventional radiological recanalization techniques may be considered as an escalation strategy in selected patients.. · Camp LC, Weber M, Arndt H. Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2965-8425.

title: Non-invasive neuromodulation after repetitive head impacts: current evidence and a precision framework for circuit-based rehabilitation.
abstract: Repetitive head impacts (RHIs) are associated with heterogeneous cognitive, behavioral, psychiatric, sleep-related, pain, and neurological symptoms. Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) remains a postmortem neuropathological diagnosis, whereas traumatic encephalopathy syndrome (TES) is a clinical research syndrome assessed during life. No intervention has been shown to modify CTE pathology, but neuromodulation may support the surviving neural circuits. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from database inception to August 2026 for this narrative review. The author evaluates magnetic and electrical stimulation, low-intensity ultrasound, photobiomodulation and cranial nerve stimulation as adjuncts to rehabilitation after repetitive head impacts. Direct RHI/TES evidence is distinguished from findings in other traumatic brain injury and concussion populations, other clinical populations and experimental models. The author then proposes a phenotype- and circuit-guided framework for treatment development. Neuromodulation should not be considered a disease-modifying treatment for CTE. Its most credible role is as a phenotype-led adjunct to rehabilitation. This approach requires identification of a viable circuit relevant to the dominant impairment, selection of an individualized stimulation dose, measurement of target engagement and pairing with symptom-relevant rehabilitation. Progress requires credible sham-controlled and factorial trials, multimodal biomarkers, clinically meaningful functional outcomes, and long-term follow-up.

title: From metastatic disease to no evidence of disease after conversion liver surgery in advanced gastric cancer with liver metastases: A case report.
abstract: Stage IV gastric cancer with liver metastases has a poor prognosis. Conversion surgery may enable long-term disease control in selected patients, but pathological complete response is rare and is usually defined only for surgically resected specimens. Here, a 54-year-old female with initially unresectable, HER2-negative, pMMR-by-IHC, EBER-positive gastric cancer and synchronous liver metastases received first-line XELOX plus tislelizumab for 4 cycles. Because of suspected oxaliplatin hypersensitivity, treatment was changed to cisplatin plus capecitabine plus tislelizumab for 3 cycles. After subsequent suspected platinum hypersensitivity, treatment was changed to capecitabine plus tislelizumab for 7 cycles. After 14 cycles, repeat endoscopic biopsy showed no tumor cells. Imaging showed significant regression of liver lesions. After multidisciplinary discussion, the patient underwent conversion liver surgery comprising resection of selected liver lesions and radiofrequency ablation of other liver lesions. R0 status was confirmed only for the resected liver specimens; ablated lesions had no pathological specimen. Histopathological examination of the resected liver specimens showed no residual viable tumor cells, consistent with pathological complete response in the resected liver lesions. The gastric primary was assessed as clinical complete response by endoscopy and biopsy. At last follow-up 1 month after surgery, imaging showed no evidence of disease; long-term outcome remains unknown. This case illustrates that selected patients with advanced gastric cancer and liver metastases may achieve a strong response to tislelizumab-based immunochemotherapy and liver-directed conversion treatment. However, the long-term benefit, the role of omitting gastrectomy, and the significance of FAPI/FDG discordance remain uncertain.

title: Spot-wise compensation of proton beam deflection and radiation field deformation in the transverse magnetic field of an in-beam MR scanner using a research version of a commercial treatment planning system.
abstract: Objective Magnetic resonance-integrated proton therapy (MRiPT) offers the potential for high-precision, image-guided particle therapy but is challenged by magnetic field (MF)-induced proton beam deflection and radiation field deformation. Unless compensated for, these effects compromise dose conformity and prohibit clinical implementation. This work aims to develop and experimentally validate a spot-wise compensation method capable of restoring proton dose distributions in the presence of a measured 3D magnetic vector field map within a clinical treatment planning system (TPS). Approach A spot-wise compensation framework was implemented in a research version of RayStation, a TPS commercially available for clinical use. The method compensates both lateral beam deflection and MF-induced radiation field deformation by shifting individual pencil-beam spots based on displacement vectors derived from dose calculations in water phantoms using the measured MF of an in-beam MR scanner integrated with a horizontal proton beamline. Two complementary strategies were implemented: a patient-specific approach based on plan-specific displacement calculations, and a generic approach using precomputed displacement maps derived from a reference phantom. Compensation performance was evaluated in representative clinical cases. Dose distributions were experimentally validated using 2D ionisation chamber array measurements. Main Results Both compensation methods effectively restored target coverage, dose homogeneity, and organ-at-risk sparing to the level of no-MF reference plans. The patient-specific method generally achieved a higher performance, whereas the generic compensation method enabled rapid automated correction with sufficient accuracy for clinical workflows involving deep-seated tumours. Local γ-analysis demonstrated excellent agreement between measured and calculated doses, with pass rates exceeding 98.5% for 3%/3 mm criteria. Significance This work demonstrates that compensation of MF-induced proton beam deflection and field deformation can be achieved entirely within a research version of the RayStation TPS using measured, MR scanner-specific MF data. The proposed method provides a scalable, robust framework for future MRiPT clinical applications.&#xD.

title: CT protocol optimization for oncologic surveillance imaging: phantom-based comparison of multi-scan and single-scan acquisition strategies.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) plays an important role in oncologic surveillance after treatment of gynecological malignancies, including patients treated with vaginal electronic brachytherapy. This phantom study evaluated CT acquisition strategies for oncologic surveillance, focusing on radiation dose reduction and objective image quality in the cranial, thoracic, and upper abdominal regions assessed quantitatively. CT acquisition protocols were investigated using an anthropomorphic Kyoto Kagaku phantom. Two acquisition strategies were analyzed: a multi-scan approach with separate acquisitions for the head, neck, thorax, and abdomen-pelvis, and a single-scan head-torso acquisition with region-specific reconstructions. Different exposure parameter settings and reconstruction kernels were evaluated. Objective image quality was assessed using semi-automated region-of-interest measurements with a custom FIJI/ImageJ macro. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and Artifact Index (AI) were calculated for cranial, thoracic, and abdominal regions. For the single-scan protocols, CTDIvol decreased from 4.21 mGy in the standard protocol to 2.97-3.99 mGy in the optimized protocols, while DLP decreased from 410 mGy.cm to 287-388 mGy.cm. Across all anatomical regions, SNR and CNR remained comparable with the standard protocol. Thoracic CNR ranged from 2.68 to 3.01, abdominal CNR remained stable in both liver and aortic regions, and AI demonstrated only moderate variability across the optimized protocols. Optimized CT acquisition protocols reduced radiation dose while preserving the evaluated objective image quality metrics in the cranial, thoracic, and upper abdominal regions. Among the evaluated configurations, a reduced dose single scan head-torso acquisition using reduced tube voltage and tube current modulation showed a favorable balance between radiation dose reduction and objective image quality under the investigated phantom conditions and was identified as a candidate protocol for subsequent clinical and reader performance validation.

title: High-Frequency Enhancement and Dual-Model Ensemble for Language-Guided COVID-19 Pneumonia Lesion Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of COVID-19 pneumonia lesions in chest X-ray (CXR) images is critical for disease quantification and clinical decision-making. However, existing methods suffer from blurred lesion boundaries, missed detection of tiny lesions, and limited generalization performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a language-guided multimodal medical image segmentation method integrating high-frequency enhancement and a dual-model ensemble. The method is developed along three dimensions: frequency-domain detail enhancement, spatial alignment optimization, and dual-model ensemble. First, a frequency-domain decomposition-based high-frequency enhancement module is designed to mitigate detail attenuation caused by encoder downsampling. Second, a two-dimensional (2D) spatial position encoding module is introduced to improve the spatial alignment between text descriptions and visual regions. Third, a dual-model ensemble architecture with differentiated frequency-domain masks is constructed to address the performance ceiling of individual models. Finally, experiments on two public datasets with different imaging modalities and data characteristics demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing single-modal and multimodal baseline methods and achieves competitive performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches, verifying the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. On the QaTa-COV19 dataset, the Dice coefficient reaches 91.85% and the mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) reaches 84.98%. On the multi-institutional MosMedData+ dataset, the Dice coefficient reaches 78.48% and the mIoU reaches 64.66%. The proposed method provides effective technical support for clinical diagnosis and follow-up assessment of pneumonia.

title: CT low attenuation area quantification versus visual scoring for early pulmonary emphysema detection in lung cancer screening.
abstract: To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans. A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection. Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05). LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset. Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

title: Baveno VI criteria validation and development of a new non-invasive strategy for varices rule-out in patients with HCC (SAPHE-R: Stiffness, ALBI, Platelets, HEpatocellular carcinoma Rule).
abstract: Accuracy of Baveno criteria for avoiding endoscopy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is uncertain, and systematic upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (UGE) may not be necessary. We evaluated Baveno VI criteria performance in this population and developed an alternative non-invasive rule to exclude esophagogastric varices of any grade, rather than high-risk varices (HRV). Patients with BCLC 0-C HCC and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) from Italian Liver Cancer (ITA.LI.CA) database, with available liver stiffness measurement (LSM), UGE, and blood tests within six months of diagnosis, were included. Independent predictors of varices identified by logistic regression were combined through grid-search to derive a rule-out strategy (SAPHE-R), validated by bootstrap-resampling and in an independent cohort (Vienna). The derivation cohort comprised 598 patients (age, 69 years; male sex, 75.3%; viral etiology, 69.3%; BCLC 0/A, 77.9%; ALBI 1, 54.2%; varices, 33.4%; HRV, 11.2%). Baveno VI criteria missed 8.5% of varices and 6.0% of HRV, sparing 31.1% of UGE. Independent predictors of varices were incorporated into SAPHE-R (LSM≤16 kPa, platelet count ≥160×10⁹/L, ALBI grade 1), which missed 4.0% of varices (HRV 3.0%, spared UGE 17.6%). In the validation cohort (n=149), SAPHE-R missed 4.8% of varices (HRV 3.1%, spared UGE 14.8%). Results remained consistent in sensitivity analyses. In an exploratory analysis, no HVPG-defined CSPH was observed among SAPHE-R rule-out patients (0/22). Baveno VI criteria showed suboptimal performance in patients with HCC and cACLD, whereas SAPHE-R provided a reliable non-invasive strategy to rule out varices, facilitating variceal risk assessment in patients with HCC.

title: Uncertainty-guided Multitask Mean Teacher Model for Hybrid ASPECTS Scoring of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: The Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment decision-making in acute ischemic stroke. Recent hybrid scoring methods that combine ASPECTS prediction with auxiliary lesion segmentation have demonstrated great potential by enhancing the model's discriminative power through multitask learning. However, their performance is still limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the insufficient exploitation of shared information across tasks, posing challenges for precise and robust stroke assessment. In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised hybrid ASPECTS scoring framework (Semi-HAS) built upon an uncertainty guided multitask mean teacher architecture, which leverages readily available unlabeled data to enhance ASPECTS scoring. Specifically, a dedicated task interaction component is introduced in Semi-HAS to explicitly extract lesion-related complementary information from the auxiliary segmentation task. The proposed component is meanwhile coordinated with a cross-task alignment loss to successfully facilitate collaboration between different tasks for more consistent ASPECTS prediction. Furthermore, we design an adaptive uncertainty estimation for both tasks to generate dual uncertainty maps for mitigating noise introduced by unlabeled data. As a result, this innovative strategy effectively guides cross-model consistency learning for transferring trustworthy knowledge from teacher to student model and improving scoring accuracy for complex anatomical conditions. Extensive experiments on both public and in-house datasets demonstrate that Semi-HAS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods by achieving superior scoring accuracy across ASPECTS regions and providing reliable patient level assessments, highlighting its promise in facilitating clinical ASPECTS evaluation and promoting personalized treatments.

title: Stochastic Siamese MAE Pretraining for Longitudinal Medical Images.
abstract: Temporally aware image representations are crucial for capturing disease progression in 3D volumes of longitudinal medical datasets. However, recent state-of-the-art self-supervised learning approaches like Masked Autoencoding (MAE), despite their strong representation learning capabilities, lack temporal awareness. In this paper, we propose STAMP (Stochastic Temporal Autoencoder with Masked Pretraining), a Siamese MAE framework that encodes temporal information through a stochastic process by conditioning on the time difference between the 2 input volumes. Unlike deterministic Siamese approaches, which compare scans from different time points but fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in disease evolution, STAMP learns temporal dynamics stochastically by reframing the MAE reconstruction loss as a conditional variational inference objective. We evaluated STAMP on two OCT and one MRI datasets with multiple visits per patient. STAMP pretrained ViT models outperformed both existing temporal MAE methods and foundation models on different late stage Age-Related Macular Degeneration and Alzheimer's Disease progression prediction which require models to learn the underlying non-deterministic temporal dynamics of the diseases.

title: From Recall to Reassurance: Common Benign Mimics in Breast Screening Assessment-A Pictorial Review.
abstract: Benign breast lesions, anatomical variants, and imaging artefacts can closely mimic malignancy on screening mammography and are a frequent diagnostic challenge in the assessment setting. This pictorial review showcases a spectrum of benign lesions encountered in a high-volume breast screening assessment setting that initially raised suspicion for malignancy but were subsequently confirmed as benign through a combination of digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT), targeted ultrasound, and clinicopathological correlation. Examples include cutaneous lesions, sebaceous cysts, intramammary lymph nodes, hamartomas, fat necrosis, vascular lesions, simple cysts and summation artefact. Through illustrative cases, we highlight key imaging features that support accurate lesion characterization and demonstrate the complementary roles of mammography, DBT, and ultrasound in distinguishing benign entities from breast cancer. Familiarity with these imaging appearances can improve diagnostic confidence, reduce false-positive recalls, and minimize unnecessary biopsies within breast screening programs.

title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier.
abstract: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x-ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP-based diagnostics, from benchtop to high-fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

title: Predicting Pathologic Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Breast Cancer Using Machine Learning of MRI Radiomics.
abstract: To develop and validate a machine learning-based MRI radiomics model for predicting the risk of non-pathological complete response (non-pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer, to identify independent influencing factors. A total of 400 consecutive breast cancer patients were randomly divided into training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Baseline clinicopathological variables, functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) parameters, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and longitudinal MRI radiomics scores were collected. Variables were selected using univariate analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression models were constructed and evaluated using area under the curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed all six factors (Ki-67 proliferation index, maximum tumor diameter, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) value, initial enhancement rate, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and radiomics score) as independent predictors of non-pCR (P < 0.05). The random forest model showed the numerically highest AUC, with an AUC of 0.835 [95% confidence interval(CI): 0.767-0.904] in the training set and 0.745 (95% CI: 0.597-0.893) in the validation set, outperforming logistic regression (training: 0.805; validation: 0.717) and support vector machine (training: 0.792; validation: 0.702). SHAP analysis revealed that feature contributions, in descending order, were as follows: radiomics score, ADC value, initial enhancement rate, TILs, Ki-67 proliferation index, and maximum tumor diameter. SHAP analysis identified radiomics score, ADC value, and initial enhancement rate as the leading contributors. The random forest model constructed in this study, integrating MRI radiomics and functional imaging parameters, exhibits acceptable discrimination and calibration for predicting pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.

title: Longitudinal Changes in Brain Connectivity and Structure after MRgFUS VIM Thalamotomy for Essential Tremor.
abstract: Essential Tremor (ET) is the most common movement disorder. Magnetic Resonance-guided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS), an incisionless surgery involving thermal ablation of targeted brain regions, like the Ventral Intermediate Nucleus of the Thalamus (VIM) and surrounding white matter tracts, is an effective treatment option. Fractional Anisotropy (FA), a metric of diffusion tensor imaging, can be used to determine white matter structural integrity and their changes following MRgFUS. This study investigates white matter and morphological brain remodeling after MRgFUS VIM thalamotomy and its association with tremor improvement, assessed by the Clinical Rating Scale for Tremor (CRST), over the first postoperative year. We retrospectively analyzed 56 ET patients who underwent unilateral MRgFUS VIM thalamotomy. Subjects' CRST scores, T1-weighted MRI scans, and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans were acquired pre-operatively and at three and twelve months post-operatively. FA maps were generated and registered to a standard space. Voxel clusters that exhibited significant change in FA over time were identified using FSL's cluster tool (p<0.001) and their change in FA value over time was Spearman correlated with relative change in CRST score. Deformation-Based Morphometry of T1-weighted images evaluated changes in structural volume, and a linear mixed-effects model was applied. We permuted these values 1000 times randomly to isolate significant (p<0.01) clusters related to the interaction between time and outcome and Spearman correlated them with relative improvement in CRST. Four main FA clusters demonstrated strong associations between CRST score and time. The insula produced consistent positive correlations at three (R=0.32, p=0.04) and twelve months (R=0.29, p=0.11). Yet, the visual cortex exhibited no significant association at three months (R=0.11, p=0.46), but did at twelve months (R=0.35, p=0.05), suggesting malleable white matter remodeling. Our morphometry analysis revealed two primary clusters located in the pre-supplementary motor area (pre-SMA) and visual cortex. The pre-SMA exhibited the strongest correlations at three months (three months: R=0.34, p=0.03, twelve months: R=0.17, p=0.36), while the visual cortex displayed a similar strength throughout (three months: R=0.20, p=0.18, twelve months: R=-0.22, p=0.23). These findings suggest that MRgFUS VIM thalamotomy is associated with broad structural tract and volumetric changes that extend beyond motor networks. Both analyses demonstrated post-treatment volume growth and increased tract structure in visual and cognitive regions. Correlation with tremor improvement indicates many of these changes may contribute to individual outcomes during the first post-operative year.

title: Incidental detection of maternal malignancy in non-reportable results from non-invasive prenatal testing: experience in Hong Kong and literature review.
abstract: Introduction Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) for fetal aneuploidy occasionally yields non-reportable results due to persistent 'noisy' signals, which may indicate occult maternal malignancy. This study investigated the clinical and genetic implications of non-reportable NIPT results, focusing on multiple chromosomal aberrations associated with maternal malignancy, with the goal of developing standardised management protocols for pregnant women with such suspicious NIPT results. Methods From 2020 to 2023, women with persistent non-reportable NIPT results were identified and followed up in Hong Kong. Cancer cases were analysed for clinical history and chromosomal patterns. Incidental cancer detection rates were calculated and compared with literature reports. Tag Z -score chromosomal abnormalities were compared between cancer and non-cancer groups; the corresponding sensitivity and specificity were calculated. Results Among 84 446 NIPT tests, 151 (0.18%) showed persistent noisy signals. Of 131 patients with follow-up data, five (3.82%) were diagnosed with maternal malignancy; the overall incidental detection rate was 0.006% (5 of 84 446). Although three women delivered healthy babies, most presented with late-stage cancer confirmed by imaging and biopsy. All five cases exhibited ≥3 chromosomal aberrations on repeat NIPT; chromosome 18 was consistently involved. Univariate analysis revealed significant differences in Tag Z -score frequencies for chromosomes 18 (P=0.026) and 21 (P=0.029) between cancer and non-cancer groups. A clinical flowchart was developed to guide management of patients with multiple aberrations. Conclusion Although rare, occult maternal malignancy represents 3.82% of non-reportable NIPT results. This risk should be included in pre-test counselling and may warrant early oncological evaluation. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging should be considered to facilitate cancer diagnosis.

title: Predictive Value of the Cincinnati Scale for Code Stroke Activation in Relation to CT Scan Findings
abstract: Background: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide and main cause of disability in adults. Timely care is essential to achieve reperfusion and preserve brain tissue. Efforts have been made to correlate CT signs with the Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale to activate the Comprehensive Stroke Protocol. Analyzing these factors may provide useful parameters for selection. Material and Methods: This analytical, cross-sectional, observational, prospective study was conducted at the Regional General Hospital in Orizaba, Mexico. A total of 497_20 non-contrast cranial CT scans were analyzed using PACS. Patients were followed through medical records until discharge diagnosis was confirmed. Data collection occurred from March 2024_45. Results: 497_2 CT scans were reviewed. The Stroke Code was most often used in the 70-79-year age group, with 56.9% female patients. Of 72_24 ischemic stroke cases, only 24_29 were within the therapeutic window. Conclusion: The Cincinnati scale as a rapid cerebrovascular screen has only moderate to low discriminatory ability. Sensitivity and positive predictive value are very low. Therefore, it is not suitable alone. The results provide opportunity to train doctors to use the Cincinnati scale alongside the NIHSS scale, which has better predictive ability. More public education is recommended to help patients present within the window.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Investigating Pseudo-Learning and Bias Propagation in MRI Brain Tumour Classification
abstract: A brain tumour is an abnormal growth of cells in the brain, which can be either benign (noncancerous) or malignant (cancerous). The 5-year survival rate for benign brain tumours is approximately 85-95%, whereas it is only 35-36% for malignant tumours. Therefore, early detection and diagnosis of brain tumours is important. The recent developments in deep learning have allowed for high precision, accuracy, and automation in detecting these tumours, including both gliomas and pituitary tumours. In this paper, three deep learning-based models for brain tumour categorisation from MRI images are compared to understand the limitations of accuracy-based evaluation with metrics such as class-wise performance and Grad-CAM. To assess the performance and observe various behavioural issues of the models used in this analysis, the MRI scans from the Brain Tumour MRI Dataset from Kaggle and the BRISC 2025 classification dataset containing MRI images from all four major tumour groups were leveraged for their training and testing. The first model serves as a baseline EfficientNet classifier, while the second model applies fine-tuning techniques to improve feature learning. The third model further enhances performance by incorporating multi-dataset training to increase data diversity. The reported confusion matrices show that Model V3 achieved 97.63% accuracy on its 800-image test set. Because its test set differs in size and may differ in composition from those of Models V1 and V2, this result should not be interpreted as a direct like-for-like comparison.The findings highlight the importance of combining conventional performance metrics with Grad-CAM analysis when investigating model behaviour, while further evaluation is needed to establish whether multi-dataset training reduces pseudo-learning or improves generalisation.

title: Predicting high-risk HPV infection and genotype co-infection using genital tract microecological and pathogen characteristics: a machine learning study
abstract: Abstract Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions. Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract co-infections may influence HR-HPV acquisition, clearance, and persistence. However, quantitative prediction models integrating vaginal microecological indicators, genital tract pathogens, and HR-HPV genotype co-infection patterns remain limited. Methods This retrospective study included 3,403 patients who underwent concurrent HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and genital tract pathogen testing at the gynecology outpatient clinic of Hainan Women and Children’s Medical Center between January 2022 and December 2025. Of these, 765 were HR-HPV-positive and 2,638 were HR-HPV-negative. Candidate predictors were selected using univariable analysis, multicollinearity assessment based on the variance inflation factor (VIF ≦ 4), and the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine learning models were developed, and their hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with 10-fold cross-validation within the training set. Classifier chains (C ≦ C) and ensemble classifier chains (ECC) were applied to the multi-label prediction of HR-HPV genotypes. Model predictions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results In multivariable logistic regression, Ureaplasma urealyticum (UU; aOR = 2.051), Chlamydia trachomatis (CT;aOR = 1.982), severe bacterial vaginosis score (aOR = 1.614), abnormal vaginal pH (aOR = 1.375), and sialidase positivity (aOR = 1.747) were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity (all P < 0.05). The random forest model achieved the best discrimination in internal validation (AUC = 0.772, sensitivity 0.735, F1 = 0.650). For the ulti-label task, eight HR-HPV genotypes with at least 30 positive cases were included; the ECC model yielded a higher Jaccard score (0.0226) than the independent-label model (0.0190). SHAP identified UU, age, CT, and cocci abundance as leading predictors, whereas a higher Lactobacillus proportion lowered predicted risk. Conclusions Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract infections were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination, and ECC provided a modest improvement in multi-genotype prediction. These findings may inform risk-based screening, pending external validation.

The random forest model achieved the best discrimination in internal validation (AUC = 0.772, sensitivity 0.735, F1 = 0.650). For the ulti-label task, eight HR-HPV genotypes with at least 30 positive cases were included; the ECC model yielded a higher Jaccard score (0.0226) than the independent-label model (0.0190). SHAP identified UU, age, CT, and cocci abundance as leading predictors, whereas a higher Lactobacillus proportion lowered predicted risk. Conclusions Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract infections were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination, and ECC provided a modest improvement in multi-genotype prediction. These findings may inform risk-based screening, pending external validation.

title: Influence of CT Tube Replacement and System Parameter Update on Reconstructed CT Values and Electron Density Conversion Curves in Radiotherapy Treatment Planning Systems
abstract: Abstract Objective Large-aperture positioning CT is a core device for radiotherapy simulation, target delineation, and accurate dose calculation. Replacement of the X‑ray tube, followed by subsequent system parameter updates (including software version upgrade, reconstruction algorithm adjustment, and detector gain calibration), may alter the X-ray energy spectrum and image reconstruction characteristics, thereby inducing systematic drift of CT numbers (Hounsfield Units, HU) and disturbing the accuracy of CT-relative electron density (CT-RED) and CT-mass density (CT-MD) conversion curves in treatment planning systems (TPS). This study aimed to quantify CT number drifts in multiple tissue‑equivalent phantoms before and after tube replacement and system parameter updates using a Philips Big Bore CT 16 scanner, to evaluate the detection efficacy of conventional AAPM TG66 image quality indicators for such occult drift, to reconstruct density conversion curves for Eclipse and Tomo TPS, and to establish a standardized quality control workflow. Methods Fault records and the tube replacement process from August 2023 to January 2024 were analyzed. Tube replacement was performed on January 13, 2024, followed by standard acceptance tests including position calibration, focus correction, long‑tube conditioning, and air scan. System software was upgraded from V3.6 to V4.8 on October 18, 2024, with resetting of reconstruction filter parameters, detector gain coefficients, and air baseline. All CT value measurements, curve reconstructions, and dosimetric verifications were performed after the software upgrade, representing the combined effect of “tube replacement + system parameter update”. Image quality was tested with a Catphan504 phantom according to AAPM TG66. CT value changes in 8 standard materials (air, polystyrene, water, LDPE, PMP, acrylic, Delrin, Teflon) before and after the intervention were compared using paired t‑tests with Bonferroni correction. CT-RED curves (standard and brain‑specific) for Eclipse and a CT-MD curve for Tomo were reconstructed using a CIRS-062M phantom containing 12 tissue‑equivalent materials. Accuracy of the new curves was validated by heterogeneous phantom planar dose verification and real patient plan QA. Results All conventional image quality indicators remained within TG66 tolerances after the intervention. Systematic CT drifts were observed in 7 of the 8 materials except water (P = 0.12, not significant), with drifts ranging 10–30 HU for most materials; Teflon showed a − 63 HU drift (P < 0.001) and air a + 33 HU drift (P < 0.001). Two CT‑RED curves for Eclipse and one CT‑MD curve for Tomo were successfully constructed, all with R² > 0.99. Dosimetric verification showed 3 mm/3% Gamma passing rates for Eclipse ≥ 98.9%, mean point‑dose deviation for Tomo 0.76%, and real patient plan QA passing rates > 98% with no significant differences before vs. after intervention (P > 0.05). Conclusion CT tube replacement and subsequent system parameter updates did not impair conventional TG66 image quality indicators, but induced systematic, material‑dependent CT number drifts that cannot be detected by routine water‑phantom uniformity tests. Re‑measurement of multi‑material CT baselines and mandatory reconstruction of density conversion curves are required. A four‑level quality control process (air calibration, multi‑material CT baseline measurement, curve reconstruction, and dosimetric verification) should be enforced after tube replacement or major software upgrades.

title: Metachronous Bilateral Primary Breast Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary breast lymphoma (PBL) is a rare extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma originating from the breast parenchyma, with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) being the most common histological subtype. Metachronous bilateral involvement is exceedingly uncommon, and standardized treatment guidelines remain lacking. Herein, we report a case of metachronous bilateral primary breast DLBCL with a 15-year disease-free interval and present a comprehensive literature review. Case presentation: A 47-year-old female presented with a palpable left breast mass in February 2026. She had a history of right breast PBL diagnosed in 2011, achieving complete remission after eight cycles of CHOP. Breast ultrasound, mammography, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a BI-RADS category 4B lesion in the left breast. Core needle biopsy confirmed DLBCL with immunohistochemistry demonstrating CD20 positivity (70%–80%), Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 90%, and negative epithelial markers. Whole-body ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT excluded systemic involvement, confirming the diagnosis of stage IE left breast PBL. The patient received a zuberitamab-containing CMOP (Hi-CMOP). After fivecycles, repeat PET/CT demonstrated complete metabolic response with the Deauville score decreasing from 5 to 1, and breast ultrasound confirmed resolution of the breast lesion. Conclusions: PBL lacks pathognomonic clinical and imaging features, and definitive diagnosis hinges on histopathological examination with immunohistochemistry. For stage IE DLBCL-type PBL, rituximab-based immunochemotherapy followed by consolidative radiotherapy represents a rational therapeutic strategy with favorable short-term outcomes. Long-term surveillance remains essential given the risk of late contralateral recurrence. Multicenter studies with larger cohorts are warranted to establish evidence-based management guidelines.

title: Multimodal Imaging-Assisted Diagnosis of a Rare Primary Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma Secondary to Imatinib plus Sintilimab in a Postoperative GIST Patient
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary cutaneous T cell lymphoma represents a heterogeneous subgroup of extranodal non‑Hodgkin lymphoma and frequently presents with non‑specific cutaneous manifestations that contribute to high rates of misdiagnosis. Emerging evidence suggests combined treatment with tyrosine‑kinase inhibitors and PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitors may drive secondary lymphomagenesis. This case adds to literature by highlighting the diagnostic value of multimodal non‑invasive skin imaging (dermoscopy plus high‑frequency ultrasound) as ancillary clues before definitive histopathological confirmation. Case Summary: A 58‑year‑old male with completely‑resected high‑risk gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) developed progressive generalized skin lesions following imatinib and single‑dose sintilimab therapy. He presented with widespread purplish‑red scaly papules and plaques accompanied by pruritus, eyebrow loss and palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy. Routine laboratory tests revealed mild monocytosis and slight anaemia. Multimodal imaging including high‑frequency ultrasound and dermoscopy identified characteristic cutaneous changes. Histopathology together with immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of primary cutaneous T‑cell lymphoma. Unfortunately, the patient was lost to follow‑up after hospital discharge, so post‑discharge therapeutic response could not be evaluated. Conclusion: Multimodal non‑invasive skin imaging assists early suspicion of PCTCL; definitive diagnosis still depends on histopathology and immunohistochemistry. Clinicians should remain alert for secondary cutaneous lymphoproliferative disorders among patients receiving combined targeted‑immune anticancer therapy.

title: A multimodal CT-based machine-learning model for differentiating pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma from conventional non-small cell lung cancer: an internally validated study
abstract: Abstract Background: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is difficult to distinguish from conventional non-small cell lung cancer (c-NSCLC) before pathological diagnosis. We evaluated whether clinical–CT semantic features, radiomics and deep-learning features can support this distinction. Methods: After image quality control, 397 patients (83 PSC, 314 c-NSCLC) from three institutions were analysed. Six models (clinical-only, radiomics-only, deep-only, clinical+radiomics, clinical+deep and full fusion) were developed and evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation (five outer folds repeated 20 times, five inner folds), with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, classifier selection and threshold selection confined to training folds. Discrimination, calibration and operating-point performance were estimated from patient-level out-of-fold predictions. The influence of CT acquisition heterogeneity was examined in sensitivity analyses. Results: The prespecified full fusion model achieved an AUROC of 0.890 (95% CI 0.848–0.930) and an AUPRC of 0.739 (0.643–0.823; PSC prevalence 0.209). At a training-derived high-sensitivity threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 0.855 and 0.755. The clinical+radiomics model performed similarly (AUROC 0.895, 0.851–0.934), the clinical-only model reached 0.843 (0.796–0.887), and deep features alone were not discriminative (AUROC 0.533). Intratumoral low-attenuation area (LAA) presence and LAA ratio were independently associated with PSC. Acquisition parameters alone also discriminated the groups (AUROC 0.901); after adjustment for acquisition variables, radiomics retained incremental value over clinical features (ΔAUROC 0.075, P<0.001), but residual confounding by source or protocol cannot be excluded. Conclusions: Intratumoral LAA features and CT radiomics may help flag PSC before pathology in an internally validated setting, whereas Kinetics-pretrained deep features added no value. Because acquisition heterogeneity may contribute to imaging-based performance and a negative prediction cannot exclude PSC, the model should be regarded as exploratory and requires external validation with standardized acquisition before clinical use.

title: Translating Imaging-based Brain Age Models for Predicting Accelerated Brain Ageing in African Populations: A Pilot Study on a Nigerian Cohort.
abstract: Abstract Background: Brain age is an emerging imaging biomarker for early detection of neurodegenerative disorders, based on the estimation of the brain’s biological age. Existing predictive models are predominantly trained on Global North (GN) neuroimaging data, limiting their sensitivity when applied to underrepresented populations due to geographic, imaging scanner, and biological heterogeneity. We investigated this bias by adapting the standard Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) method to a population-specific (PS) brain age model. Methods: Using a multi-institutional T1-weighted brain MRI dataset from 309 Nigerian adults, we implemented a robust low-compute image analysis pipeline which includes repurposing clinical scans and high-resolution cortical parcellation with multi-stage quality control. The PS-GPR model was trained on regional brain volumetric features from the Nigerian MRI scans and its performance compared to four common GN pre-trained models. Results: The proposed PS-GPR model showed a significantly lower prediction error (mean absolute error = 9.82 years) without age-bias correction and few seconds inference time compared to GN-trained machine learning models (mean absolute error = 10.00 – 16.70 years). SPARROW, a generalizable deep learning framework achieved an MAE of 7.87 but failed on 6% of the test set. This early work demonstrates the importance of representative data to build resource-efficient clinically viable models. Conclusion: This population-specific model is a step towards sensitive low-compute African brain age models. With the expansion of imaging data beyond Nigeria through the Africa Neuroimaging Archive (AfNiA), we will further develop the PS model to identify individuals with accelerated brain ageing for early intervention in at-risk adults.

title: Multifocal Well-Differentiated Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumor Presenting as Partial Small Bowel Obstruction in an Elderly Female: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are rare, slow-growing malignancies that frequently present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to diagnostic delays averaging five to seven years. Despite the existence of blood-based biomarkers including serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), most patients continue to present with advanced locoregional or metastatic disease. This case illustrates the diagnostic and surgical challenges of SI-NET in an elderly patient and highlights the clinical consequences of delayed biomarker utilization. Case presentation: A 77-year-old White female was referred to a surgical clinic after her primary care physician identified a small bowel mass on imaging ordered for chronic abdominal discomfort and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss. CT imaging demonstrated a solid mesenteric mass with adjacent adenopathy and small bowel tethering, producing the characteristic spoke-wheel sign of mesenteric desmoplasia. Serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-HIAA were not obtained prior to surgical referral. She underwent exploratory laparotomy with open small bowel resection and side-to-side anastomosis. Surgical pathology confirmed multifocal, well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (Grade 1, Ki-67 ~ 1%), staged pT4N1, with lymphovascular and perineural invasion and a positive mesenteric margin. Postoperative Dotatate PET identified a single PET-avid mesenteric lesion, prompting referral to a tertiary hepatobiliary center. A second exploratory laparotomy resected a 1.5 cm mesenteric nodule requiring direct repair of a superior mesenteric artery branch. Final pathology demonstrated fibrosis and chronic inflammation with no residual neuroendocrine tumor. The patient elected active surveillance with annual follow-up. Conclusions This case demonstrates the striking discordance between low tumor grade and advanced locoregional disease extent in SI-NETs and underscores the missed opportunity for earlier detection through routine biomarker screening in symptomatic patients. The PET-positive mesenteric nodule that yielded only fibrosis on re-resection raises important questions about functional imaging specificity in the desmoplastic postoperative mesentery. Clinicians should maintain a low threshold for obtaining serum chromogranin A and urinary 5-HIAA in patients presenting with unexplained weight loss and chronic gastrointestinal symptoms.

title: FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia with multisystem involvement: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia (PVNH) is an X-linked neuronal migration disorder classically associated with epilepsy. Accumulating evidence indicates that it is a multisystem disorder involving cardiac valvular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic manifestations. We report a patient with an unusually comprehensive multisystem phenotype to emphasize the need for systematic extracranial evaluation in FLNA-related PVNH. Case presentation: A 33-year-old woman presented with two decades of headache and palpitations. Physical examination revealed digital clubbing and prominently dilated cardiac valves. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral periventricular heterotopia. Enhanced whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic nonsense variant in FLNA (NM_001110556.2:c.2193C > G, p.Tyr731Ter). Multisystem involvement comprised focal epilepsy, polyvalvular regurgitation, interstitial lung disease, and ophthalmologic abnormalities. Seizures were controlled with oxcarbazepine and lamotrigine, and the patient was referred for coordinated cardiologic, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic follow-up. Conclusions FLNA-related PVNH should be managed as a multisystem disorder rather than isolated epilepsy. Routine cardiovascular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic screening, combined with genetic counseling for X-linked dominant transmission, should be integrated into standard care.

title: Preoperative diffusion-perivascular MRI burden and postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease
abstract: Abstract Postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may reflect pre-existing brain vulnerability, but the preoperative imaging correlates of this vulnerability remain uncertain. We examined whether a combined diffusion and perivascular imaging burden was associated with delirium after bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. This single-centre observational cohort included 100 patients with Parkinson disease undergoing bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation and 32 healthy controls scanned with the same preoperative MRI protocol. Delirium was assessed during postoperative days using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale with clinical adjudication. Age- and sex-adjusted reference models fitted in healthy controls were used to standardise tract diffusion metrics, diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space, and basal ganglia enlarged perivascular space counts. Directionally aligned diffusion and perivascular scores were averaged with equal domain weights. Patients who developed postoperative delirium (n = 30) had higher combined burden than those who did not (n = 70; 95% CI, 0.584 to 1.526; q<.001). Using Firth penalised logistic regression, higher combined burden remained associated with postoperative delirium after adjustment for age, sex, education, Mini-Mental State Examination score, disease duration, and motor severity (95% CI, 1.49 to 4.25; Wald P<.001). Higher burden was also associated with longer delirium duration and higher peak screening scores among affected patients. Exploratory internal prediction yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.701 after adding burden to clinical variables, compared with 0.538 for clinical variables alone. These findings support preoperative diffusion-perivascular burden as a candidate marker of perioperative neuropsychiatric vulnerability requiring multicentre validation.

title: Germline Whole-Gene Deletion of SDHA in a Carotid Body Paraganglioma Identified by Whole-Genome Sequencing and Confirmed by MLPA: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background : Carotid body paragangliomas are frequently associated with germline variants in succinate dehydrogenase ( SDH ) genes. Among these, SDHA variants are particularly challenging to diagnose due to low penetrance and the presence of highly homologous pseudogenes. Standard diagnostic workflows, including whole-exome sequencing and targeted panels, often fail to detect large structural variants, such as whole-gene deletions, leading to potential underdiagnosis. This case is the first to report a germline whole-gene deletion of SDHA identified via whole-genome sequencing (WGS), providing definitive physical evidence of the Knudson two-hit hypothesis through the somatic loss of the remaining allele in the tumor tissue. Case presentation : A 63-year-old female presented with a 2-cm, left carotid body tumor. There was no relevant family history. The tumor was successfully resected, and histopathology confirmed a paraganglioma. While immunohistochemistry showed a loss of both SDHA and SDHB expression, WGS of peripheral blood revealed what is, to our knowledge, the first reported germline whole-gene deletion of the SDHA gene (copy number ≈ 1.1) in the region chr5:210,651–314,171. Notably, this type of large structural variant is potentially elusive to standard genetic analysis workflows. Subsequent WGS of the tumor tissue confirmed biallelic inactivation through the loss of the remaining allele (copy number ≈ 0.86), representing a classic two-hit mechanism. This large-scale deletion of all SDHA exons was further validated using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), confirming it as the pathogenic driver. The patient remains under rigorous long-term follow-up given the reported 15% risk of malignancy associated with SDHA variants. Conclusions : This case highlights the clinical utility of WGS in overcoming the inherent limitations of exome-based sequencing for SDHA analysis. When clinical suspicion remains high - specifically in cases with SDHA-negative immunohistochemistry but negative standard genetic testing - WGS or MLPA should be employed to detect hidden structural variants. Accurate molecular diagnosis is essential not only for understanding the mechanism of tumorigenesis but also for tailoring oncological surveillance and genetic counseling for the patient and their family.

title: Operator-rated puncture performance and first-pass lesion tissue area in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: an exploratory single-center sub-analysis of endoscopic ultrasound- guided tissue acquisition
abstract: Abstract Background: Adequate tissue acquisition is important for histological assessment and ancillary testing in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We primarily explored the association between operator-rated puncture performance and first-pass lesion tissue area during endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) in patients with PDAC. A secondary analysis examined whether this association was observed in the overall cohort, irrespective of final diagnosis. Methods: This exploratory single-center sub-analysis used prospective data from a multicenter randomized trial of 22-gauge fine-needle biopsy needles. Endoscopists rated overall puncture performance on a five-point scale after EUS-TA. Ratings were analyzed using two post hoc dichotomizations: very easy/easy versus indeterminate/difficult/very difficult, and very easy versus all other ratings. First-pass lesion tissue area was quantified automatically on histological slides using a digital microscope with image-analysis software. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations between ratings and tissue areas in each cohort, adjusting for needle type, puncture route, operator experience, and lesion size. Firth logistic regression assessed associations between ratings and exploratory ≥ 4-mm² benchmark attainment in the PDAC cohort. Trends in tissue area across very easy, easy, and remaining ratings were assessed using the Jonckheere–Terpstra test. Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) suitability was summarized descriptively. Results: Of 62 patients, 48 had PDAC. In the PDAC cohort, the very easy/easy comparison yielded inconclusive adjusted associations with tissue area and benchmark attainment. A very easy rating was associated with greater tissue area (median, 5.45 vs. 1.90 mm²; adjusted difference, 1.93 mm²; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.12–3.74) and benchmark attainment (57.7% vs. 22.7%; adjusted odds ratio, 4.44; 95% CI, 1.17–21.06). Tissue area decreased with less favorable ratings (p for trend = 0.016). Two of six patients assessed for CGP were considered suitable. In the overall cohort, lesion size remained associated with tissue area, whereas adjusted associations for both rating dichotomizations were inconclusive. Tissue area decreased with less favorable ratings (p for trend = 0.034). Conclusions: In patients with PDAC, an endoscopist’s very easy rating was associated with greater first-pass lesion tissue area after adjustment for lesion size and procedural factors. Prospective pass-by-pass studies are needed to validate this exploratory association and determine its utility in EUS-TA. Trial registration: Parent trial: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT), jRCT1042220099, registered on 25 November 2022.
