title: Systematic differences between ultrasound and MRI assessment of fetal ventricular width in cases of fetal mild ventriculomegaly: a cohort study.
abstract: Prenatal assessment of the lateral ventricles is essential for detecting and classifying fetal ventriculomegaly (VM). Although ultrasound (US) is the primary screening tool, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly used to complement diagnosis. However, discrepancies between US and MRI measurements, particularly in mild VM, may affect classification, counseling, and planning clinical management. The aim of the study is to compare US and MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles, evaluate the agreement between both methods, with particular focus on mild ventriculomegaly, and additionally assess the feasibility of deriving conversion formulas between both modalities. Methods This cohort study included 120 fetuses examined between 2011 and 2021 at a referral center: 75 with isolated mild VM and 45 controls. All underwent a standardized US assessment and fetal MRI. Ventricular width was measured twice for each modality; mean values were used for statistical comparison. Analysis included Wilcoxon tests, Friedman tests, Bland-Altman plots, Pearson's chi-square tests, Theil-Sen regression, and linear modeling. Results MRI systematically provided greater ventricular measurements than US. In the study group, the bias was 0.71mm for coronal MRI and 0.33mm for axial MRI. Agreement between methods was limited, with measurement discrepancies observed in 34% of cases (coronal) and 33.3% (axial). Combined analysis of both groups confirmed persistent measurement discrepancies, though the overall axial MRI bias decreased to 0.15mm. Theil-Sen modelling enabled the development of conversion formulas for both measurement planes. Conclusions MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles tend to be slightly higher than ultrasound measurements, particularly in the coronal plane. These systematic differences may change the VM classification and should be considered in clinical interpretation. Ultrasound demonstrated better measurement reproducibility. The obtained formulas may support improved cross-modality comparison in clinical practice.

Results MRI systematically provided greater ventricular measurements than US. In the study group, the bias was 0.71mm for coronal MRI and 0.33mm for axial MRI. Agreement between methods was limited, with measurement discrepancies observed in 34% of cases (coronal) and 33.3% (axial). Combined analysis of both groups confirmed persistent measurement discrepancies, though the overall axial MRI bias decreased to 0.15mm. Theil-Sen modelling enabled the development of conversion formulas for both measurement planes. Conclusions MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles tend to be slightly higher than ultrasound measurements, particularly in the coronal plane. These systematic differences may change the VM classification and should be considered in clinical interpretation. Ultrasound demonstrated better measurement reproducibility. The obtained formulas may support improved cross-modality comparison in clinical practice.

title: Secondary metastasis resection after biomarker-stratified first-line treatment of metastatic colorectal carcinomaInterim analysis of the IVOPAK II study with a risk-benefit assessment of secondary metastatic resection.
abstract: Objective The IVOPAK II study (Interdisciplinary Care with Quality Control in Palliative Treatment of Colorectal Cancer) prospectively evaluated the risk (postoperative complications, mortality) and benefit (overall survival) of multimodal treatment with secondary metastasis resection for initially nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma. Patients and methods A total of 40 patients from 10 centers were enrolled. Patients with quintuple wildtype (K-RAS, N-RAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, ERBB2, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus cetuximab, while patients with RAS-mutation (K-RAS or N-RAS, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab. CT scans were presented at two-month intervals to the interdisciplinary tumor board at the University Hospital Erlangen to assess potentially curative secondary metastatic resection. After a median follow-up of 32 months, outcomes of the multimodally (chemotherapy treatment plus metastasis resection) and the palliatively (only chemotherapy treatment) treated patients were compared. Results The rate of secondary metastasis resection was 45% (18/40). Overall survival was significantly longer in the multimodal treatment group compared to the palliative treatment group (median 61 vs. 22 months, p=0.002), this also applied to progression-free survival (median 39 vs. 11 months, p=0.018). Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 morbidity occurred in 28% (5/18) of patients, and 90-day mortality was 6% (1/18). Univariate analyses revealed a significant improvement in overall survival among patients with ECOG performance status 0, solitary metastatic site and multimodal treatment. In multivariate analysis, the ECOG performance status proved to be an independent prognostic factor. Conclusion Following palliative biomarker-stratified first-line treatment for nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the multimodal approach with secondary metastatic resection demonstrated a significant survival benefit.

title: Lactation Management in Patients With Cancer: An Evidence-Based Framework for Surgical Practice.
abstract: BackgroundThe coexistence of lactation and cancer care, termed oncolactation , is becoming increasingly common as childbearing is delayed and more women are diagnosed with malignancy during the reproductive years. However, evidence-based guidance regarding breastfeeding during oncologic evaluation and treatment remains fragmented, particularly for surgeons involved in multidisciplinary cancer care.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with a systematic literature search using PubMed/MEDLINE and professional society guidelines (American Society of Breast Surgeons (ASBrS), American College of Radiology (ACR), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed®). Publications addressing surgical management, diagnostic imaging, systemic therapy, radiation therapy, and reproductive counseling in lactating patients with cancer were critically synthesized to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.ResultsMost diagnostic and surgical interventions-including mammography, breast MRI, computed tomography, image-guided biopsy, and general anesthesia-are compatible with continued breastfeeding when appropriate precautions are observed. Cytotoxic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and most targeted or immunotherapeutic agents remain contraindicated because of insufficient safety data or potential infant toxicity. Radiation therapy generally precludes breastfeeding from the treated breast, but permits continued feeding from the contralateral breast. Emerging evidence also supports individualized counseling regarding fertility preservation, future pregnancy, and survivorship.ConclusionsOncolactation should be incorporated into routine surgical oncology practice. Most surgical and diagnostic procedures can be performed without interrupting breastfeeding, whereas systemic therapies require individualized pharmacologic assessment. Integration of evidence-based lactation guidance into multidisciplinary cancer care promotes safe, patient-centered decision-making while maintaining oncologic safety and supporting breastfeeding whenever feasible.

title: A multivariate Bayesian biomarker screening algorithm that incorporates clinical covariates.
abstract: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has limited treatment options and poor survival. Early detection of HCC improves survival, but current ultrasound screening is inconsistent and poorly adhered to. Biomarker-based blood tests offer a more accurate, accessible, and reliable alternative. Recent developments in methods for early detection of HCC have focused on the trajectories of multiple biomarkers, assuming that biomarkers follow a joint hierarchical mixture model with random changepoints. We extend this model, allowing covariates to influence three aspects of the model: biomarker trajectories, diagnosis times, and subject-specific prior risks. We evaluated whether covariates could capture unexplained heterogeneity in biomarker levels to improve early detection. A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm was implemented to derive posterior distributions used in risk calculations among future patients and to determine whether a patient has a positive screen. The screening algorithm was evaluated through simulation studies under a range of possible covariate extensions. The Hepatitis C Antiviral Long-term Treatment against Cirrhosis (HALT-C) trial was used to further study the proposed biomarker screening algorithms for HCC using cross-validation.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Velopharyngeal MRI in Children With Unexplained Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the utility of velopharyngeal MRI in contributing additional diagnostic information for patients with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) of unknown etiology.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingTertiary children's hospital.ParticipantsChildren with clinically significant VPI without a confirmed etiology.InterventionsStandardized perceptual speech assessment with nasometry, non-sedated MRI, and multidisciplinary review for treatment planning.Main Outcome MeasuresMRI-informed etiologic classification, anatomic and functional contributors to VPI, and management recommendations.ResultsAmong 89 children, six (6.7%) presented with clinically significant VPI of unknown etiology on routine examination. MRI identified occult submucous cleft palate or atypical levator veli palatini morphology in five (83.3%) and adenoid-supported VP closure in three (50%). Involution was expected to unmask increased pharyngeal depth in two (33.3%). MRI supported patient-specific recommendations for speech therapy, surgical interventions, and longitudinal monitoring.ConclusionsMRI provided clinically meaningful diagnostic information beyond routine examination and informed management decisions for children with VPI.

title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

title: Interventions to increase participation in lung cancer screening programmes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT). Methods Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion. Results Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Educational/informational interventions (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.19) as well as SDM alone (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.57-2.32) did not improve LDCT uptake, despite the second improving decisional outcomes in both intervention and control groups. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare. Conclusions Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

title: Geriatric respiratory medicine 2026: from artificial intelligence to personalised management of the multimorbid patient.
abstract: The profound demographic shift toward an ageing population has decisively moved the burden of chronic and acute lung diseases towards older adults, necessitating a transition from organ-centred models to integrated, multidimensional care. This review outlines a pragmatic framework for managing the complex interplay of immunosenescence, frailty and multimorbidity. In acute care, "pneumonia-associated sarcopenia" is identified as a critical driver of recurrent infections and functional decline, requiring a shift towards aspiration prevention and the aid of diagnostic tools such as lung ultrasound. The selection of noninvasive respiratory support, including high-flow nasal cannulas and noninvasive ventilation, must balance physiological efficacy with the risks of delirium and patient self-inflicted lung injury. Preventive strategies have evolved with the introduction of 20-valent pneumococcal and respiratory syncytial virus vaccines, alongside proactive screening for ɑ1-antitrypsin deficiency to enable precision interventions. Chronic disease management emphasises a "device-centric" inhalation therapy approach, tailoring delivery systems to impaired peak inspiratory flows and cognitive status rather than to pharmacology alone. The advent of biological therapies, particularly the use of dupilumab and mepolizumab in eosinophilic COPD, offers a transformative "steroid-sparing" effect, aiming for clinical stability and preserved independence. Finally, the integration of artificial intelligence as "augmented intelligence" and the "4Ms" multidisciplinary model (mentation, medication, mobility, morbidities) provide the necessary tools to navigate clinical complexity. This holistic strategy ensures that technological innovation remains anchored in patient-centred goals.

title: Impact of reduced scan extent on tumor detection in <sup>68</sup>Ga-PSMA PET/CT for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
abstract: Background PSMA PET/CT plays an important role in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BCR-PCa). In general, PET/CT is performed as a limited or true whole-body examination. The majority of PET/CT scanners operate by measuring several bed positions or continuous motion with a limited axial field of view (FOV). Shortening the scan area thus results in a time saving, with unknown information loss regarding the detection of tumor manifestations. Methodology This retrospective single-center study included 200 patients with BCR-PCa after initial curative therapy who underwent a 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT scan from vertex to toe (true whole-body). Using retrospective subdivision into hypothetical partial body measurement protocols, the undetected tumor manifestations were examined. Classic PET/CT protocols were used: vertex to mid-thigh, skull base to mid-thigh, as well as CT-equivalent examination areas: chest/abdomen/pelvis (CAP), abdomen/pelvis (AP) and pelvis. Results Of 200 patients with a median PSA of 1.1 ng/mL, 128 (64%) showed at least one structural correlate of BCR-PCa in the true whole-body scan. The overall detection rate did not change for limited classic PET-protocols, or CAP measurements. CAP scans would not have detected all tumor manifestations in 16 patients (8%) and not all tumor-affected organ systems in six patients (3%), AP scans in 41 patients (21%) and 18 patients (9%), pelvic scans in 61 patients (31%) and 37 patients (19%), respectively. PSA may contribute to the prospective restriction of the scan area. Patients with PSA ≤ 0.75 ng/mL showed no diagnostic gain from whole-body imaging. This means that in 45% of patients in our cohort, a limitation to CAP scan would have been possible without losing information. Conclusions For a resource-saving use of routine PSMA-PET/CT, a scan from the vertex to the mid-thigh seems sufficient for detecting relevant metastases. For patients with low PSA levels, a more focused protocol that includes only the CAP region can be considered.

title: ACR lung-RADS: updates and future directions.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

title: Müllerian-type high-grade serous carcinoma presenting exclusively with pleural lesions and no detectable abdominopelvic primary tumor: a case report.
abstract: Background Müllerian-type high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) most commonly originates from the fallopian tube, ovary, or peritoneum and usually presents with abdominopelvic disease. Thoracic presentation without a detectable abdominopelvic primary tumor is extremely rare and poses a diagnostic challenge. Case presentation We report the case of a 60-year-old woman who was referred to our hospital after pleural thickening was detected during a routine medical checkup. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed left pleural thickening with mild pleural effusion. Thoracoscopic pleural biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle-shaped cells with mild nuclear atypia, with scattered calcifications and osteocyte-like elements. Immunohistochemical staining showed positivity for PAX8, WT-1, AE1/AE3, CK7, p16, and p53, and negativity for calretinin, D2-40, TTF-1, and Napsin A, supporting a Müllerian-type HGSC. Diagnostic/staging laparoscopy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy revealed no macroscopic tumor or disseminated lesions. Both ovaries and fallopian tubes were carefully examined pathologically, with the fallopian tubes examined using the SEE-FIM protocol. No malignant lesion or serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) was identified. Peritoneal washing cytology was negative. p53 and Ki-67 immunohistochemistry of the tubo-ovarian specimens was not performed. Discussion The absence of a detectable abdominopelvic primary tumor after radiological, laparoscopic, and pathological evaluation suggests an extremely rare thoracic presentation of Müllerian-type HGSC. Both ovaries and fallopian tubes were carefully examined pathologically, including examination of the fallopian tubes using the SEE-FIM protocol, and no malignant lesion or STIC was identified. Nevertheless, an occult microscopic Müllerian primary cannot be completely excluded, particularly because p53 and Ki-67 immunohistochemistry of the tubo-ovarian specimens was not performed. Primary pleural Müllerian carcinoma, EOPPC, and Müllerian-type HGSC of undetermined primary origin therefore remain possible classifications. Müllerian-type HGSC should be considered in the differential diagnosis of pleural tumors in women, even when no abdominopelvic primary tumor is identified. Comprehensive radiological, laparoscopic, and pathological evaluation is important for determining the most appropriate classification. In the absence of an identified primary site, classification should remain cautious, and EOPPC should be regarded as a possible interpretation rather than a definitive diagnosis.

title: Leveraging Digital Histopathology to Build Capacity and Collaboration Toward the Diagnosis of Pediatric Solid Tumors in Mexico.
abstract: Purpose Pediatric pathology in Mexico remains limited by an uneven distribution of specialized training and constrained resources, which can affect the accuracy of pediatric malignancy diagnosis. This study aimed to evaluate national diagnostic capacity for common organ-based pediatric solid tumors-renal tumors, neuroblastic tumors, and hepatic neoplasms-through a retrospective hybrid central pathology review. A secondary objective was to identify targeted areas for capacity building and strengthen collaborative networking. Materials and methods A hybrid retrospective pathology review (2005-2023) was conducted across eight institutions that treat pediatric oncology patients. Eligible cases included off-therapy patients age 0-18 years diagnosed with renal, hepatic, or neuroblastic tumors. Paraffin blocks, slides, clinical data, and original pathology reports were submitted. Cases underwent conventional pathology review, digital slide scanning, and joint virtual evaluation. Final diagnoses were compared between original, conventional central pathology review, and digital review, and individualized feedback was provided to each institution. Results A total of 162 specimens were reviewed, including 584 original stained slides, 940 paraffin blocks, and 1,168 digitized slides. At least 54 online review sessions were conducted, and 24 virtual feedback sessions were held. Overall diagnostic concordance across original, central, and digital evaluations was 80% for renal tumors, 90.9% for neuroblastic tumors, and 92.1% for hepatic neoplasms. Common limitations included inconsistent/inadequate sampling and incomplete/erroneous subclassification and reporting. Conclusion Findings confirm strong baseline diagnostic capabilities for common pediatric solid tumors across participating Mexican centers, while highlighting specific gaps in sampling, reporting standardization, and access to ancillary testing. The project facilitated the creation of a pediatric pathology network, demonstrating that a hybrid centralized-digital review model can strengthen specialized pediatric pathology capacity in resource-limited settings.

title: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort.
abstract: Background and objectives Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort. Methods Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers. Results A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (B MCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10 -4 ) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI] indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI] proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p 's < 5.01 × 10 -6 ) and Simoa-Based pTau181 ( p < 4.51 × 10 -15 ) and neurofilament light chain ( p < 5.34 × 10 -7 ). Discussion Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

Methods

Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers.

Results

A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (BMCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10-4) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI]indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI]proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p's < 5.01 × 10-6) and Simoa-Based pTau181 (p < 4.51 × 10-15) and neurofilament light chain (p < 5.34 × 10-7).

Discussion

Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

title: Duplicated Appendix With Mucocele Mimicking an Appendiceal Neoplasm in a 45-Year-Old Woman: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Appendiceal duplication is an extremely rare congenital anomaly, with an incidence of 0.004% to 0.009%. An association with an appendiceal mucocele is even rarer. It can complicate the diagnosis and management of right iliac fossa pathology and remains difficult to identify preoperatively. Failure to recognize it can result in recurrent symptoms, missed pathology, intraoperative challenges, and medicolegal consequences. This report describes the case of a 45-year-old woman with history of a loculated peri-appendiceal abscess managed with percutaneous drainage and intravenous antibiotics, subsequently found to have a duplicated appendix with mucocele identified after right hemicolectomy. CASE REPORT A 45-year-old woman presented with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and fever that began 2 months ago. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated ruptured appendicitis with a loculated peri-appendiceal abscess, successfully managed with percutaneous drainage and intravenous antibiotics, resulting in clinical improvement. She re-presented 2 months later with recurrent abdominal pain. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed a dilated, firm appendiceal tip and a mass-like ileocecal inflammatory complex, raising suspicion of malignancy. Due to the distorted anatomy and inability to exclude an underlying neoplasm, a right hemicolectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed a Type B2 (Cave-Wallbridge) duplication of the appendix, one of which showed mucocele formation and features of resolving appendicitis with no evidence of malignancy. CONCLUSIONS Appendiceal duplication is classified according to the Cave-Wallbridge system and is rarely associated with appendiceal mucocele. Diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion and careful intraoperative assessment. Extended resection may be required when anatomy is distorted or malignancy cannot be excluded, to prevent missed pathology and recurrence.

title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
abstract: Introduction This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. Methods Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups. Results The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

title: Case of Appendiceal Goblet Cell Adenocarcinoma With Gastric Metastasis.
abstract: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma (GCA) is a rare appendiceal neoplasm that typically metastasizes to the peritoneum and pelvic organs, with no reported gastric involvement. We report a 72-year-old man with multiple comorbidities presenting with recurrent small bowel obstruction. Imaging revealed a cecal and a gastric mass; colonoscopy confirmed poorly differentiated right-sided adenocarcinoma. Surgical resection with intraoperative biopsies identified high-grade appendiceal GCA infiltrating the cecum, mesentery, and gastric wall. Immunohistochemical staining showed cytokeratin 7 negativity and cytokeratin 20 positivity, suggesting an appendiceal origin. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of the gastric lesion confirmed gastric metastasis, demonstrating identical morphology and immunoprofile, thus expanding the metastatic spectrum of GCA.

title: Whipple Disease: A Two-Decade Multisystem Masquerade Preceding Gastrointestinal Presentation.
abstract: Whipple disease is a rare multisystem infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei that can present with extraintestinal manifestations preceding gastrointestinal symptoms by years. We report an unusually prolonged course in a patient with nearly 2 decades of treatment-refractory seronegative inflammatory polyarthritis who later developed gastrointestinal symptoms. Although initial upper endoscopy with biopsies was nondiagnostic, repeat evaluation following symptom progression demonstrated small bowel involvement, with diagnosis established by periodic acid-Schiff staining and polymerase chain reaction of small bowel biopsies. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of Whipple disease and the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion in longstanding refractory symptoms and multisystem involvement.

title: The Influence of Contralesional Brain Age Gradients on Chronic Stroke Aphasia Severity and Treatment Response.
abstract: The adult brain follows normative aging trajectories, yet stroke abruptly disrupts this process. Beyond the focal lesion, undamaged regions can deviate from expected aging due to diaschisis or pre-existing vulnerabilities, reflecting tissue health that may constrain recovery. Chronic post-stroke aphasia, a persistent language disorder, shows wide individual variability in severity and treatment response, and these differences are not fully captured by lesion characteristics or demographic factors. Further, prior imaging biomarkers have been difficult to scale because they rely on specialized acquisitions or nonstandardized analytical pipelines. Here, we used a standardized, lifespan-informed brain age model (volBrain) trained on large public datasets to quantify regional deviations from normative aging using only routine structural MRI (T1-weighted). In 188 individuals with chronic stroke (67 female, 121 male), regional aging deviations in the contralesional hemisphere explained aphasia severity beyond lesion volume, lesion location, and basic demographics. In a treated subgroup, baseline brain aging patterns also predicted language gains that persisted 6 months after therapy, indicating prognostic value. By characterizing how individual brains diverge from expected aging, this approach captures variation in tissue integrity that is relevant for both impairment and recovery. This provides a scalable framework that can be integrated across sites and studies, linking normative aging models with post-stroke prognostics and informing precision neurorehabilitation.

title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.

title: Binary Classification of Breast Cancer Images Using CNNs Enhanced by ALO-CLAHE-MSER Preprocessing
abstract: This work presents an intelligent image-processing framework for automatically detecting and clas-sifying benign and malignant regions in breast tissue by integrating Contrast Limited Adaptive His-togram Equalization (CLAHE), Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER), and metaheuristic opti-mization algorithms. Identifying tumor-related regions in breast images is challenging because their visual characteristics can vary considerably with tissue density, illumination conditions, surface tex-ture, intensity distribution, lesion severity, and image acquisition conditions. These variations can make conventional image segmentation and manually configured MSER approaches sensitive to pa-rameter selection and less robust when detecting heterogeneous cancerous regions. To address these limitations, this study highlights the critical role of metaheuristic optimization as a key driver for fully automating and optimizing the combined CLAHE-MSER pipeline for binary breast cancer classifica-tion. Methods: First, CLAHE is applied to the input medical images to improve local contrast and enhance visual differences between healthy and cancerous tissue. The enhanced images are subse-quently processed using the MSER technique to identify stable intensity regions potentially associated with lesions or tumor masses. Rather than relying on manual configuration, the MSER parameter space and enhancement thresholds are formulated as a multidimensional optimization problem, and metaheuristic optimization algorithms are employed to automatically explore the parameter space and determine optimal configurations for region detection. Candidate solutions are iteratively evalu-ated using an objective function designed to improve the quality, stability, spatial coherence, and ac-curacy of the detected tumor regions prior to binary classification. The proposed metaheuristic-driven CLAHE-MSER framework therefore lets the detection process adapt automatically to the visual char-acteristics of individual medical images while eliminating dependence on manually selected parame-ters. Results: We performed experimental evaluations on medical images containing healthy, benign, and malignant regions. We quantitatively evaluated the performance of the proposed CLAHE-MSER framework, optimized by metaheuristic algorithms, using several image-quality, region-detection, and binary classification metrics. The experimental results indicate that incorporating CLAHE improves local contrast and facilitates the identification of subtle differences between healthy and affected tis-sue. Furthermore, metaheuristic optimization significantly improves MSER parameter selection, re-sulting in more consistent and spatially coherent detection of tumor regions than conventional MSER configurations and non-optimized approaches. Metaheuristic optimization serves as the central component to automate and refine the detection process by dynamically identifying suitable parameter configurations for different image conditions. The proposed methodology represents a promising computational ap-proach for automated breast cancer screening, computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), lesion classification, and intelligent medical decision support systems.

title: A Systematic Review and Descriptive Quantitative Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Cervical Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has been frequently utilised in cervical cancer screening, diagnosis, lesion assessment and clinical decision support, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This systematic review examined the application of AI in cytology, colposcopy, visual examination, histopathology, and multimodal clinical data. Also reviewed PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore to identify 4094 records. After the exclusion of 2053 duplicates and applying pre-defined eligibility criteria, 898 studies were included. Directly extractable diagnostic-performance measures were available from 60 studies. Accuracy was reported in 40 studies, sensitivity in 19, specificity in 16 and AUC in 12 studies. A total of 13 studies reported both sensitivity and specificity. There was considerable heterogeneity in populations, datasets, reference standards, diagnostic tasks, AI methods, validation procedures and performance reporting. Complete TP, FP, TN and FN data were not available across the eligible evidence base and pooled diagnostic accuracy estimation and summary receiver-operating-characteristic analysis were not possible. Therefore, the quantitative results were summarized descriptively. Evidence indicates broad application of AI approaches but also limitations in terms of comparability, external validation, reporting completeness and clinical generalizability. Future research should focus on standardized reporting, multicenter datasets, independent external validation and prospective clinical evaluation.

title: An acoustic coupling fluid improves intraoperative ultrasound image quality during glioma surgery: Results of a Pivotal Multicenter Study (NCT04734444)
abstract: Abstract Intraoperative ultrasound uniquely provides repeatable, real-time guidance throughout glioma resection without interrupting surgery. However, image quality deteriorates at resection completion, when imaging is most critical: irrigation fluids attenuate ultrasound less than brain tissue, producing hyperechoic artefacts beneath the cavity that obscure or mimic residual tumour. Existing operator-dependent strategies do not correct this mismatch. Here, we show that SonoClear, a tissue-mimicking acoustic coupling fluid, reduces these artefacts and improves interpretability. In a prospective, non-randomised study at five centres, 44 patients received SonoClear and 40 contributed to paired comparisons with standard irrigation fluid. SonoClear reduced below-cavity artefactual signal (ratio of contrast-to-noise ratios, irrigation/SonoClear: 1.70; 95% CI, 1.48–1.95). Five independent neurosurgeons masked to the fluid reported a mean paired Surgeon Image Rating improvement of 1.96 points (95% CI, 1.80–2.11). No serious adverse events were judged probably or definitely device-related within 30 days; postoperative magnetic resonance imaging showed no major findings in 36 evaluated patients. These findings support acoustic matching to improve ultrasound guidance, including at resection completion; effects on resection extent and patient outcomes require investigation.

title: Successful emicizumab prophylaxis in treatment-refractory acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Abstract Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is a rare bleeding disorder characterized by acquired quantitative or qualitative abnormalities of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and may occur in association with autoimmune disease. Management can be challenging when conventional hemostatic and immunomodulatory therapies fail. We report a 63-year-old man with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and no personal or family history of abnormal bleeding who developed life-threatening hemorrhage following dental extractions, resulting in airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy and red blood cell transfusion. Evaluation demonstrated an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time, markedly reduced factor VIII (FVIII) activity, profoundly decreased VWF antigen and activity, and no detectable FVIII inhibitor. The late onset of bleeding, negative genetic testing, poor VWF recovery following high-dose VWF/FVIII concentrate, and underlying autoimmune disease supported a diagnosis of AVWS. Severe VWF deficiency persisted despite treatment with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Emicizumab was subsequently initiated for prophylactic hemostasis. The patient remained free of spontaneous bleeding despite persistent severe reductions in VWF and FVIII measurements and subsequently underwent upper endoscopy with biopsy and colonoscopy without hemorrhagic complications using adjunctive tranexamic acid. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of RA-associated AVWS successfully managed with emicizumab prophylaxis. This case demonstrates sustained clinical hemostasis with emicizumab in treatment-refractory AVWS associated with RA and supports further investigation of FVIII-mimetic therapy as a potential prophylactic strategy when conventional therapies are ineffective.

title: Synoptic procedural reporting to improve quality indicators in systematic Staging Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS) in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): protocol for an ambispective multi-centre quality improvement study
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate mediastinal staging by systematic staging endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) is essential for prognosticating and guiding management in curative-intent treatment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Narrative procedural reports are often incomplete and inconsistent between clinicians, limiting assessment of procedural quality and meaningful audit. Synoptic (structured, check-list style) reporting has improved documentation completeness and procedural quality in other domains of medicine, and a recent Australian multicentre study demonstrated synoptic reporting significantly improved both report and procedural quality in staging EBUS. This ambispective, international, multicentre study aims to evaluate whether synoptic procedural reporting improves quality indicators of systematic staging EBUS, encompassing both process and outcome measures, and will assess acceptability and feasibility to proceduralists. Methods: This ambispective multicentre, single-arm interventional study will recruit approximately 15 lung cancer services with substantial EBUS procedural volume. Eligible patients will have known or suspected clinical stage IB-IIIC NSCLC undergoing systematic staging EBUS for treatment planning. Each centre will implement a mandated synoptic report requiring documentation for each of the five mediastinal lymph nodes: examination, size of node and biopsy details. Three months of staging procedures will be contributed prior to and following implementation of this reporting practice. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients with a complete staging procedure. Secondary outcomes include PET-occult lymph node metastases detection, nodes sampled, radiologically normal node sampling, inter-site variance, and proceduralist feasibility/acceptability. A sample of 590 patients (295 pre-, 295 post-intervention) provides 80% power to detect an 8% increase in complete staging. Mixed-effects logistic and Poisson regression, with random effect for centre and adjustment for pre-specified baseline case-mix covariates, will be used. Discussion: This study will provide the first international multicentre evaluation of whether synoptic reporting improves procedural completeness and clinically meaningful outcomes in systematic staging EBUS. Demonstrating improved complete staging procedures and PET-occult lymph node detection, with proceduralist acceptability, would support widespread adoption of synoptic reporting as a quality improvement tool, strengthen alignment with WABIP quality frameworks, reduce variance in care, and support more accurate multidisciplinary decision-making for NSCLC patients. Trial registration: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR), ACTRN12625001281482. Registered 18 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

title: From detection to decision: radiographic predictors of clinical complications in 514 supernumerary teeth: A retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Supernumerary teeth exhibit various morphological characteristics and may lead to a range of complications. This study aimed to evaluate radiographic characteristics of supernumerary teeth in children and to determine associations with complications and treatment status. Materials and methods This study included 386 systemically healthy paediatric patients (5–15.9 years) with 514 supernumerary teeth identified on panoramic radiographs. Variables included number, location, morphology, eruption direction, eruption status, root development stage, and complications. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, independent samples t-tests, and multivariable binary logistic and multinomial regression models. Results The mean age was 9.07 ± 2.08 years, and 70.2% of patients were male. Significant differences were observed between erupted and impacted teeth regarding morphology, eruption direction, root development stage, complications, and Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) use (p < 0.05). Morphology and root development stage were associated with complication patterns (p < 0.05). Multivariable regression analyses showed that CBCT use was associated with eruption status, dentition “stage, side distribution, and delayed eruption. Anterior maxillary localisation was strongly associated with conical and tuberculate morphologies. Midline location was associated with increased odds of both complete and partial root development (p < 0.001). Conclusion Supernumerary teeth exhibit distinct radiographic characteristics associated with clinical complications. Morphology, eruption status, and root development were associated with clinical and radiographic findings. Early radiographic evaluation is essential for individualised treatment planning.

title: Functional and MRI improvement followed by a mixed trajectory during cannabinoid-terpenoid exposure in glioblastoma: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Glioblastoma has limited salvage options, while viable tumour, treatment injury, postoperative change, oedema and corticosteroid effects may produce overlapping clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings. Materials and Methods: Clinical records, serial MRI examinations and signed radiology reports were reviewed descriptively for a patient with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-promoter-methylated glioblastoma. The exposure history and contemporaneously documented neurological findings were aligned with seven MRI time points. No blinded central review, standardised volumetry or formal RANO 2.0 adjudication was performed. Results: After two operations, radiotherapy, concomitant temozolomide and three adjuvant cycles, serial MRI documented progression before April 2025. During a non-standard exposure state comprising intranasal perillyl alcohol and alpha-bisabolol, individualised cannabinoids and docosahexaenoic acid/medium-chain triglyceride oil, with dexamethasone fixed at 2 mg/day, hemiplegia/KPS 50 improved to hemiparesis with regained walking/KPS 80, coinciding with reduced enhancement. Later MRI showed increasing right temporal and cerebellar enhancement, including a new contralateral cerebellar focus, despite substantially stable postoperative cavity and T2/FLAIR extent. June 2026 lesion perfusion curves were low-amplitude without pathological hyperperfusion. The patient subsequently died after an overall survival of 45 months. Conclusions: This uncontrolled case documents early functional and radiological improvement on a stable corticosteroid background, followed by an anatomically progressive but biologically indeterminate trajectory. It does not establish treatment causality, survival benefit, formal tumour response or component-specific efficacy; mixed viable tumour and treatment effect or radiation necrosis could not be excluded. Although this single case does not establish a verified benefit the observed overall survival reached a time span of extraordinarily 45 months.

title: Neural correlates of empathy in autism: a coordinate-based meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose . Autistic and non-autistic people often differ in how readily they understand one another’s intentions and emotional states. Although empathy is commonly invoked to explain these differences, which components of empathic processing differ in autism, and their neural underpinnings, remain unclear. Methods . We conducted a pre-registered coordinate-based meta-analysis (activation likelihood estimation; ALE) of task-based fMRI studies of empathy in autism, examining within-group convergence, conjunction and between-group divergence separately for affective and cognitive components. Eleven studies (12 independent samples) met inclusion criteria, comprising 213 autistic and 216 non-autistic participants and 600 foci across 35 experiments; a multi-agent AI second reviewer supported screening and extraction. Results . Both groups shared a core empathy network (precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex, right middle temporal gyrus/posterior superior temporal sulcus, left inferior frontal gyrus, dorsomedial paracingulate), but the rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a canonical cognitive-empathy hub, converged only in non-autistic participants. The between-group contrast was strongly asymmetric: non-autistic participants exceeded autistic convergence in ten regions, eight of them cognitive-empathy nodes, the largest in rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; autistic participants exceeded non-autistic convergence in one region only, the posterior right temporoparietal junction. Subdomain analyses indicated relatively preserved convergence for affective empathy, with sparser, more diffuse overlap for cognitive empathy. Conclusion . These findings are consistent with a dissociation between relatively preserved affective and altered cognitive empathy in autism, and suggest a redistribution of activation within the mentalizing network rather than a global absence of empathy-related processing. Key words: autism spectrum disorder; empathy; activation likelihood estimation; functional magnetic resonance imaging; dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; temporoparietal junction

title: Cross-Domain Chest Radiograph Report Generation Under Dataset Shift: Bidirectional Audit Study.
abstract: Background Cross-domain chest radiograph report generation may produce formally valid reports that are nevertheless repetitive, weakly case-specific, or missing clinically relevant findings. These failures can be missed when evaluation relies on a single language-overlap or clinical-label score. Objective This study aimed to evaluate cross-domain report generation with a bidirectional layered audit, characterize direction-specific and end point-specific failure profiles under a composite training-side control and 3 decoding policies, and explore whether selected audit dimensions remained informative for a contemporary medical vision language model. Methods A fixed R2Gen-style system was evaluated bidirectionally on 575 IU X-ray and 401 MIMIC-CXR (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care Chest X-Ray) target records. The audit included surface validity, complete-report recurrence and concentration, a predefined prefix end point, lexical diversity, official Stanford CheXpert/NegBio labels, paired cluster-bootstrap inference, and blinded review by 2 medical trainees. The primary human audit included 210 reports from 70 randomly sampled cases, with blinded adjudication of unresolved primary end point disagreements. A 60-report targeted panel was used for failure-mode analysis. Separately, a fixed MedGemma 1.5 4B configuration generated reports for all 976 records. Results In MIMIC-CXR-to-IU X-ray transfer, out of 575 reports, ON (protocol-defined training-side control enabled)+B4 (beam search with a beam size of 4) reduced the predefined recurrent prefix from 575 (100%) to 8 (1.4%; Holm-adjusted P =.002). However, 569 (99.0%) ON+B4 outputs still belonged to exact duplicate groups. In IU X-ray-to-MIMIC-CXR transfer, the 14-category CheXpert/NegBio micro- F 1 was higher for ON+B4 than for OFF (protocol-defined training-side control disabled)+B4 (0.1687 vs 0.0744; Holm-adjusted P =.01). This apparent advantage was not broad-based: after cardiomegaly was excluded in a post hoc descriptive sensitivity analysis, the difference changed from +0.0944 to -0.0610. Text-level tracing showed that the original contrast was mainly driven by a labeler response to recurrent, semantically normal heart-size wording. Across the primary human-audit cells, major omissions occurred in 12 to 15 out of 35 reports, and major unsupported findings occurred in 10 to 16 of 35 reports, with no consistent configuration ordering observed. The exploratory MedGemma micro- F 1 was 0.4722 on IU X-ray and 0.4340 on MIMIC-CXR, but 381 out of 575 (66.3%) IU outputs belonged to exact duplicate groups. Conclusions No configuration performed consistently well across end points, and no single metric captured all forms of cross-domain degradation. The MedGemma stress test suggested that recurrence and label-traceability checks remain useful across architectures, although it was not a matched performance comparison. Cross-domain report generators should undergo bidirectional evaluation, final-text verification, and image-grounded human review before external validation or clinical deployment.

title: Arthroscopy-Validated Diagnostic Performance of a Deep Learning Reconstruction Pipeline for Rapid 7-Minute Five-Sequence 3-T Knee MRI.
abstract: BACKGROUND. Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) methods can enhance image quality and reduce scan time of knee MRI compared with conventional approaches but require validation against independent reference standards to ensure robustness and accuracy. OBJECTIVE. The purpose of this study was to assess the diagnostic performance of a two- to threefold parallel imaging-accelerated 7-minute five-sequence 3-T knee MRI protocol using a deep learning-based image reconstruction pipeline (AIR Recon DL, GE HealthCare), with arthroscopic surgery as the reference standard. METHODS. A total of 117 consecutive adult patients (mean age: 44 ± 16 [SD] years; 65 men, 52 women) with painful knee conditions who underwent DLR 3-T knee MRI and arthroscopic knee surgery with a median MRI-to-surgery interval of 35 days (range: 5-88 days) between June 2021 and May 2024 were retrospectively identified and included. MRI studies were independently reviewed by seven musculoskeletal radiologists for image quality parameters using Likert scales (range: 1 [very bad] to 5 [very good]) and the presence of meniscus tears, cruciate and collateral ligament tears, and articular cartilage defects. Statistical analyses included interreader agreements and diagnostic performance testing. RESULTS. Overall image quality of DLR knee MRI scans was good (median: 4 [IQR, 4-5]), with minimal image noise (median: 4 [IQR, 4-4]), good edge sharpness (median: 4 [IQR, 4-5]), absence of reconstruction artifacts (median: 5 [IQR, 4-5]), and high interreader agreement for all quality metrics (κ ≥ 0.83). Diagnostic performance for detecting arthroscopy-validated structural abnormalities was good to excellent (AUC ≥ 0.81) with good to very good interreader agreement (κ ≥ 0.62). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and AUC values were 89%, 87%, 88%, and 0.87 for medial meniscus tears (prevalence at arthroscopy: 78/117, 67%); 72%, 91%, 83%, and 0.82 for lateral meniscus tears (prevalence at arthroscopy: 50/117, 43%); 97%, 98%, 97%, and 0.97 for anterior cruciate ligament tears (prevalence at arthroscopy: 30/117, 26%); and 73%, 89%, 86%, and 0.81 for articular cartilage defects (prevalence at arthroscopy: 182/702, 26%). CONCLUSION. Clinical 7-minute five-sequence 3-T knee MRI with DLR provides good to excellent diagnostic performance for detecting arthroscopy-validated internal derangement of the knee. CLINICAL IMPACT. DLR enables rapid high-quality clinical 3-T knee MRI with high diagnostic performance for arthroscopy-validated abnormalities.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of computed tomography in patients with non-specific symptoms of cancer referred directly from general practice: a retrospective follow-up study.
abstract: Background The urgent-referral Cancer Patient Pathway for Non-Specific Symptoms and Signs of Cancer (NSSC-CPP) was introduced in Denmark in 2012 to reduce delays in cancer diagnoses. In Region Zealand, it includes direct referral from GPs to contrast-enhanced computed tomography of thorax, abdomen, and pelvis (ceCT-TAP). In 2013, the NSSC-CPP cancer prevalence was 20%, but easy access to computed tomography (CT) may change referral patterns. Aim To examine cancer prevalence, diagnostic accuracy of ceCT-TAP, and changes in NSSC-CPP referral patterns. Design and setting Retrospective cohort study conducted in Region Zealand, Denmark. Method We included patients with non-specific symptoms or signs of cancer who were referred by GPs between 1 July and 31 December 2019. Primary endpoints were cancer prevalence and diagnostic accuracy of ceCT-TAP. Secondary endpoints were cancer types, referral trends between 2012 and 2019, and prevalence of GP-reported symptoms and clinical findings. Patients were followed up until cancer diagnosis or up to 12 months after ceCT-TAP, whichever came first. Results In total, 729 referrals were recorded, a five-fold increase compared with 140 referrals in the same period of 2013. Malignancy was diagnosed in 95 (13%) patients. Twelve patients had a false-negative ceCT-TAP result, yielding a negative likelihood ratio (LR) for malignancy of 0.15. Conclusion Despite a five-fold increase in GP referrals for ceCT-TAP since 2012, it remains an important diagnostic tool, identifying malignancy in one in seven patients. However, as the LR- was >0.10, a normal ceCT-TAP does not convincingly rule out cancer and should not stand alone as the only decision-support tool.

title: An Automated Framework Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging Feature Masking and Support Vector Machine for Schizophrenia Classification.
abstract: Automated classification of schizophrenia can improve the quality of life for people with schizophrenia and reduce social costs. At present, however, the usual standards for diagnosing mental illnesses are still based on the subjective assessment of psychiatrists and lack objective quantitative biomarkers for early detection. Neuroimaging-based machine learning has achieved some success, but the existing models have not addressed the high dimensionality of small-sample magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies. These data characteristics are prone to sub-optimal automatic feature extraction and weak out-of-sample generalization. Based on the above problems, an automated classification pipeline that combines MRI feature engineering with a support vector machine (SVM) classifier to accurately differentiate patients with schizophrenia is introduced. First, to address inter-subject anatomical differences, comprehensive brain preprocessing and spatial alignment were performed. Then, intensity-based statistical features were derived from the preprocessed volumes, reduced in the input space via background masking to remove non-brain tissues, and subsequently aggregated into atlas-based regional features. A refined feature matrix is then fed into an SVM to construct the optimal separating hyperplane for final classification. This study adopted an 80:20 train-test split strategy, with five-fold cross-validation performed exclusively on the training set for model selection and hyperparameter tuning, followed by final performance evaluation on the held-out test set. Using the public COBRE dataset, the final SVM model achieved an accuracy of 96.7% on the held-out test set. This framework is expected to evolve into an objective, data-driven auxiliary diagnostic tool for schizophrenia and to provide timely treatment decision support in clinical practice.

title: Comparative Clinical Impact of Transbronchial Cryobiopsy and Forceps Biopsy Utilizing Radial EBUS Guidance for the Diagnosis of Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions.
abstract: Background The prevalence of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) is increasing; however, their diagnosis remains challenging despite the availability of various modalities. Transbronchial cryobiopsy (TBCB) offers an additive benefit in diagnostic yield. Combining radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-EBUS)-guided transbronchial forceps biopsy (TBFB) with cryobiopsy may enhance tissue acquisition. Methods This retrospective study reviewed 197 patients with pulmonary lesions who underwent bronchoscopy-guided biopsy between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2023. Strict diagnostic yield and diagnostic accuracy were calculated according to the predefined definition, and the additive impact of cryobiopsy was further analyzed. Results The cohort comprised 117 patients in the TBFB group and 80 in the TBCB group. The overall mean age was 68 years and 60% were male; baseline lesion characteristics were comparable across groups, with lesions <20 mm in 45% and 44% of the TBFB and TBCB groups, respectively, and a positive CT bronchus sign in 82% and 85%. Compared with TBFB alone, the TBCB group achieved a higher strict diagnostic yield (76.2% vs. 63.2%) and diagnostic accuracy (86.8% vs. 80.4%), respectively. Among the 33 patients in whom R-EBUS-guided TBFB was followed sequentially by cryobiopsy, the addition of cryobiopsy further increased diagnostic yield and accuracy by 21.6% and 13.5%, respectively. Procedure-related severe bleeding and severe hypoxia occurred in 2.5% and 1.3% of patients in the TBCB group, both significantly higher than the corresponding rates in the TBFB group (p < 0.05). Conclusion R-EBUS-guided TBCB demonstrated efficacy for diagnosing PPLs, offering superior diagnostic yield and accuracy than conventional R-EBUS-guided transbronchial lung biopsy alone.

title: Clinical and radiological comparisons of posterior labral tears with and without posterior glenohumeral instability.
abstract: Background We compare clinical and radiological characteristics and evaluate surgical outcomes of posterior labral tears based on the presence of glenohumeral instability. Methods Patients who were unresponsive to conservative treatment and underwent arthroscopic posterior labral repair were reviewed retrospectively. Patients were divided into two groups: those with glenohumeral instability (group 1) and those without (group 2). Demographic, radiological, physical examination, and intraoperative data were collected. Clinical outcomes were assessed at a minimum 2-year follow-up using the visual analog scale for pain, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons, and Rowe scores. Results The study included a total of 85 patients (40 in group 1 and 45 in group 2) with a mean follow-up duration of 31.8±12.2 months. Patients in group 2 were older (31.4±1.0 years old, P<0.001), had longer symptom durations (30.1±5.6 months, P=0.002), and included fewer histories of trauma (16 patients, P=0.009). Competitive sports were more common in group 1 (9 patients, P=0.005), whereas weightlifting exercises were more common in group 2 (24 patients, P=0.047). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) underestimated incomplete posterior labral tears more frequently in group 2 than in group 1 (P=0.033). The incidence of arthroscopically detected tears among MRI-occult tears was higher in group 2 (10 patients) than in group 1 (2 patients, P=0.029). Statistically significant improvements in shoulder function were observed postoperatively in both groups. Conclusions Clinical and magnetic resonance findings of posterior labral tears without glenohumeral instability differ from those with instability. Surgical treatment achieved satisfactory clinical outcomes regardless of the presence of instability. Level of evidence: III.

title: Prehospital point-of-care ultrasound as a decision-support tool: A structured narrative review.
abstract: Background Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may support focused bedside decisions, but prehospital implementation remains limited by operational constraints, heterogeneous protocols, variable training, and limited outcome-focused evidence. This narrative review examines prehospital POCUS as a clinical decision-support tool across cardiac, thoracic, trauma, pediatric, and obstetric applications. Methods A structured narrative review was conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from April 2017 to February 2026. Search terms combined the prehospital setting, ultrasound, and clinical applications. Of 464 records identified, 38 full-text articles were included, including nine systematic reviews on cardiac evaluation (n = 2), thoracic evaluation (n = 3), and trauma assessment (n = 4). Screening and full-text assessment were performed by a single reviewer. No formal risk-of-bias assessment, certainty grading, quantitative synthesis, or meta-analysis was performed. Results In cardiac arrest, prehospital POCUS may identify cardiac activity and selected reversible causes, guide interventions, confirm return of spontaneous circulation, and support prognostic assessment, provided that image acquisition does not interrupt resuscitation or delay defibrillation. In nontraumatic shock and cardiac dysfunction, focused cardiac, lung, and vascular ultrasound may help characterize shock mechanisms, guide fluid therapy, and identify actionable findings such as pulmonary congestion, pericardial effusion, right ventricular strain, or major aortic pathology. In acute dyspnea, lung ultrasound may improve diagnostic confidence, particularly for cardiogenic pulmonary edema. In trauma, E-FAST has high specificity and may support triage, destination choice, trauma pathway activation, and preparation for definitive care; however, limited sensitivity prevents its use as a rule-out test. Pediatric and obstetric applications are feasible but remain emerging. Conclusions Prehospital POCUS is an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Its value lies in answering actionable questions that may influence treatment, triage, transport destination, hospital prealert, or pathway activation. Implementation requires protocols, training, quality assurance, and governance, and must not delay time-critical care or transport.

title: FreqFuseNet: Scale-Normalized Dual-Frequency Fusion for Thin-Wall Head-and-Neck OAR Segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of thin-wall organs-at-risk (OARs) in head-and-neck computed tomography (CT) is challenging because small contour deviations can substantially affect boundary agreement. We present FreqFuseNet, a segmentation architecture with a fast Fourier transform (FFT) primary branch and a frequency channel attention network (FcaNet) residual branch that explicitly aligns heterogeneous frequency-feature scales before bounded residual fusion. An initialization-time analysis revealed an approximately 863-fold activation-scale disparity between the two branches, corresponding to an approximately 43-fold unintended residual-to-primary magnitude ratio under naive fusion with a nominal coefficient of 0.05. FreqFuseNet uses per-sample, per-channel scale alignment to preserve the intended relative amplitude without additional normalization parameters.
