title: Multi-parametric MRI radiomics to predict sensitivity to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy based on multi-regions of interest in locally advanced rectal cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background To evaluate whether baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models, integrating multiple regions of interest (ROIs), can predict pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), and to validate performance externally. Methods In this multicenter, retrospective cohort study, 510 patients with LARC treated with NCRT followed by total mesorectal excision were enrolled (330 for training, 83 for internal validation, and 97 for external validation). Radiomic features were extracted from three ROIs (primary tumor, mesorectal region, and lateral lymph node regions). After redundancy reduction and clustering, the top 30 features were selected using gradient boosting decision trees via cross-validation. Four classifiers, logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and extra trees, were evaluated, with SMOTE applied to address class imbalance. Model performance was compared across ROI combinations, MRI sequences, and algorithms using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Overall, 98 of 510 patients (19.2%) achieved pCR. The multi-ROI, multi-parametric model based on extra trees achieved an AUC of 0.717 in the external validation set. Among single-ROI models, tumor ROI yielded the highest AUC (0.630). Among MRI sequences, the ADC-based model performed best (AUC 0.629). Conclusion Baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models integrating multiple ROIs showed modest predictive performance for pCR in LARC and demonstrated similar predictive utility in an independent external cohort. This approach may provide pre-treatment risk stratification and support future research on individualized treatment strategies and organ preservation.

title: Venous wash-out at contrast-enhanced ultrasound for the identification of hematologic splenic lesions: an exploratory real-world substudy.
abstract: Purpose Splenic lesions are a relatively rare but clinically relevant finding in internal medicine practice, particularly when hematologic or lymphoproliferative disorders are suspected. The aim of this exploratory subanalysis was to evaluate the role of CEUS perfusion patterns, with particular attention to venous wash-out and its timing, in discriminating between hematologic and non-hematologic disease in a real-world Internal Medicine cohort. Methods An exploratory retrospective subanalysis was conducted on patients included in the intervention arm of a multicenter Quality Improvement study evaluating a structured contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS)-based diagnostic pathway in newly identified splenic lesions. Consecutive adult patients with newly detected splenic lesions identified on B-mode ultrasound who underwent CEUS as part of the initial diagnostic evaluation were included. CEUS perfusion patterns were qualitatively classified according to arterial wash-in, venous wash-out, and wash-out timing. The diagnostic reference standard consisted of histologic and/or cytologic examination when available, or integration of clinical, laboratory, and imaging follow-up data within 90 days. In patients without histologic confirmation, non-hematologic classification required clinical and laboratory stability or improvement, stability or resolution of the splenic lesion on follow-up imaging, identification of an alternative non-hematologic diagnosis when present, and absence of a hematologic diagnosis during the 90-day follow-up. In line with the parent study, one patient in the intervention-arm cohort did not receive a definitive lesion-specific etiologic diagnosis within 90 days; however, no patient remained indeterminate for the prespecified binary endpoint because classification as hematologic versus non-hematologic was possible in all cases. The study endpoint was binary diagnostic classification (hematologic vs non-hematologic). Results Fifty patients were included, of whom 11 (22%) had a hematologic diagnosis and 39 (78%) had a non-hematologic diagnosis. In univariable analysis, multiple lesions, systemic symptoms, and especially venous wash-out were associated with hematologic diagnosis. Venous wash-out was present in 10/11 hematologic cases and in 3/39 non-hematologic cases. In hematologic cases, wash-out was almost always early (< 60 s), whereas in the few non-hematologic cases with wash-out it was late. In the exploratory multivariable model, venous wash-out was the only variable independently associated with hematologic diagnosis. Because of the small number of hematologic events, this association should be interpreted as statistically unstable and hypothesis-generating. Venous wash-out showed a sensitivity of 90.9%, specificity of 92.3%, positive predictive value of 76.9%, negative predictive value of 97.3%, and accuracy of 92.0%. Conclusion In patients with newly identified splenic lesions, venous wash-out at CEUS, particularly if early, was the pattern most strongly associated with hematologic diagnosis in this cohort. The absence of wash-out was associated with a low probability of hematologic disease, suggesting a possible utility of CEUS in diagnostic rule-out in real-world Internal Medicine settings. However, diagnostic performance estimates, particularly negative predictive value, should be interpreted cautiously in view of the low prevalence of hematologic disease and the exploratory sample size. These findings require confirmation in larger cohorts.

title: Utility of ultrasonography for articular cartilage assessment in knee osteoarthritis: a comparative study with clinical scores and magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Objective To assess the utility of ultrasonography in evaluating femoral articular cartilage in knee osteoarthritis and to determine the relationship between sonographic cartilage abnormalities and clinical pain scores. Methods A prospective study was conducted on 63 clinically diagnosed knee osteoarthritis patients (126 knees) and 30 age-matched controls (60 knees). All participants underwent clinical evaluation and ultrasonography by two reviewers. Cartilage thickness and morphological abnormalities were assessed using a semi-quantitative sonographic grading system. Pain severity was evaluated using the visual analogue scale (VAS), and the relationship between sonographic cartilage grade and clinical pain was statistically analysed. A subgroup of 18 knees also underwent MRI for exploratory comparison of cartilage grading. Results Cartilage abnormalities were detected by USG in 97% of OA knees compared to 50% of controls (p < 0.001). Medial condyle cartilage was significantly thinner in osteoarthritis knees (1.48[95% CI 1.37-1.60] mm) than controls (1.74[95% CI 1.59-1.88] mm, p = 0.027). Interrater agreement was almost perfect (Quadratic weighted Cohen Kappa was 0.89[95% CI 0.93-0.97). Higher cartilage grades (≥ 2B) on USG had significantly higher VAS scores compared to low cartilage grade (< 2B) (p < 0.001). USG showed fair agreement (Quadratic weighted Kappa = 0.40[95% CI 0.9-0.72] in detection of all cartilage abnormalities with MRI, however it underestimated severity compared to MRI (≥ Grade 2B in 67% vs. 95%). Conclusion Ultrasound is a reliable, accessible tool for detecting femoral cartilage changes in knee osteoarthritis, showing significant correlation with clinical symptoms. Its affordability, safety, and dynamic capabilities make it a valuable adjunct for initial assessment and monitoring in routine clinical practice.

title: Discovery of benzoxazole derivatives as novel α-synuclein aggregate ligands with potential for PET tracer development.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, and the abnormal aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) constitutes its core pathological hallmark. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of cerebral α-Syn aggregates holds great promise for the early diagnosis of PD. However, the imaging quality critically depends on the ligands with high binding affinity and selectivity for α-Syn aggregates. In this work, we developed a new type of benzoxazole-based α-Syn aggregate ligands via an SPR-based screening. Among them, candidates D15 (K D = 0.12 μM) and D16 (K D = 0.08 μM) exhibited high binding affinities for α-Syn aggregates in vitro and good potency in the SH-SY5Y cellular model and brain tissues from α-Syn PFF-injected PD mouse models, as well as excellent selectivity for tau and Aβ aggregates in rTg4510 and APP23 transgenic mouse brain sections. Thanks to their favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and suitable structures for radiolabeling for PET imaging, these new ligands represent promising candidates for the development of α-Syn PET radiotracers, offering a valuable foundation for the early diagnosis of PD and related synucleinopathies.

title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [ 68 Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

title: Toward truly agentic radiology AI: A multimodal architecture framework and differentiated implementation roadmap.
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence(AI) represents a structural transition from task-specific tools to autonomous systems capable of goal-oriented, multi-step reasoning. However, translating this potential into radiology requires a fundamental shift from text-dominated architectures to avision-first approachthat engages the specialty's diagnostic core. In this paper, we characterize the multimodal challenge distinguishing radiology from text-centric domains, where high-dimensional images serve as the primary diagnostic substrate rather than supplementary data. We reviewthree image-text coupling architectures, their clinical capabilities, limitations, and deployment feasibility. These include output-level coupling through sequential image-text pipelines, representation-level coupling through contrastive aligned dual encoders, and token-level coupling through generative vision-language models. To guide development, we introduce afive-level taxonomy of autonomy(Levels 1-5), establishing clear validation checkpoints and regulatory expectations for increasing machine independence, from text-based workflow automation to fully autonomous closed-loop systems. We emphasize that interoperability via standardized protocols, includingDICOMweb, HL7-FHIR, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A), is as critical as the AI models themselves. Finally, we address critical implementation guardrails, including mitigatingalgorithmic hallucinations, defending againstadversarial prompt injection, and preserving human diagnostic proficiency amidst the risk of AI-induced skill decay. This comprehensive roadmap provides a structured path for integrating autonomous visual reasoning into modern medical imaging environments.

title: Systems pharmacology reveals the molecular mechanisms of nerolidol against polycystic ovary syndrome through integrated transcriptomic, network pharmacology and experimental validation.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder marked by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation and oxidative stress, arising from dysregulation across several interconnected molecular pathways. Because its pathogenesis is multifactorial, therapies targeting diverse biological processes at once remain scarce. Nerolidol, a naturally occurring sesquiterpene alcohol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties, has an action against PCOS whose molecular basis remains unresolved. Transcriptomic differences associated with PCOS were examined using the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) dataset GSE34526. Exploratory differential-expression screening identified nominally altered probes using an unadjusted P < 0.05 and |log 2 FC| > 1; however, no individual probe remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR < 0.05. Functional enrichment analysis was subsequently used to investigate biological processes and pathways represented by these exploratory transcriptional signals. Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment were applied to pinpoint dysregulated biological processes and signalling pathways. Computational findings were tested in a letrozole-induced PCOS rat model treated with nerolidol, with efficacy judged from oestrous cyclicity, ovarian histopathology, reproductive hormone profiles, oxidative stress biomarkers, inflammatory mediators and metabolic parameters. Transcriptomic analysis showed marked enrichment of processes related to kinase regulation, insulin secretion, intrinsic apoptotic signalling, receptor-mediated signalling and the DNA damage response, while KEGG analysis pointed to pathways governing endocrine regulation, cell signalling and metabolic homeostasis. In animal experiments, nerolidol restored oestrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, corrected endocrine disturbances, and reduced oxidative stress and PCOS-related pathology. These phenotypic effects were functionally concordant with several biological processes highlighted by the computational analyses. However, because the predicted signalling molecules and pathways were not directly measured in ovarian tissue following nerolidol treatment, the proposed molecular mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring targeted experimental validation.

title: Right putaminal gray matter change tracks psychomotor recovery after accelerated iTBS in melancholic treatment-resistant depression.
abstract: Background Psychomotor retardation is a prominent and disabling feature of melancholic depression. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) may hasten antidepressant effects, but neural substrates of early symptom improvement remain unclear. Given the central role of frontostriatal circuitry in motivation and behavioral activation, structural alterations in the striatum may represent a possible neural substrate of early therapeutic change. Methods Structural MRI was acquired from 61 patients with melancholic TRD and 77 healthy controls, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess baseline striatal gray matter volume differences. Patients then underwent a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of left dorsolateral prefrontal aiTBS, comprising 20 sessions over four days. In 50 patients with complete pre- and post-treatment data, we tested whether GMV change in the baseline-identified striatal region was associated with clinical change in the active and sham groups (n = 25 each). Results Patients showed greater right putamen GMV than controls at baseline. After active aiTBS, greater right putamen GMV increase was associated with greater psychomotor retardation improvement. This association was absent after sham stimulation and was not observed for overall depression severity. Conclusion The right putamen appears structurally altered in melancholic TRD. After active aiTBS, short-term putamen GMV increase was associated with psychomotor rather than broader depressive improvement. This pattern should not be interpreted as structural normalization but may reflect a relationship between putaminal change and early psychomotor recovery.
originalAbstract:
Background

Psychomotor retardation is a prominent and disabling feature of melancholic depression. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) may hasten antidepressant effects, but neural substrates of early symptom improvement remain unclear. Given the central role of frontostriatal circuitry in motivation and behavioral activation, structural alterations in the striatum may represent a possible neural substrate of early therapeutic change.

Methods

Structural MRI was acquired from 61 patients with melancholic TRD and 77 healthy controls, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess baseline striatal gray matter volume differences. Patients then underwent a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of left dorsolateral prefrontal aiTBS, comprising 20 sessions over four days. In 50 patients with complete pre- and post-treatment data, we tested whether GMV change in the baseline-identified striatal region was associated with clinical change in the active and sham groups (n = 25 each).

Results

Patients showed greater right putamen GMV than controls at baseline. After active aiTBS, greater right putamen GMV increase was associated with greater psychomotor retardation improvement. This association was absent after sham stimulation and was not observed for overall depression severity.

Conclusion

The right putamen appears structurally altered in melancholic TRD. After active aiTBS, short-term putamen GMV increase was associated with psychomotor rather than broader depressive improvement. This pattern should not be interpreted as structural normalization but may reflect a relationship between putaminal change and early psychomotor recovery.

title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement Findings in Isolated Left Ventricular Dilatation and Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Background Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and isolated left ventricular dilatation (ILVD) are defined as left ventricular (LV) dilatation, with reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), respectively. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) findings, including LGE extent, location, and number of areas to predict all-cause death in ILVD and DCM, separately. Methods Between 2008 and 2021, we conducted a bicentric retrospective study including all consecutive ILVD and DCM patients referred for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). The primary outcome was all-cause death. A propensity-score matching was performed to balance characteristics between ILVD and DCM populations. Cox regressions were performed to determine the prognostic value of each LGE feature. Results Of 2,752 patients (age 52±8 years, 56% males), 408 (15%) patients died after a median (interquartile range) follow-up of 9 (7-12) years, including 268 (16%) of 1,668 DCM patients and 140 (13%) of 1,084 ILVD patients. Overall, 737 (27%) patients had LGE, including 472 (28%) of 1,668 DCM patients and 265 (24%) of 1,084 ILVD patients. After propensity-score matching, in ILVD patients with LGE (N=265), the LGE extent (hazard ratio [HR] 1.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.78, p=0.015), multiple LGE areas (HR=3.39, 95% CI: 1.66-6.92, p<0.001), and its septal location (HR=2.68, 95% CI: 1.59-4.52, p<0.001) were strong prognosticators of death after adjustment. Similarly, after propensity-score matching, in DCM patients with LGE (N=277), the LGE extent (HR=1.39, 95% CI: 1.06-1.83, p=0.018), multiple LGE areas (HR=2.70, 95% CI: 1.20-6.08, p=0.017), and its septal location (HR=2.82, 95% CI: 1.47-5.41, p=0.002) were strongly associated with death. The CMR LGE score performed well in participants with LGE (area under the curve [AUC] at 10 years, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.69-0.89]). Conclusions LGE findings were strongly and independently associated with death in both ILVD and DCM patients, with each successive LGE characteristic providing significant incremental prognostic value beyond traditional prognosticators, including LVEF.

title: Histological Stages of Appendicitis Associated With Imaging Characteristics: A Computed Tomography and Ultrasound-Based Comparative Study.
abstract: Introduction Appendicitis diagnosis relies heavily on medical imaging procedure studies; however, a definite diagnosis is obtained through histological assessment. Understanding the imaging characteristics and their relation to various histological phases enhance the quality of treatment recommendations. This study analyzed imaging characteristics of acute appendicitis in relation to its histological severity. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted using data from a third-level hospital. Appendectomy specimens from patients with prior computed tomography (CT) scans or ultrasound (US) imaging were included. Histological stages were categorized into simple, suppurative, abscessed, and perforated phases, depending the presence of edema, vascular congestion, neutrophilic infiltrate into the muscular layer, microabscess formation, mucosal ulceration, purulent exudate, macroscopic pus, and perforation with transmural inflammation. Imaging features as fat stranding, presence of free fluid, contrast enhancement within the appendix, appendicolith detection, reactive lymph nodes in the vicinity, appendix diameter itself, increased echogenicity, and detecting heightened perfusion via Doppler imaging were compared across these stages. Results Among 760 patients included (51.4% women, mean age 30.1 ± 5.3), 196 (25.8%) had CT scans and 361 (47.5%) had US. CT confirmed appendicitis in 59.2% of cases, yielded a negative result in 19.4%, and provided an inconclusive diagnosis in 21.4% of cases, commonly identifying fat stranding, free liquid, and contrast enhancement. US diagnosed appendicitis in 67.6% of cases, whereas 32.4% were reported as negative, with findings including increased echogenicity, Doppler perfusion, appendix identification, and free liquid in the right parietocolic gutter. All imaging characteristics were less prevalent in early stages compared to advanced stages, with a higher negativity rate in earlier stages. Conclusions Imaging findings are associated with the histopathological severity of appendicitis. Increased histopathological severity is associated with greater frequency of CT and US findings. These relations suggest the potential for managing appendicitis based on the histological phase suspected from imaging findings. Further research is warranted.

title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.
originalAbstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.

title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

title: [Translated article] Accuracy of the Akmese sign as a diagnostic method for posterior root tears of the medial meniscus in Peruvian healthcare facilities.
abstract: Background Medial meniscus injuries are the most prevalent knee injuries, frequently causing pain, instability, and orthopaedic surgeries. Although several clinical tests are used for meniscal pathology, most were developed for general meniscal lesions rather than specifically for medial meniscus posterior root tears (MMPRT). Evidence on root-specific physical examination signs remains limited. Recently, the Akmese manoeuvre has been introduced as a non-invasive diagnostic tool, assessing pain or tenderness during physical examination. This study aimed to determine the accuracy of the Akmese sign for the clinical diagnosis of MMPRT. Methods This prospective cohort diagnostic study included patients aged 18-55 years scheduled for arthroscopic surgery following a clinical diagnosis of medial meniscus injury between January 2022 and July 2023. Diagnostic performance metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV), and likelihood ratios (LR+, LR-), were calculated, using arthroscopy as the reference standard. The interobserver reliability of the Akmese manoeuvre was assessed using the kappa coefficient. Results A total of 201 individuals met the eligibility criteria, with a mean age of 38.4 ± 9.8 years. The Akmese sign was positive in 26 patients, and MMPRT was confirmed by arthroscopy in 28 patients. The Akmese sign demonstrated a sensitivity of 85.7%, specificity of 98.8%, PPV of 92.3%, NPV of 97.7%, LR+ of 74.1, and a LR- of 0.15. Conclusion In this selected surgical population, the Akmese manoeuvre showed promising diagnostic performance and very good interobserver reliability for identifying MMPRT. The sign may be useful as an adjunctive clinical tool to support preoperative suspicion, targeted MRI review, and surgical planning, but it should not be considered a replacement for MRI or arthroscopic assessment.

title: Foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle as a predictor of reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease: A comparative study with muscle mass and pulmonary function.
abstract: Background Reduced exercise capacity, measured by the 6-min walk distance (6MWD), is a critical prognostic factor in interstitial lung disease (ILD). However, conventional physiological markers often fail to identify early functional decline. We aimed to evaluate whether the foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle (F-F PhA), a non-invasive surrogate marker of muscle quality, predicts reduced exercise capacity better than traditional muscle mass and pulmonary function indices. Methods In this retrospective study of 68 patients with ILD, F-F PhA was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and erector spinae muscle area (ESM_CSA) via computed tomography. Reduced exercise capacity was defined as 6MWD < 450 m. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and pulmonary function (%DL CO or %FVC), with internal validation performed via 1000-resample bootstrapping. Results In multivariable analysis, F-F PhA was independently associated with a 6MWD < 450 m when adjusted for age and %DL CO (OR: 0.228, 95% CI: 0.088-0.591, p = 0.002; bootstrap p = 0.005) or %FVC (OR: 0.213, 95% CI: 0.091-0.496, p = 0.001; bootstrap p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed F-F PhA had the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC: 0.802), outperforming %DL CO (AUC: 0.729) and ESM_CSA (AUC: 0.701). Combining age, %DL CO , and F-F PhA achieved the highest performance (AUC: 0.833). Conclusions F-F PhA serves as a robust, independent indicator for predicting reduced exercise capacity in ILD, outperforming conventional muscle mass. As a non-invasive tool, F-F PhA complements established functional tests in screening for early physical decline.

title: NU-1025 Modulates Immunogenic Cell Death in Bladder Cancer: A Multi-omics Insight.
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has shown limited efficacy in bladder cancer, underscoring the need for therapeutic strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) can stimulate adaptive immunity and remodel the tumor microenvironment, yet its comprehensive landscape and druggable potential in bladder cancer remain unexplored. Here, we performed integrative bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO bladder cancer cohorts to characterize ICD-associated subtypes, construct a prognostic risk model, and analyze immune infiltration. Connectivity Map (CMap) database and the XSum algorithm were employed for computational drug screening. Molecular docking was used to predict interactions between candidate compounds and immune checkpoint proteins. In silico ADMET and toxicology profiles were evaluated. The clinical relevance was assessed through independent CT urography imaging and PD-L1 immunohistochemistry data. Two ICD molecular subtypes were identified with distinct prognostic and microenvironment features. An eight-gene ICD risk model was established and validated, effectively stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups with differential survival, immune cell infiltration, and tumor mutational burden. Through computational screening, NU-1025 was nominated as a top candidate capable of reversing the high-risk gene expression pattern. In silico profiling indicated favorable drug-like properties and low toxicity risk. Clinical data analysis revealed that high-grade bladder tumors frequently exhibit low PD-L1 expression, aligning with the predicted need for ICD-inducing agents. Overall, this research decodes the ICD landscape in bladder cancer and, via a computational drug repurposing pipeline, nominates NU-1025 as a novel candidate with predicted ICD-inducing and/or immune checkpoint modulatory activity.

title: Association of Spinal Epidural Lipomatosis With Systemic Lipid Metabolism in Patients With Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
abstract: Background context Spinal epidural lipomatosis (SEL) is often regarded as a local consequence of obesity, yet its relationship with systemic lipid metabolism and symptom severity in lumbar spinal stenosis remains unclear. Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) is central to atherogenic lipid transport and ectopic fat deposition. Examining the association between systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities, including elevated ApoB levels, and epidural fat accumulation may provide insights into the metabolic pathogenesis and clinical relevance of SEL. Purpose To determine whether SEL is associated with systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities and greater preoperative symptom burden in patients undergoing surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). Study design Retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study. Patient sample A consecutive series of 1,145 patients who underwent posterior decompression for symptomatic LSS between December 2023 and December 2025. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 patients without SEL. Outcome measures Serum lipid and other biochemical markers, epidural fat/spinal canal (EF/SpC) index on lumbar magnetic resonance imaging, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and visual analog scale (VAS) scores for leg and back pain. Methods SEL was diagnosed and graded on preoperative lumbar MRI according to the Borré classification, using the epidural fat/spinal canal index. Propensity score matching was performed for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking history, drinking history, hypertension, and diabetes. Biochemical variables and preoperative clinical scores were compared between matched SEL and non-SEL patients. Conditional logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with SEL. BMI-adjusted partial Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between the EF/SpC index and biochemical markers. Regression-based trend analyses were conducted to assess changes in lipid-related markers across increasing SEL severity grades. Results Among 1,145 patients with LSS, 105 (9.2%) met the diagnostic criteria for SEL. After matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 non-SEL controls. The SEL group had higher apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels than controls, as well as higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. ApoB remained independently associated with SEL in conditional logistic regression (odds ratio per 0.1 g/L, 1.141; 95% confidence interval, 1.019-1.277; P=0.022). Within the SEL group, the EF/SpC index correlated positively with triglycerides (ρ=0.43, q<0.001) and ApoB (ρ=0.40, q=0.002), while atherogenic lipid markers increased progressively with SEL severity. Patients with SEL also showed higher Oswestry Disability Index and leg-pain visual analog scale scores, whereas back-pain scores were similar between groups. Conclusion In patients undergoing surgery for LSS, SEL was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile after matching for BMI and other major baseline characteristics, as well as greater preoperative disability and leg pain. The association of ApoB with SEL, together with the graded relationships of ApoB and triglycerides with epidural fat burden, suggests that SEL may reflect systemic lipid metabolic dysfunction rather than local epidural fat deposition alone.

Patients with SEL also showed higher Oswestry Disability Index and leg-pain visual analog scale scores, whereas back-pain scores were similar between groups.

Conclusion

In patients undergoing surgery for LSS, SEL was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile after matching for BMI and other major baseline characteristics, as well as greater preoperative disability and leg pain. The association of ApoB with SEL, together with the graded relationships of ApoB and triglycerides with epidural fat burden, suggests that SEL may reflect systemic lipid metabolic dysfunction rather than local epidural fat deposition alone.

title: Optical Fiber Needle Probes for In Situ-Distributed Biosensing Based on Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry.
abstract: In situ detection is crucial for diagnosing lesions during surgery, endoscopy, or biopsy but has always been a challenge in medical diagnostics. Optical fiber biosensing needle probes, with their small size, can be nearly noninvasively guided to the lesion site for in situ detection. However, existing optical fiber biosensing probes are single-point sensors, unable to precisely locate lesions. We propose an optical fiber needle probe for in situ distributed sensing of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) biomarker GPC3 in soft matter based on optical frequency domain reflectometry (OFDR). The needle type probe is fabricated by integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-assisted anti-GPC3 antibody-functionalized micro/nano fiber into a metal needle with a lateral opening near the distal tip. Through differential-phase demodulation, calibration experiments with varying GPC3 concentrations reveal that the needle probe exhibits an 8 mm sensing length with a sensitivity of 0.0031 rad/(ng/mL). More importantly, the proposed needle probe achieves the precise spatial localization of both independent and simultaneous multiple 250-μm mimic lesions loaded by GPC3 in an agarose-glycerol hydrogel soft matter phantom with a spatial resolution of 25 μm and a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.23 ng/mL, which offers unparalleled advantages compared with existing biosensors. The proposed method provides a potential for in situ detection and localization of HCC or other lesions.

title: Temporal Bone Osteosarcoma in Pregnancy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Introduction Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor; however, involvement of the temporal bone is exceptionally rare, particularly during pregnancy. The coexistence of malignancy and pregnancy presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges requiring multidisciplinary management. Case Presentation A 23-year-old woman presented with persistent right otalgia and an external auditory canal lesion initially diagnosed as cholesteatoma. Following surgical resection, final histopathology revealed temporal bone osteosarcoma with early locoregional recurrence and intracranial extension. Pregnancy was incidentally diagnosed during oncologic evaluation at 24 weeks of gestation. Given the aggressive nature of the tumor, pregnancy termination followed by palliative chemotherapy was initially recommended; however, the patient elected to continue the pregnancy after multidisciplinary counseling. She received chemoradiotherapy with ifosfamide/mesna and 40 Gy radiotherapy. Subsequently, severe anhydramnios and early fetal growth restriction developed, likely secondary to fetal nephrotoxicity associated with ifosfamide exposure. A cesarean section was performed after antenatal corticosteroid administration, resulting in the delivery of a live preterm neonate admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, and discharged after 58 days of hospitalization. Conclusion Temporal bone osteosarcoma during pregnancy is exceedingly rare and requires complex multidisciplinary management balancing maternal oncologic treatment and fetal risks.

title: Variability and bias in the calculation of iodine uptake with an adaptive background subtraction method in contrast-enhanced mammography.
abstract: Objective. This work evaluates variability and bias in the calculation of iodine uptake from contrast-enhanced dual-energy mammography (CEM) images using an adaptive background subtraction method. Approach. The iodine uptake images were custom-generated using weighted subtraction, followed by subtraction of a smooth background estimated by interpolation from neighboring regions outside the lesion (adaptive background subtraction). Three main sources of variability and bias were assessed: differences in breast tissue linear attenuation coefficients, stability of the mammography system, and intra- and inter-observer variability in lesion segmentation. Tissue-related effects were evaluated theoretically. System stability was assessed using weekly phantom measurements acquired over a 4-year period. For observer variability, four radiologists performed two segmentation rounds of iodine-enhancing regions in 40 CEM studies. Typical uptake values were below 5 mg cm -2 . Whenever possible, variability was expressed as the 95% coverage interval (2σ), where σ represents the standard deviation . Main results. Theoretical evaluation showed that tissue composition differences may introduce biases in iodine uptake exceeding 0.5 mg cm -2 , although typical lesion compositions produce biases below the visual detection threshold. Long-term phantom measurements demonstrated excellent system stability over four years (2σ ≈0.2 mg cm -2 , and limit of detection = 0.24 mg cm -2 ), with a 7% change in calibration following a workstation upgrade. In the clinical dataset, the four radiologists achieved high detection agreement when segmenting the primary lesions and greater variability for secondary lesions; the inter-observer variability in mean uptake was approximately 2σ ≈0.6 mg cm -2 . Significance. These findings indicate that iodine uptake quantification in CEM using an adaptive background subtraction method is technically robust, which is a key element for exploring its potential usefulness as an imaging biomarker.

title: Generative modeling of complex-valued brain MRI data.
abstract: Objective. Standard magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction pipelines discard phase information captured during acquisition, despite its sensitivity to tissue properties that are not represented by magnitude alone. The aim of this study is to develop a generative framework that jointly models magnitude and phase information in complex-valued brain MRI data and enables the conditional generation of MRI samples representing normal and abnormal brain tissue. Approach. The proposed generative framework combines a conditional variational autoencoder, which compresses complex-valued MRI scans into latent representations while preserving phase coherence, with a flow-matching-based generative model. Synthetic sample quality is assessed using a real-versus-synthetic classifier, image-space coverage tests, and downstream classifiers trained on synthetic data for abnormal tissue detection. Main results. The autoencoder preserves phase coherence above 0.997. Real-vs-synthetic classifiers yielded low AUROCs between 0.53 and 0.64 for generated phase images supporting realistic phase modeling. Magnitude was moderately distinguishable, with AUROCs between 0.53 and 0.82, suggesting appreciable overlap between real and synthetic sample distributions while also indicating a distribution shift for several sequences. Image-space coverage was broad. On the held-out test split, no consistent directional difference from the matched real-to-real references was detected in any evaluated setting, while the training split showed slight to moderate undercoverage depending on acquisition sequence and tissue condition. In downstream normal-versus-abnormal classification, classifiers trained entirely on synthetic data achieve an AUROC of 0.880, surpassing the real-data baseline of 0.842 on the fastMRI dataset. This advantage persists on an independent external test set with biopsy-confirmed labels. Significance. The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of jointly modeling magnitude and phase information for normal and abnormal complex-valued brain MRI data. Beyond synthetic data generation, the framework enables future investigation of how magnitude and phase jointly encode pathology-specific features once sufficiently large raw MRI datasets with fine-grained, pathology-confirmed labels become available.

title: Nonlinear stability phenotypes and collapse dynamics of multi-organ radiomics in total-body PET imaging: toward digital twin-oriented robustness assessment.
abstract: Objective Radiomics analysis in PET offers a high-dimensional representation of tissue characteristics, yet its reliability is limited by sensitivity to acquisition perturbations, particularly dose reduction. This study aims to introduce a nonlinear stability phenotyping framework to characterize dose-response behavior of multi-organ radiomics and evaluate their potential relevance for future digital twin-oriented applications. Approach: A multi-center dataset of 550 total-body PET scans was analyzed. Dose reduction was simulated using list-mode subsampling (dose reduction factor - DRF = 2-100). A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted per organ. Stability was quantified using Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) and summarized as stability fractions. Nonlinear models were fitted to organ- and feature-level trajectories. Stability phenotypes and critical thresholds were derived, along with organ-level instability metrics. Main results: Radiomics stability exhibited strongly nonlinear, organ-dependent behavior. Feature-level analysis identified frequent sigmoid-associated collapse patterns with high descriptive model fits (R²>0.90). The liver showed the highest instability burden (30.8% unstable features), followed by esophagus and kidneys (18-20%). Texture features were the primary source of instability, whereas shape features remained robust. Organ-level trajectories demonstrated heterogeneous responses, with some organs maintaining high stability (0.80-0.95) across DRFs, while others showed sharp declines (down to 0.64). Linear (stable) behavior dominated at the organ level, though masking underlying nonlinear feature dynamics. Significance: Radiomics stability in total-body PET follows nonlinear, phenotype-driven dynamics with identifiable tipping points and organ-specific sensitivity. The proposed framework provides a behavior-based approach for evaluating radiomics robustness and supports the selection of reliable features and organs for robust quantitative imaging and may inform future digital twin-oriented applications.

title: Silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates for ultrasound-activated immunomodulatory therapy of MRSA pneumonia.
abstract: The clinical management of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) pneumonia is hindered by biofilm infections and cytokine storms. A key challenge is the lack of real-time monitoring tools for the inflammatory microenvironment during treatment. In this study, we developed a theranostic platform (CS@EAgNP) using TPP-modified chitosan to load silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates (AgNP) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). This system combines ultrasound (US) imaging with US-activated therapy. The CS@EAgNP nano-aggregates can act as an excellent US contrast enhancer. In vivo US imaging indicated that AgNP generated significantly enhanced echo signals at the infection site, providing real-time and high-contrast visualization of the inflammatory foci that was unattainable with normal lung tissue. Moreover, these nano-aggregates release NO, silver and EGCG under US. The NO and silver penetrate biofilms to kill MRSA, while EGCG scavenges reactive oxygen species and modulates inflammation. This reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and TNF- α , mitigating the cytokine storm. In vivo results further confirm that this image-guided strategy achieves significant bacterial clearance and promotes lung tissue regeneration without detectable toxicity to major organs. This integrated approach bridges diagnosis and treatment, offering a promising solution for managing MRSA pneumonia.

title: Geo-economic variations in structure and organization of intensive care units: the ISOREA survey.
abstract: Purpose Little is known on critical care services globally. This study aimed to describe ICU resources and organization across countries and assess variability by income group, between countries, and within countries. Methods Participating centers provided structured data on hospital and ICU characteristics via electronic case report form (January 2018 to July 2020). Questionnaire included 237 items covering general characteristics (2 topics) and ICU resources and organization (18 topics). We computed standardized functional domain scores (ISOREA score), classified ICUs using Marshall criteria, and readiness for essential emergency and critical care using a modified Schell score. Results A total of 1,426 ICUs from five continents were recruited, and 1,225 were analyzed, from high-income countries (HICs, 58%), upper-middle-income (20%), and low/lower-middle-income countries (LLMICs, 22%). Most ICUs were in referral centers (90%) and large urban areas (80%). Most variables (93%) were significantly associated with income group, Most variables (93%) were significantly associated with income group, with 88% showing higher levels in HICs and lower levels in LLMICs. Six domains showed major disparities: extracorporeal support, respiratory support, emergency access to interventional radiology and surgery, neurology and trauma care, patient file and general monitoring, and cardiovascular and hemodynamic monitoring. According to the Marshall classification, 79% of ICUs in HICs were classified as level III, whereas 55% of ICUs in LLMICs were classified as level I. Domains with higher ISOREA scores varied primarily between countries, whereas lower-performing domains exhibited greater variability across ICUs within the same country. Adjustment for income group reduced, but did not eliminate, country-level clustering. Conclusion Substantial disparities exist in ICU resources and organization across income groups, countries, and ICUs. ICU capacities appeared multidimensional, extending beyond resource limitations.

title: Serial Mass Tuberculosis Screening Among the Elderly in Eastern China from 2021-2023.
abstract: Rationale The impact of repeated community-wide tuberculosis screening is uncertain because evidence from large-scale, multi-round screening campaigns is limited. Objectives We evaluated whether annual, community-based, chest-radiography screening was associated with reduced tuberculosis prevalence and detection of asymptomatic disease across multiple screening rounds. Methods We conducted three annual chest X-ray screening rounds (2021-2023) among adults aged ≥60 years in Lanxi City, Zhejiang Province. All participants underwent chest radiography at community health centers, with referral for diagnostic evaluation and bacteriological testing. We estimated detection yields per 100,000 screened persons, assessed trends, and used direct standardization and repeated-participation analyses. Measurements and main results Across all rounds, 214,948 screening encounters were completed. From Round 1 to Round 3, screening-detected prevalence declined for overall tuberculosis (233.1 [95% CI, 194.2-279.7] to 146.3 [95% CI, 123.1-173.9] per 100,000 screened persons) and bacteriologically-confirmed tuberculosis (162.1 [95% CI, 130.3-201.7] to 108.6 [95% CI, 88.8-132.7] per 100,000 screened persons). From Round 1 to Round 3, asymptomatic tuberculosis decreased as both a proportion of cases (47.8% to 26.6%) and prevalence among screened participants (111.5 to 38.9 per 100,000). Compared with Round 1, tuberculosis prevalence was lower in Round 2 (-28.1% change; 95% CI, -44.0 to - 7.5) and Round 3 (-37.2% change; 95% CI, -51.2 to - 19.2). The Round 2-to-Round 3 difference was smaller and included the null (-12.8% change; 95% CI, -31.7 to 11.4). Standardization and repeated-participation analyses yielded broadly similar patterns. Conclusions Serial community-level screening was associated with declining tuberculosis prevalence, including asymptomatic disease, with the largest reduction occurring between the first and second screening rounds.

title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
abstract: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

title: The eye in systemic vasculitis.
abstract: Purpose of review This review summarizes the spectrum of ocular manifestations in systemic vasculitis, emphasizing recent advances in clinical recognition, multimodal imaging, biomarkers, and targeted treatment. Recent findings Ocular involvement may precede systemic manifestations and affect the anterior segment, retina, choroid, optic nerve, or orbit. In giant cell arteritis, vascular ultrasound is a preferred first-line imaging modality, while orbital and retinal imaging may provide complementary information on ischemic injury and treatment response. Ultra-widefield fluorescein angiography improves the detection of peripheral retinal nonperfusion in Takayasu arteritis. In antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, particularly granulomatosis with polyangiitis, ocular or orbital inflammation may be the initial or isolated manifestation, and rituximab-based therapy has been associated with favorable outcomes in orbital inflammatory disease. In Behçet uveitis, ocular-specific diagnostic criteria, imaging biomarkers, and treat-to-target biologic strategies are emerging. However, many of these approaches require validation in larger prospective studies. Summary Prompt recognition and multidisciplinary management are essential to prevent irreversible visual loss. New imaging methods and targeted therapies have broadened diagnostic and therapeutic options. Despite these advances, standardized ocular outcome measures and validation of emerging imaging and molecular biomarkers remain important priorities.

title: Is the use of Porous Threaded Titanium Implants Associated with Lower Rates of Implant Migration in Elderly Pelvic Ring Injuries?
abstract: Objectives To determine if porous threaded titanium implant (PTTI) screws placed in the posterior pelvic ring as iliosacral (IS) or transiliac-transsacral (transsacral) were associated with implant positional changes, alterations in postoperative weightbearing restrictions, or the necessity of revision surgery in operatively managed geriatric pelvic ring injuries, compared to standard stainless steel screws. Methods Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Academic Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria Patients with operatively managed pelvic ring injuries (AO/OTA61) from January 2017 to June 2025, aged ≥65 years with a minimum of 6-months of radiographic and clinical follow-up were included.Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary study outcome was the incidence of postoperative pelvic ring implant positional changes, ≥2mm from immediate postoperative radiographs compared among patients treated with PTTI versus standard stainless steel screws for IS and transsacral fixation. Secondary outcomes included subsequent revision surgery or alterations in postoperative weightbearing restrictions related to implant positional changes. A multivariable logistic regression was used to determine associations of demographic, injury, and treatment variables with implant positional changes, the necessity for revision surgery, or negative changes in postoperative weightbearing restrictions. Results 271 patients were included; 215 (79.3%) were managed with standard screws, while PTTIs were used in 56 (20.7%). The standard screw cohort had a median follow-up of 8.9 months (interquartile range 6.2-11.3 months), while the PTTI cohort had a median follow-up of 9.1 months (interquartile range 6.3-10.9 months). Compared with the standard screw cohort, the PTTI cohort had a higher proportion of female sex (57.2% versus 73.2%, respectively; p=0.029) and a higher average age (74.0 years versus 78.6 years, respectively; p<0.001).Radiographic migration ≥2mm for posterior implants was observed in 18.1% of patients in the standard implant cohort versus 0.0% in the PTTI cohort (p<0.001). Implant migration >1cm was observed in 3.7% of patients in the standard implant cohort versus 0.0% in the PTTI group (p=0.231). The implant positional changes resulted in negative weightbearing restriction changes in 9 of 215 (4.2%) patients in the standard implant cohort compared with 0 of 56 in the PTTI cohort (p=0.120). Of the patients with standard implants, 9 (4.2%) underwent revision for posterior implant loosening, compared with 0 (0.0%) in the PTTI cohort.On multivariate analysis, posterior implant positional changes were associated with a protective effect from PTTI and anterior ring fixation (OR 0.1, 95% CI 0.0-0.7, p=0.023 and OR 0.2, 95% CI 0.1-0.4, p<0.001, respectively). The necessity for revision surgery or negative change in postoperative weightbearing restrictions was not significantly associated with PTTI use (OR 0.3, 95% CI 0.1-1.3, p=0.106). Conclusions In geriatric pelvic ring injuries, PTTIs had no migration after placement and were associated with a lower incidence of any implant positional change and posterior implant positional changes. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III.

title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

title: A Head-to-Head Comparison of Detection Rate and Tumor Uptake of FAPI, PSMA, and FDG PET/CT in Newly Diagnosed High-risk Prostate Cancer.
abstract: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-FDG PET/CT. This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68Ga-PSMA-11, and 18F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity. A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18F-FDG. Combined 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden. 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: A Favorable Partial Response in Patients With Glioblastoma Multiforme Following Combined [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 and Chemotherapy.
abstract: This report highlights the potential role of [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET/CT in the early detection of active tumor recurrence in a 64-year-old woman with glioblastoma multiforme (IDH-wild type, WHO grade IV), preceding definitive radiologic evidence of disease progression. Following confirmation of recurrence, the patient underwent combined chemotherapy and [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 radioligand therapy, resulting in a favorable partial molecular and anatomic response as demonstrated by serial PET/CT and MRI examinations. This case illustrates the potential theranostic value of FAP-targeted imaging and radionuclide therapy in the management of recurrent glioblastoma.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: FDG PET/CT Unmasking Acute Rheumatic Fever Presenting as Polyenthesitis.
abstract: A 13-year-old boy underwent FDG PET/CT to evaluate fever of unknown origin, which demonstrated extensive abnormal activity around joints of all 4 extremities and probable myopericarditis. Subsequent rheumatologic evaluation, including cardiac auscultation and echocardiography, identification of subcutaneous nodules, and elevated antistreptolysin O titers, established the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever (ARF). Symmetrical polyarthritis with enthesitis-myotendinitis is an uncommon manifestation of ARF.

title: FAPI PET/CT Outperforms MRI and FDG PET/CT in Tumor Delineation for Low-grade Nasopharyngeal Papillary Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Low-grade nasopharyngeal papillary adenocarcinoma (LGNPPA) is a rare entity. We report a 27-year-old man with a 1-year history of bloody postnasal drip. MRI revealed a protuberance on the roof and posterior wall of the nasopharynx with contrast enhancement. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed mild uptake with poorly defined lesion extent, whereas 18F-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated intense uptake confined to the tumor with clear boundaries. No metastases were detected. Postoperative pathology confirmed LGNPPA, and the tumor boundary delineated on FAPI PET/CT precisely matched the pathologic extent. This case suggests that FAPI PET/CT may be superior to FDG PET/CT and MRI for tumor delineation in LGNPPA.

title: Sarcoid-like Reaction With Pleural Involvement After Neoadjuvant Chemo-immunotherapy For Lung Cancer: A Rare Mimic of Disease Progression.
abstract: We report a patient with stage IIA (cT2bN0M0) lung adenocarcinoma who developed new diffuse pleural, pulmonary, and nodal FDG uptake on 18FDG-PET/CT after three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus cisplatin-pemetrexed, with slight regression of the primary tumour. These findings raised the diagnostic dilemma between disease progression and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-related sarcoid-like reaction (SLR). Rapid clinical and metabolic improvement after corticosteroid therapy supported SLR, which was subsequently confirmed histologically by noncaseating granulomas without viable tumour at surgery. This case highlights pleural involvement in SLR as a rare and diagnostically challenging immune-related adverse event.

title: FDG PET/CT in IgG4-related Disease Involving the Urethra.
abstract: Urethral involvement in IgG4-related disease is rare. We describe FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI findings in a woman with IgG4-related disease presenting as urethral wall thickening with obstructive urinary symptoms. FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI showed significant circumferential thickening of the urethral wall with intense diffuse activity (SUVmax, 13) and multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes in pelvic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, pulmonary hilar, and axillary regions. This case indicates that IgG4-related urethral disease should be included in the differential diagnosis of FDG-avid urethral or periurethral lesions.

title: Exceptional Thyroid Recurrence of Solitary Bone Plasmacytoma Detected by 18F-FDG PET/CT.
abstract: A 70-year-old man with prior occupational radiation exposure and a history of solitary bone plasmacytoma of the left hemipelvis treated with radiotherapy underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT for follow-up. Imaging revealed focal hypermetabolism in the right thyroid lobe, with no additional abnormalities detected. Ultrasound revealed an EU-TIRADS 5 nodule, and the cytologic analysis was indeterminate (Bethesda III). Core biopsy confirmed thyroid plasmacytoma. Although solitary bone plasmacytoma usually progresses to multiple myeloma, distant extramedullary relapse is uncommon. Thyroid involvement is exceedingly rare. This case highlights the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT and the need for histologic confirmation of suspicious thyroid lesions.

title: Not Every PSMA-Expressing Bone Lesion Is Prostate Cancer: Incidental Detection of Metastatic Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma on Staging 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT.
abstract: 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT is widely used for staging prostate cancer but may also detect nonprostatic malignancies owing to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression in tumor neovasculature. Here, we report a case of a newly diagnosed high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma that underwent staging 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT. In addition to the primary prostatic lesion, PSMA-expressing lesions were identified in the sternum and right thyroid lobe. While skeletal involvement was initially presumed metastatic prostate cancer, further evaluation revealed follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma. This case highlights an important diagnostic pitfall and demonstrates the value of PSMA-PET/CT in uncovering clinically occult synchronous malignancies.

title: A Tale of 3 Tracers: Contrasting Uptake Patterns of 18F-FDG, 68Ga-DOTATATE, and 18F-MFBG in a Pediatric Neuroblastoma Patient.
abstract: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.

title: [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Incidental Detection of a Benign Phyllodes Tumor in a Patient With Prior Colon Cancer.
abstract: We present [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

title: FDG PET/CT Combined With 3D CT Reconstruction in Diagnosing Inflammatory Granuloma Secondary to Fish Bone Perforation of the Ascending Colon.
abstract: A 71-year-old woman with a 5-week history of right-sided abdominal pain was initially suspected of hepatobiliary disorders. Upper abdominal ultrasound and MRI revealed unremarkable hepatobiliary findings. Although no hepatobiliary lesions were identified, MRI incidentally detected an ascending colon mass highly suspicious for malignancy. The patient underwent FDG PET/CT for differential diagnosis and preoperative staging. PET/CT with 3D CT reconstruction demonstrated a linear hyperdense foreign body within the ascending colon wall, causing focal bowel wall thickening with intense FDG avidity. These imaging findings were consistent with a foreign body-induced inflammatory granuloma, a diagnosis ultimately confirmed by colonoscopy and biopsy.

title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Reshapes Diagnostic Classification in a Real-World Memory Clinic Cohort.
abstract: Background Plasma phosphorylated tau-217 (ptau217) accurately identifies Alzheimer disease (AD), but its impact on real-world clinical diagnosis remains unclear. We evaluated the effect of plasma ptau217 on diagnostic reclassification in a memory disorders clinic. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 100 patients evaluated for memory impairment. Initial clinical diagnoses were established based on clinical evaluation, neuropsychological testing, and brain MRI without plasma biomarker results. Follow-up diagnoses were assigned after the availability of plasma ptau217 results. Diagnostic reclassification was assessed using binary (ptau217 > 0.18) and higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325) classification schemes. McNemar tests evaluated reclassification patterns, with subgroup analyses by apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 carrier status. Results Diagnosis reclassification occurred in 37.8% and 46.9% of patients using the lower and higher threshold, respectively (both P<0.001). With the higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325), reclassification among APOE ε4 carriers was balanced (42% from AD to non-AD vs. 43% from non-AD to AD, P=0.096). In contrast, APOE ε4 noncarriers showed significantly greater reclassification from AD to non-AD than from non-AD to AD (66% vs.14%, P<0.001). Conclusions Plasma ptau217 meaningfully influences diagnostic decisions in memory clinic practice and may be particularly valuable for refining diagnoses among APOE ε4 noncarriers.

title: Novel therapies for glioblastoma.
abstract: Purpose of review Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and treatment-resistant primary brain tumor in adults. Given its clinical severity and biological complexity, research efforts are focused on understanding and targeting intratumoral heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, drug delivery barriers, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This review highlights emerging therapeutic approaches for the treatment of glioblastoma including advances in radiation planning, molecularly targeted therapy, immunotherapy, blood-brain barrier modulation, and neuronal signaling. Recent findings Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of glioblastoma treatment, and advances in image-guided planning are being developed to refine treatment margins and improve tolerability without compromising efficacy. Blood-brain barrier permeability is being improved through device-assisted approaches, including focused ultrasound in combination with systemic therapies. Molecularly targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches continue to be evaluated, increasingly with biomarker-informed strategies to optimize patient selection. In parallel, drug repurposing, neuronal modulation, and metabolic interventions have shown promising preclinical and retrospective signals and are moving towards prospective studies. Interventions to improve quality of life are also underway with early palliative care showing significant impact for patients with glioblastoma. Summary As the field moves towards tailored and precision-guided approaches, combination strategies remain central to addressing the multiple mechanisms by which glioblastoma evades treatment.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
abstract: This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine studies were included. Computer vision studies (n = 32) most often used panoramic radiographs (n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and segmentation (n = 10) and caries detection (n = 9). Non-imaging ML studies (n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data (n = 8) or salivary/biological samples (n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker-based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely (33%-96%). Computer vision and non-imaging ML show promise for paediatric dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for standardized evaluation before clinical integration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AI-based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk stratification. Computer vision and non-imaging machine learning approaches appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.
